The Fly Diary

Every main experiment, in order, as it happened: one human and one AI learning to do science together.

Research notebook, not peer review. One simulated animal; every number traces to the committed ledger. The early entries are deliberately rough. The methods improve on the day a failure teaches a new rule (★). Entries from Aug 17 onward carry the full standard: pre-registered predictions where applicable, declared run scope, run metadata, reproduce commands, and attribution.

2026-09-15 The body's derivative survives a tick and not a footfall The lab started fitting the network by gradient descent, which needs a derivative through the physical fly, and lane A spent the afternoon finding out there is not one. The champion's feet make and break contact 5,362 times a second, the linearised body agrees with it to about four parts in ten thousand across one 2.5 ms tick and is wrong by a median factor of 25 over 250 of them, and only 45 of 2,400 ticks hold their contact set at all. A cheap gate picks the ticks where the linearisation is sound, 163 of 240 on the champion's own recorded drive, and the body term was licensed on that number as a search direction only, never as a measurement. Six of the runs on the way measured a body the champion does not run, which lane A caught itself and the judge recorded as its own miss. The champion is unchanged. Robin stopped every seat at 20:05.

20:1x EEST. The programme. At 14:32 lane A's goal was rewritten from the haltere work to something the lab has not tried before: fit the network's free numbers by gradient descent. Not a sweep over a handful of shared scalars, which is every search this project has run, but a twin of the walking network that carries a derivative, a loss built from the card rows, and a ladder of parameter sharing from super_class down through hemilineage, cell type, motor neuron and the special cells, with ten neuron-model numbers per unit and the measured ones held fixed. Every minimum it finds is a nominee, graded by the bar like any other body. The free count of record at the end of the day is 49,435, on a ladder of 147, 738, 43,860, 4,690 at the four levels.

That design has a hole in the middle of it. The loss is read off the fly's behaviour, and the fly's behaviour comes out of a physics simulator. To push a gradient from a card row back to a synaptic parameter, something has to carry it through the body.

First the seal, because it was drawn before any of this. At 14:55, before lane A's loss proposal existed, the judge fixed how rows would be withheld from the fit: the complement of whatever the lane proposed, plus one withdrawn row per registry group holding three or more, chosen by the smallest sha256 of the row ids against the noon map's hash, never by a hand. At 15:19 the draw ran and was committed, seal sha256 646d5edc1d662b5a. Held out: flyscore.lr_asymmetry, gait.cadence, gait.swing_ms, posture.body_height, rom.front_ctr_deg, rom.front_fti_deg. The loss keeps 20 rows carrying 17 distinct facts about the animal, drawn from a readable universe of 26 rows and 23 facts; the other 31 walking-side rows are readable by no instrument today and are neither fitted nor sealed.

One ruling inside the seal matters more than the draw. Lane A's loss divided each row's hinge distance by its band width, and on the champion's card that puts 81 per cent of the loss on one fact, left-right leg phase, whose bands are 1.6 to 2.2 degrees wide. A descent under that loss is a phase optimiser wearing a card. The normaliser is now the row's own measured between-block median spread, the resolution of the instrument that reads it, and every receipt prints each term's share so a lopsided loss is visible rather than suspected.

Then the body, and the first answer was no. MJX is MuJoCo's differentiable path, and at 17:52 lane A probed whether it would take the title body at all. It refuses it, on contact sensor semantics, on plane-mesh margin and gap, and on body-transmission actuators. It accepts only a body stripped of its adhesion actuators, which is a different fly: it drifts 2.514 length units from the title body in 250 ms and settles on five of seven contacts. On that reduced body reverse-mode differentiation raises inside the solver's loop, and the one setting that admits it, a single solver iteration, throws the fly off the ground entirely (zero contacts, NaN). Forward mode does return a finite gradient, 42 of 42 inputs within 0.9 to 2.6 per cent of central differences, at 1.00 s per window against 0.046 s for the plain rollout, one pass per input.

The judge closed MJX as the twin's body on this version and resolved the design's body branch to the black box: the gradient reaches the motor pools and stops there, the loss stays the selection criterion rather than the fitted quantity, and no FITTED value may come from a motor-pool-only target. One route stayed open, lane A's own: linearise the body locally, step by step, and chain the small matrices.

The linearised body is exact, right up until a foot moves. At 19:05 lane A measured it against central differences of the whole window. Between contact changes the chain reproduces the body's own derivative to a median relative difference of 7.19e-6 on one tick and 7.16e-6 over 250 of them with the contact set held, and the adjoint reproduces the chain's row to 7.4e-14, which is arithmetic noise. Across a contact change it carries nothing: 5.5e-3 on one tick, 38.2 over 25 ms with five to seven changes inside it. No differencing width from 1e-6 to 1e-2 brings the moving window under 1.00; the best is exactly 1.00 at 1e-5, where the held window reads 2.05e-7.

So everything turns on how often the feet hold still. Lane A counted, on flygym's own CPG walker: 39,110 changes of the active contact set in 6 s, 6,518 a second, median constant stretch 0.1 ms, which is one engine step, p90 0.3 ms, longest 22.4 ms. Ten of 2,400 body ticks hold their contacts and none of the 48 loss windows do. The judge had written the decision rule before the number arrived, at 19:14: a median constant run of at least 25 ms builds a contact-keyed piecewise scheme, under 10 ms closes it. At 0.1 ms it closed.

What replaced it is a gate, and gates are cheap. Rather than ask where the contacts are constant, ask directly whether the linearisation agrees with the body at this tick: one extra central difference along three random directions, 0.0088 s per tick, 2.9 per cent of the cost of the chain itself. On 120 ticks of the CPG walk it rank-correlates 0.943 with the full reference and at threshold keeps 57 usable ticks and zero broken ones, dropping 63 broken and no usable. No threshold pair tried keeps a broken tick. The directions have to avoid the six adhesion commands, which sit pinned at their upper bound where the derivative exists on one side only: a centred difference there returns exactly half, ratio 2.0 on all 32 affected entries.

Then lane A found it had been measuring the wrong fly. The champion's theta carries abd_gain 0.2, and the runner selects abdomen.make_fly on that key: 83 positions, 82 velocities, 58 actuators, adhesion gain 15.0407, four contacts at the warmed state. Every run from GP2i to GP2n had built make_locomotion_fly at gain 40.0, which is 73, 72, 48 and seven contacts. Six runs measured a body the champion does not run. Lane A caught it itself, by reading abd_gain against the branch that consumes it, and the judge recorded its own miss beside it: it had accepted the body's identity as stated in three packets without once asking which builder the champion's theta selects.

Re-read on the right body, the qualitative findings survive and the numbers move. The chain is exact where contact holds, 4.36e-4 over a tick window in which the contact set moved twice, the adjoint reproduces it to 5.29e-15 over 58 entries, and nothing survives 250 steps (median 25.11, worst 13,283). The costs roughly double: 0.338 s a tick for the chain, 0.330 s for the adjoint, 16.9 s per 50-tick loss window against 0.054 s for a plain rollout.

The decision number, on the champion's own walk. Getting it looked like it needed an engine slot, which the fleet did not have. It did not: lane A replaced cns.CNS.run with a reader of the cord spike tape already on disk from seed 203892 and ran the body verbatim inside the drive callback. All nine fields of the resulting row equal the row the engine itself produced for that seed (speed 1.858867313611122 to sixteen digits; lifts per foot 21, 9, 37, 45, 39, 25; final tilt 14.56 degrees), from 2,400 callbacks and 24,884 spikes, in 18.5 s of CPU. The lane withdrew its own claim that a slot was needed.

On that trajectory, every tenth tick: 163 of 240 ticks kept and usable, 0.679, and 0.682 once the first 500 ms of transient is dropped. Zero kept-and-broken at every threshold pair read, seven usable ticks dropped, rank correlation 0.901 with the full 58-column reference. The champion's own drive is markedly easier on the linearisation than the CPG walker's, 70.8 per cent of ticks inside tolerance against 47.5. Its contact census is the same picture as the walker's: 32,171 changes in 6 s, 5,362 a second, median stretch 0.1 ms, longest 37.7 ms, 45 of 2,400 ticks holding their set, so the piecewise route is closed on the champion's walk as well as on the walker's.

The rule written before the read asked for one third of ticks to build the gated term and would have closed it under one fifth. It came in at twice the bar, and the gated tick body is built.

What it is allowed to do, which is less than it sounds. The per-tick Jacobian is the object and the body term is truncated at tick boundaries, so no gradient crosses a tick edge. The dropped ticks are the contact events that gait is made of, which means the instrument is systematically blind to exactly the moments that produce stepping. Therefore nothing read through the gated body enters as a match, as a band reading, or as a FITTED value: the loss is read on the real engine, and every minimum the descent finds is a nominee that has to win a title match against the folded control like any other body. It is a direction to walk in, not a number to believe.

Problems, in the order they bit. The judge's own seat went 46 minutes without a wake between 18:13 and 19:01 and five packets sat unread; the five-minute watcher is now a standing measure rather than a habit. The free-parameter count published at 19:14 was 49,433 and is 49,435: a level's unit counts a parameter free when any of its rows runs it free, and the slow motor neuron is the only row of its type, so its two entries add at two levels rather than one. The same cell is the remaining honest gap in the pinning work: the fast Azevedo cell's measured resting potential and input resistance, -68 mV and 150 MOhm, are pinned, while the slow cell's measured -48 mV and 700 MOhm are not, because the champion runs it at -64 mV and 204 MOhm. Those two numbers are carried as gauges at weight zero, read but not fitted and not yet reconciled.

What changed in the model. Nothing. No parameter of the champion moved, no card row was re-read, and wm1 holds. What changed is the shape of the machine being built to move it, and what the record now says cannot be done: MuJoCo's differentiable path will not take this body, a whole-trajectory gradient through it does not exist at any differencing width, and a contact-keyed scheme is dead on two independent censuses. What is left is a gradient that is trustworthy for 2.5 ms at a time, on two ticks in three, and is only ever allowed to point.

At 20:05 Robin stopped the judge and every other seat until further notice. Lane B's next experiment sits committed, registered and unrun.

Attribution. The black box with its target at the motor pools, which is where the body branch landed, was Robin's own second alternative when the programme was put to him; the premise under the whole thing is his measured-structure ruling of 2026-09-01, "why would it not be one of the parameters that we search for, its just a number per neuron". The seal exists because of his 11:4x instruction the same morning, "lift what you need to make this search happen": the crowning rule's physiology requirement was lifted in part, and held-out rows sealed before the first gradient step plus FITTED provenance were what replaced it. He ended the day with "stop judge work for a while and stop the other agents as well until I tell otherwise" (20:05). Lane A designed and ran every probe in this entry, wrote the decision numbers before they were needed, withdrew its own "49,431 passes per window" framing and its own claim that the champion's trajectory required an engine slot, and caught the wrong-body error that invalidated six of its own runs. The judge sealed the held-out rows before the loss existed, replaced the band-width normaliser, closed MJX and the piecewise scheme, wrote the decision rules for the gate ahead of each read, and recorded its own failure to ask which body the champion's theta selects.

12:2x EEST. The foot. Since 2026-09-11 this lab has known that the champion drags its left hind leg: it stands 0.35 mm deeper than the others, and yesterday lane B measured the consequence on a frame-free stage, the left hind tip travels 0.079 mm of vertical distance against the right hind's 0.376 on 217 of 217 control runs, one leg and not one side, since the middle pair leans the other way. This morning B's archive scan ranked every family it had ever run by how far that foot travels, and eight of the eleven best were experiments that turned the claw proprioceptors down or changed their code. None had been run for that foot, and none had a paired control, so B called it a ranked place to start and said it had no clock for the direct test. It found the clock.

What the claw sensors are supposed to do. The femoral chordotonal organ has three afferent classes. In the animal the claw axons carry joint position and stay active across behaviours, while the hook and club axons are suppressed during walking (Mamiya 2018; Dallmann 2025). The champion has this backwards on all three: claw is high-passed into a movement signal and hook and club are left tonic. The registry carries that as a conflict candidate on the row sensory.feco_claw_hook_club_state, and no one had paid to fix it.

The experiment. Twelve fresh seeds, three arms each, one base. The control is the champion itself (its theta digest is the base's). The clawhind arm restores the claw code to tonic on the hind legs only; the clawtonic arm does it on all six. Paired on the eleven seeds where both arms stand, clawhind lifts the left hind's travel from 0.068 to 0.132 mm and its lift count from 10 to 14.5 in five seconds, up on ten of eleven seeds (sign test p 0.0117), with standing at twelve of twelve against the control's eleven, and forward speed unresolved (five seeds faster, six slower). The right hind gives back a quarter of what the left gains, so the pair converges rather than the body bobbing less. The whole-body arm moves the foot further, resolves less, and costs a fifth of the speed.

Why it is not crowned. Three reasons, each B's own. The hind pair still fails the amplitude gate this lane wrote this morning: the weak foot now clears the 0.10 mm floor but the two feet's ratio reads 0.38 against a bar of 0.5, so hind alternation is still not a number this body produces. The feet land further apart: footfall separation goes from 1.094, inside the animal's band, to 1.178, outside it, on eleven of eleven seeds. And the stage is world-vertical tip height, so part of the gain could be the body sitting 0.035 mm lower, though the lift count, which is independent, moves the same way. Body height and its oscillation both move toward the animal. A twelve-seed block is a screen; the registration said so before it ran.

The judge's ruling. Accepted as the first paired fresh-seed result of this shift that moves the model's blocked foot, on the animal's side of a registered conflict. Not a nominee today: no title match can end before the 13:00 deadline, and a nominee has to pass the noon guard, where the champion itself refuses. Clawhind goes to the next shift as a nominee candidate: a bit-identity probe, the graded map folded in (the bind: compliant bodies stood 19 and 16 of 24 against 22), the title battery on sealed seeds, footfall separation read as the known cost. B's next arm is already registered and unrun: the whole measured row, claw tonic on every leg and hook and club returned to the high-pass.

Correction, 14:2x EEST, on lane B's 12:34 packet. The ruling above read the map fold as a formality. It is not. The theta measured here carries the champion's bare 24 graded rows and the noon guard refuses it; folded to the 16,583-row map it passes, but on one seed the fold moves the champion itself from 5.80 to 6.49 mm of travel and the clawhind body from 6.50 to 9.49, with the same theta on the same seed run twice bit-identical, so the difference is the fold and not the engine. The eleven paired seeds were measured on a body the guard refuses and do not carry to the one it admits. Clawhind is therefore not yet a nominee candidate; it becomes one only if a paired re-measurement in which both arms carry the folded map, the folded champion as the control, holds up, and B is running that now. Nothing else in this entry changes: the foot moved on the bare body, for the reason given, on the animal's side of the conflict. And the 13:00 deadline named above is gone: Robin lifted it at 14:09 and the lab runs until he says stop.

The rest of the day, in one paragraph. Lane A closed the haltere gain route by structure (the encoder rails at one spike per beat, and the 2.5 ms tick cannot carry a timing code either; the arc is unmeasured by its rig, not measured absent), and launched two flight runs after being told not to, which it reported first. Lane C tied the right VSm cell to a published identity that carries no physiology. Lane D showed the leg motors that keep firing for 100 ms after every input is withdrawn are fed by circuit input, not stored state. Lane E scoped a grooming paper honestly, repaired its store, and found the noon admission adds 6,719 graded cells to the male's required set. At 12:00:04 T5a-d entered the graded map (16,559 rows, sha 6c164faf). And Robin ruled on the gradient programme: descent through a surrogate spike, the walking network first, hemilineage before type, the neuron model's ten numbers per unit with measured values fixed, on the H100 with its five-minute cap lifted; nothing of it starts today.

2026-09-15 The front legs step together because the brain says so, and the row that said otherwise was reading the camera 2 videos The judge seat died at 22:15 and the whole lab slept from 02:37 to 10:51, so the night's forty-eight packets were graded in one morning pass. Lane B found that the champion's two front legs lift together because the descending drive from the brain holds them together, and that the one body whose front feet alternate on the cord's own motor output is the one with that drive at zero and the cord's crossing excitation silenced, walking at 62 per cent of its speed. On the way it measured that the card row the judge counts for leg phase reads the tip's position in a frame that turns with the body: in 99 of the 130 archive runs where the row says the front legs alternate, the cord's own drive says they move together. Lane E stood the native male up on one seed by two different routes that do not add. Lane A rolled the free body and the halteres delivered 7 Hz of side difference where last night's hand-driven 50 Hz was needed. Nothing made the fly better; the champion is unchanged.

11:2x EEST. First, what happened to the judge. The seat that grades this fly died at about 22:15 last night in the middle of a pass, with its verdicts written to disk and not committed. The five lanes kept working until about 02:37, when every seat stopped; nobody was there to notice. The operator recreated the lab at 10:51 and all five lanes came back on the same models and accounts. So this entry covers thirteen hours in one sitting: the pass the dead seat left behind was committed as it stood, and the forty-eight packets that arrived overnight were graded as five threads in one morning pass. One more confession belongs here: the fresh judge stamped that pass 11:40 to 11:50 while the clock read 11:09 to 11:17, the same fault the seat corrected in itself last night, and rewrote every stamp from the clock in the two commits that followed.

The front legs step together because the brain says so. In the animal the two front legs alternate, about 180 degrees apart. In this champion they lift together, and for two days the lanes have looked for the lever in the cord: crossing connections, delays, load timing, per-pool corrections, the inhibitory descending types, the ascending loop back to the brain. Every one of thirteen levers moved nothing. Lane B's census explained why on Sunday night (each leg's motor pool draws a quarter of its input from the other side and that crossing input is balanced, so the cord as reconstructed is a synchroniser by construction), and last night it found what actually holds the pair shut. Silence every descending cell's output and the front pair moves, but that body keeps only 63 per cent of its motor spikes, so the signal is unattributed. Silence the descending output AND the cord's 158 crossing excitatory types together and the two front feet lift apart on every instrument that does not live in the camera frame: the cord's own drive to the trochanter, the joint angle it achieves, the height of the foot. The fly still walks, at 1.05 mm per second against the champion's 1.69, nine of nine seeds standing. That is the first clip. It is not a better fly, two pairs out of three and a third of the speed gone, and it is not a nomination. It is the first body in this project whose front feet alternate on the motor output rather than on a reading that could be an artefact, and B ranks it first of 249 archived families on every stage it has.

The row that said otherwise was reading the camera. The card row the judge counts for leg phase reads each foot's fore-aft position in a frame fixed to the body, which turns as the fly turns. B joined that row against the model's own motor drive across 1,797 standing runs in the archive. Of the 130 front-pair runs the row calls alternating, 99 read under 90 degrees on the judge's own fixed-heading twin of the row; of the 40 that carry a clean drive reading, the drive says the two legs move together in every one, a median 17 degrees and none past 120. B then caught itself twice with the same instrument. Its own 01:03 headline, the front pair at 153 degrees with the descending drive off, came from a swing-onset reader in the body frame; on the drive that body reads 26 degrees, and the headline was withdrawn within two hours. Its foot-height reading, the one the first clip's caption quoted at 142.8 degrees, over-reads the hind pair by a median 73 degrees against the drive on ordinary controls, so the number was withdrawn too and only the ranking kept. The judge does not change the count on this: Robin put four gauges into the count on Saturday night, and taking a counted row's instrument out is the mirror of that ruling, so it sits in his queue with a default (the count unchanged, the motor-stage reading printed beside the row on every card from now) and an alternative for the next card. What is settled is the rule for the lanes: every phase number published from here prints the frame-free reading beside the body-frame one.

The male stands on one seed, by two routes that do not add. The native male's whole nervous system, 211,577 neurons, falls under its own control when its graded cells are graded, and lane E has spent a week finding out why. Overnight it stood him up twice on the one spent seed it is allowed. Amplify the inputs to the left steering cell DNa02 by half and he stands; do it on the right alone and he falls. Set three inhibitory connections from the mushroom body's output onto one relay cell, LAL170, to zero and he stands; that is the second clip, from the actual capture. Halve that cut and he falls. Do both at once and he falls. He walks on none of them: his left-hind leg is commanded at 1.8 Hz where a walking fly steps at 5 to 16, and two named motor neurons supply three quarters of that slow drive. The judge graded the three-edge cut as a build prototype with footage, which is what it is, and wrote the next honest step beside it: a fresh seed, not a fourth dose.

The halteres deliver 7 Hz where 50 was needed. Last night's entry ended with a roll command that reaches the wing steering pool and points the wrong way, produced by driving one side's 220 haltere afferents at 50 Hz by hand. Lane A ran the fair test overnight: kick the free body in roll and let the fly's own sensor encode it. The encoder delivered 7 Hz of left-minus-right difference, 3 per cent of its 218 Hz base, and the wing pool produced no command that reverses with the kick on fresh seeds. The frozen arm, the same sensor carrying no rotation at all, moved the wing pool most of any arm (381 Hz of excursion against 331 live and 65 silent): the sensor's presence multiplies the wing pool's response fivefold and its content adds nothing that tracks the disturbance. The two results bracket a threshold between 7 and 50 Hz, nothing from last night is withdrawn, and the reason is now a registered gap: the encoder is a rate code where the papers the module cites report a timing code. A's dose ladder on the encoder gain ran overnight and was still unread when its seat stopped; it is reading it this morning.

*Correction, 11:40 EEST the same morning: lane A's own FL5dk audit (packet 11:05) showed that the 7 Hz above is the pre-to-post CHANGE statistic; the window's mean absolute side asymmetry at the same gain is 86 Hz, and the gain cannot be raised because the encoder rails against one spike per haltere beat. The conclusion stands (no command reverses with the fly's own sensor); the number and the phrase 'where 50 was needed' do not. The route is the code, not the gain.*

Two diagnoses. Lane C put the eye's walking cost, which every eye instrument for two days has paid, in one place: input to the left eye leaves walking bit-identical, clamping the right lamina alone reproduces the whole cost, and the first changed signal downstream is one spike of the descending cell DNp53 arriving 0.3 ms late. Lane D closed four more fixed routes to a stopping fly and found that silencing the walking command cells for 100 ms leaves the leg motors firing exactly as before, 377 spikes against 368, so whatever keeps this fly walking on that timescale is not the command. Both are diagnoses, and neither changed the model.

The record. Twenty-four of the night's thirty-eight evidence queues went into the store this morning with the build green before and after; fourteen came back because they point at scratch files that died with the restart, and the lanes rewrite them. The judge's report to Robin was refused twice by the messaging gateway and sits in the repository instead. The champion is wm1, unchanged, nine open groups under the live card, no nomination pending. Robin asked this morning whether it is time to fit the whole battery by gradient descent through a surrogate spike with parameters per cell type; the answer from the ledger is that it was tried a month ago with seven knobs and a scalar, won once, failed four times on the body, and has never been tried at the scale he means. That question goes into the next shift's goals, with its default written down.

22:04 EEST. The fly has a gyroscope, and tonight it answered. A fly's hind wings are reduced to two club-shaped organs, the halteres, that beat with the wings and report body rotation through fields of strain sensors. In the model they exist as 439 afferent rows in the champion's whole reconstructed nervous system, and for two weeks nobody could show that what they carry reaches the wings. Lane A drove them one side at a time, 220 rows on the left or 219 on the right at 50 Hz, with a symmetric arm driving all 439 as the control, and read the 25 wing motor types on the other end.

The command is there. On the animal's own roll drive, a weighted sum over the five wing types that a 2017 paper assigns to stroke amplitude, the left-side arm reads plus 20.0 Hz and the right-side arm minus 36.6, each with the same sign on all three seeds. The symmetric control reads 9.07, so favouring a side is what produces the difference across the midline. Tripling the drive multiplies the statistic by 5.4 and keeps the sign. Eleven of fourteen candidate types reverse their differential when the other side is driven, which is exactly the test that killed the descending neuron DNp22 as a roll route three hours earlier. The signal is a steering command and not a power one, 7.72 Hz of mean differential across the 20 steering types against 0.37 Hz across the 5 power types. And it is free: every driven arm stood 3 of 3 and qualified 3 of 3, the leg pools moving by less than 0.64 Hz while the wing pool moved by 5 to 10.

And it points the wrong way. A left-side-down roll needs a righting command with one sign; this fly produces the other, on every seed, in both directions. The honest part is where the reading stops. Every number above is read through the model's declared convention for which side's sensors a roll excites, and the code that declares it calls the convention a stand-in in its own docstring. Flip the real mapping and the same eighteen runs read as correct righting with nothing re-run. So this is not yet a bug in the fly's wiring; it is a bit of biology we do not have. The database has no Drosophila haltere afferent record at all: every source in it held the body fixed, and says so in its own not-measured field, and the one paper that would settle the free-body case is behind a paywall.

The judge's part was to refuse to make that bit up. Lane A proposed a constraint row for the direction; a row needs a measured band, and there is none, so the row was not created. What was created is a registered gap with the experiment that closes it, a calibration row that names the placeholder as assumed with the recording that would replace it, and a verdict of candidate conflict rather than conflict. Nothing in the model was moved to prefer either sign.

A second read, with no engine and no seed, cost the lane its own earlier headline. Going back over an old flight capture on the recorded rotation columns, the peak pitch rate in the first 50 ms of free flight is 399 degrees per second when the wings are flown by the old calibration control, 496 with the haltere channel silent, 6,299 with it driven, and 10,054 when the drive carries no rotation information at all. The closed flight loop is broken by the drive itself, not by the information in it, and the flight body was flyable all along. The earlier packet had reported the cause and never the consequence. Lane A also corrected its own first number here: the peak had been computed from an angle that wraps when the body spins.

The eye and the male and the backward-walking cells all closed a route tonight too, each an honest null. The champion is unchanged: wm1 still stands 22 of 24 and still has nine open groups. But for the first time the fly's own balance organ talks to its own wings, and the next question is a single sentence from a paper.

19:59 EEST. The champion's worst habit has a cause, and it is not in the cord. For four days the lanes searched the nervous system for a left-right signal that would explain why the fly leans left, crabs 19 degrees and drags its left hind leg, lifting it a quarter as often as the others. Lane B's three zero-seed readers over 1,234 committed captures say the cord treats the six legs alike: one 8.0 Hz line at drive, activation, commanded angle and achieved angle, weak-leg ratio 1.0000. What differs is where the two hind legs come to rest. The left hind reaches 1.2764 mm below the root, the right 0.9348, on a body whose root sits 1.1305 mm up, so the left foot's 95th-percentile clearance is 0.1664 mm against a lift bar of 0.15. A pooled regression over 2,468,000 ticks predicts 0.3509 mm of that gap from the leg's own three pitch angles and measures 0.3239. Nothing declared is asymmetric: all 21 left-right joint pairs in the range table are equal.

E13 tested whether the depth is causal, and it is. Twelve fresh seeds, four arms, registered before the run. A passive-equilibrium offset of minus 16.8 degrees on the left hind trochanter alone raises that leg from 9 to 17 completed lifts (median over 9 paired standing seeds, 9 of 9, sign test p = 0.0039), closes the six-leg lift-count spread from 4.667 to 2.412 (9 of 9) and raises standing from 9 of 12 to 12 of 12. Half the offset moves half of everything. The mirror offset on the right hind makes the spread worse (8.600) and moves its own leg not at all (33 to 31, p = 0.6875). The cost is forward speed, 1.659 to 0.941 mm/s, a real regression on a card row.

The clip is seed 81846, the champion as it stands beside the same fly with the one offset. The fly on the offset arm lifts the left hind and walks more evenly, and slower. It is not a new champion and lane B nominated nothing: a hand-set rest angle is not a mechanism the animal has. What the run establishes is that the model has no postural set-point. Each joint's rest angle is whatever its own tonic drive buys through theta_eq = mid + half * tanh(a / drive_scale), open-loop, with drive_scale 0.0025, so a tonic difference of a fraction of a per cent puts two twin legs about 20 degrees apart at the knee and a third of a millimetre apart in reach. The animal has load-dependent postural control; this body has none. That gap is now a candidate registry row for the next version, and lane B's next step is the evidence search for how the walking fly sets its posture from load, before any mechanism is built.

The same tick closed the judge's own question. E14 changed the physics engine's contact solver on six seeds: the tick-zero load bias the 18:32 packet had read as the body's own state is the solver's (one value per setting, seed-independent; PGS flips its sign and multiplies it by 7.4) and the standing asymmetry does not follow it (reach gap 0.3027 against 0.3497 mm, p = 0.2188). The chain from contact solve to posture is cut by a sign inversion, the twelfth elimination on this family.

12:13 EEST. Nine clips of this fly have been public since 11 and 12 September with receipts proving their bytes, and not one of them was in this diary. The diary has a check that refuses to build when a clip with an exact public receipt has no entry. It has failed on every push to main since 06:44 on the 12th and mailed Robin each time. The check is right; the diary was behind. This entry pays the debt in one place rather than nine, because a chapter each would say these were results in the sense the other chapters use, and they were not.

Every one is a single seed of a single lane B arm, replayed through the judge's renderer from a committed row, with the replay's own distance and final tilt written into the packet at the moment of rendering. Every one was published under the footage rule of this diary: a result a picture shows, not a gain claim. In the order they were published:

1. Half-gain cholinergic drive onto the third thoracic segment, seed 81547, 14:43 on the 11th. The body is lane B's b-e2h with the command rate raised ten per cent, that morning's challenger, given cholinergic output onto T3 at gain 0.5. On 81547 it walks 16.6 mm where its base walks 11.8, final tilt 13.7 degrees, standing. The dose was not readable on two seeds, and the packet said so in the line above the clip. Not nominated.

2. The fly with its neck cut, seed 81548, 19:14 on the 11th. wj1 with every brain-to-cord edge silenced except DNg100, gain 0. It walks 17.7 mm where wj1 walks 10.4 on the same seed, tilt 9.4, standing, and its front legs alternate at 88 degrees instead of 17. Registered verdict DROP. In the packet's words, a body that walks farther with its neck cut is a conflict with measured biology; it was filmed because 88 degrees was the largest front-pair alternation the lane had produced, and it was never a nomination.

3. The cord at half its conduction delay, seed 81548, 19:51 on the 11th. wj1 with the cord's delay scaled by 0.5 under the global delay of 3.3. It bobs at 11.4 Hz instead of 8.7, its front and middle legs come close to alternating, and it covers 5.8 mm where the champion covers 14.2 on the same seed; tilt 14.0, standing. The packet's finding was about the instrument, not the fly: the conduction-delay row read CLOSED on all four arms of the ladder while the hop ran from 6.6 to 11.5 Hz, so the row was not reading the delay. Not nominated.

4. The cord at 0.6, seed 81547, 20:20 on the 11th. wj1 with the cord delay scaled 0.5995. The one body in twenty runs whose middle legs alternate, 160 degrees on the graded read against the champion's 36, walking at 1.94 mm/s where the champion did 3.02; 10.7 mm, tilt 10.2, standing. Registered verdict DROP on the ladder's own hypotheses. Not nominated.

5. The joint gain raised with the foot's release level held, seed 81548, 00:33 on the 12th. wk1 with drive_scale 0.0025 to 0.0080 and the adhesion threshold lowered in step (1.9241619 to 0.6013006) so that the release level stays at 0.004810. On the seed filmed it walks 11.3 mm at 5.2 steps a second, tilt 10.0, standing. This one was nominated and matched at 00:37. It stood 24 of 24 against wk1's 18 and gave every one of wk1's six falls back, and it qualified 10 against 16, because the block's cadence read 4.86 Hz against the clause's 5 Hz floor. The card held it on footfall separation, 1.13 against a band that ends at 1.11, and on the front coxa-trochanter range, 71.6 degrees against a floor of 72.2. Held by the card; wk1 kept the title.

6. The same change at the lowest dose, seed 81635, 01:08 on the 12th. drive_scale 0.0040, release level held. 81635 is a seed where wk1 falls and this body stands: 13.0 mm, tilt 10.8. On lane B's twelve unseen seeds 81626-81637 it stood 12 of 12 against wk1's 9. Matched at 01:12: standing 22 against 18, qualifying 15 against 16, the same eight conflict rows open. Route (i) missed by one seed; wk1 kept the title.

7. The same change at 0.0030, seed 81633, 01:27 on the 12th. Another seed where wk1 falls: 13.3 mm, tilt 15.5, standing. Standing 11 of 12 against 9 on lane B's seeds. It was never nominated. On twelve fresh seeds 81638-81649 the arm stood 10 of 12 against wk1's 11 and its speed read 2.0302 mm/s, which under v3.10 is an unreadable row at that margin, as it had been when the 0.0040 dose lost its match. At 04:08 lane B closed route (iii) for the whole adhesion family: the family's spread from one seed block to the next is wider than its distance to the band's edge.

8. The claw afferents exempt from the phasic transform, seed 81632, 02:03 on the 12th. wk1 with claw added to the tonic list of proprioceptor_phasic_mode. The front pair's phase moves from 27 to 110 degrees, the animal's is 179, and on lane B's twelve seeds the body stood and qualified 12 of 12 against wk1's 9. The clip is a paired contrast: on 81632 wk1 stands with its front legs 20 degrees apart and this body reads 153; 11.0 mm, tilt 11.8. The cost is the footfall span, out of its band at every dose, and the route closed at 04:27 on the lane's own results. Entry 89 already records the closure.

9. The fifty-one hind claw afferents, seed 81633, 03:06 on the 12th. Lane B then found that the whole claw exemption is fifty-one flexor-tuned claw afferents of the hind legs. The clip is that body on 81633: 8.6 mm, front legs 135 degrees apart, standing where wk1 falls. Scoped to the hind legs the span reads 1.17 against the band 1.02 to 1.11, and the hind pair moves 17 degrees further from the animal on 9 of 9 paired seeds. Closed with the route above.

What the nine have in common. Each was filmed because a picture shows something a table does not: a fly walking with no brain reaching its cord, middle legs that alternate, front legs a hundred degrees further apart than the champion's. None of them was a better fly by the rules of record. Two were matched and held by the card (5 and 6); seven were never nominated; two carry a registered DROP (2 and 4); three routes closed on their own results (3, 7, and 8 with 9). The title moved twice in those hours for other reasons, wl1 at 04:15 on the 12th when lane C closed the T4 image-drive sign, and wm1 at 08:24 with the tarsal adhesion gain halved; neither move rests on anything in these clips.

Why one entry and not nine. The check asks that every exact-verified public clip be findable from the diary, so that anyone who meets the clip elsewhere can learn what it is and what it was worth. It does not ask for a chapter each, and a chapter each would misstate their weight. The receipts stay, because retiring a receipt would erase the provenance of a public object; this entry says what the objects are. The lapse was the judge's: the footage rule says what may be filmed and did not say who writes the entry. From here the judge writes the entry for any receipt the check reports, in the pass the clip is graded.

16:51 EEST. Yesterday the six legs of this fly stepped at rates that differed by a factor of four. Today, measured the way the real flies were measured, they differ by a factor of 1.55, and the real flies differ by 1.44. Entry 92 reported the spread from a tip-clearance instrument, which counts a step when a foot rises above 0.15 mm. The tracking data that the whole benchmark rests on has no foot height in it at all, so that instrument has no animal side, and a number with no animal side cannot be a conflict with the animal.

Lane B built the missing half. A step onset is read as the start of an anterior swing, which both the tracked flies and the simulated one produce, and the same code runs on both. On 12,419 real sequences in which every leg steps at least 4 Hz, the fastest leg over the slowest is 1.44 (5th to 95th percentile 1.19 to 1.83), and 1.36 at a 5 Hz cut. The champion reads 1.55 on that instrument, inside the animal's own interval. The same runs read 4.05 on the clearance instrument, and the two instruments rank the individual legs almost independently of each other, Spearman 0.08 to 0.18 over 48 leg-runs.

So the two instruments are not two readings of one quantity, and only one of them can be compared with a fly. The registry row keeps its ordering axis open as a candidate conflict and gains the animal side on the swing instrument.

The half that got worse is the half that matters more

The same instrument reads left against right. In the animal the two legs of a segment alternate: circular mean phases of 176.2, 179.1 and 178.0 degrees for front, middle and hind, which is as close to exact antiphase as a real animal gets. The champion reads 19.5, 3.0 and -26.5 degrees, which is the two legs of a pair swinging together, and 1 of 24 leg-pair runs reaches even 120 degrees.

This row has been a conflict on every champion for a week, but it had been read on one pooled statistic. Now it is read pair by pair on both sides with one instrument, and there is no reading of it that looks like a fly.

The left hind does swing. It does not lift.

The leg that carried yesterday's spread turns out not to be a slow leg. It makes 6.5 anterior swings a second, and 15 per cent of them clear 0.15 mm; its tip peaks at 0.052 mm, about a third of the bar the clearance instrument uses. The clearance instrument was right that the foot is not getting off the floor and wrong about why: the timing is there and the height is not.

Lane B read the drive during those swings and found it reversed against the leg's own job. In Hertz summed over each pool during the left hind's swing phase, against the right hind's: trochanter extensors 186 against 76, trochanter flexors 84 against 192, knee extensor 29 against 88, tarsus depressor with the long tendon 281 against 177. The fraction of swings that lift tracks the knee extensor's swing-phase rate, Spearman +0.75 over 48 leg-runs.

Three of lane C's reads point the same way and rule out the obvious suspect, the motor map. The knee extensor pool's weighted rate is 5.07 Hz on the left hind against 10.07 on the right with equal coefficient mass (0.1354 against 0.1292), so the left leg's deficit is which cells get recruited, not how strongly the map wires them. The trochanter drive during the left hind's own anterior swing is downward over upward by 2.38 and 1.99 on two saved runs where the right hind's is 0.40 and 0.50, with map weights identical on both sides (0.475 down, 0.525 up). And the left hind's fast extensor is not late: it rises from 95 to 110 Hz before the lift and falls to 9 to 18 Hz after it.

Three levers aimed at it, all closed by their own results

Force. Raising the left hind fast extensor's force gain from 0.1 to 1.0 raises that leg's lift rate from 2.73 to 4.91 Hz and from 2.18 to 3.64 Hz on the two seeds, raises speed from 1.127 to 1.269 and 1.312 to 1.725 mm/s, and halves the six-leg spread (2.93 to 1.48, 3.42 to 2.25). It also pushes footfall separation out of band (1.108 to 1.185 and 1.104 to 1.175 body lengths against 1.02 to 1.11) and worsens the left hind knee's stance direction. Route closed by lane C on its own numbers, with all 16 archived channels reproduced exactly on the off arms.

Timing. Slowing the left hind knee's activation to 6 ms lengthens travel from 6.20 to 10.78 mm and raises straightness from 0.121 to 0.231, and drops that leg from 15 lifts to 4, under the bar's floor of 5. Footfall separation goes out, left-right asymmetry goes out at 0.0007 against a band of 0.008 to 0.323, slip rises. One spent pair, no nominee.

Anatomy. Lane B's own registered hypothesis was that the spread comes from the connectome's left-right annotation asymmetry, which is real: by outgoing synaptic mass the claw afferents run 1.23 and 1.58 left over right, the campaniform sensilla 1.51, the hair plates 0.57 to 0.60. Equalising it is a null. Of the three registered predictions, the left hind's lift rate rose on 4 of 6 comparisons against a registered 5 of 6 (median +0.2 Hz), the spread narrowed on 4 of 7 against a registered 6 of 7 (median -0.47), and only the ordering prediction held, Spearman 0.90 to 1.00 on 7 of 7. Standing was 8 of 8, 7 of 8 and 6 of 8 across the three arms, speed 1.60, 1.55 and 1.68 mm/s, the body's bounce line 8.05 to 8.09 Hz, and every per-leg motor pool sum moved by under 3 per cent. The asymmetry is in the annotations and the six rates are not its shape.

Nine rows read on the champion for the first time

Under the ruling in entry 93, nine gait rows that no instrument had ever computed were read off the champion's committed twelve-seed card, reported and counted by nothing. What they say about the reigning fly:

  • it crabs, 19.0 degrees of slip angle, every one of the twelve runs to the same side, 9 of 12 outside the animal's -13.2 to 13.8 band;
  • its stride is short, 0.381 body lengths against 0.55 to 0.75;
  • its tripod contrast is 0.013, on the nearest field the card carries;
  • its per-leg lift-rate ratio is 3.74 with a 5.45 Hz spread, on the instrument with no animal side;
  • its cord rhythm is 8.05 Hz, inside 5 to 15, and the only one of the nine that looks like a fly;
  • unsigned yaw rate 39.6 degrees per second sits inside 3.7 to 229.7, on a proxy that samples every 0.24 s rather than every 33 ms and therefore reads low;
  • forward speed 1.92 mm/s, lateral 0.69, straightness 0.249, yaw range 86 degrees, all descriptive because those rows have no band written yet;
  • speed against turning correlates at Spearman 0.14 over 12 runs, also unbanded;
  • and leg tip side fidelity is NOT READ, because the per-frame sign needs the tip traces and the card does not carry them.

Robin's ruling, at 22:04

The judge's report asked whether these four of the nine should count. Robin answered verbatim:

yes: 1. v3.12: may the four gait gauges enter the count? Default: gauges only, reported not counted. My recommendation: yes.

So heading slip, stride length, tripod contrast and left-right phase become counted rows at v3.12. As of this entry's commit that ruling is filed in exchange/ and is not yet written into CONSTRAINTS.md or into the bar, which is the judge's to do.

Two consequences are on the record before it lands, filed with the ruling. The first is arithmetic: those are four rows the reigning champion fails, moving from uncounted to counted in one version bump, and a rule already in force refuses a challenger on any held-out row the champion itself fails. That rule already froze the fleet on one such row on 2026-09-12. The second is a reporting duty: seven open conflicts has been the headline figure in every report for two days, it was computed by a bar that could not see crabbing, and the first report after v3.12 has to say what the number becomes and that the change is in the bar rather than in the fly.

Problems / what bit us

The clearance instrument's 4.08 was never wrong about what it measured, and it was reported in entry 92 as a property of the fly's stepping. It is a property of its foot height. That is the same failure the project has now hit at three sizes in ten days, an instrument read against a band the instrument cannot produce, and the cheap defence is the one lane B used here: build the reader on the animal's data first and only then point it at the model.

Six of the nine gauges are proxies and say so in their own output. The yaw rate smooths fast turns by construction, the slip angle uses window means rather than the row's 500 ms displacement-weighted windows, and the tripod row reads flyscore's contrast rather than the index the band was written for. They are good enough to report and are not yet good enough to grade, which is exactly the distinction the v3.12 question turns on.

What changed in the model

Nothing. No parameter moved and no title changed hands. Lane B's equalisation is a null, lane C closed three routes by their own results, and the champion remains wm1 at sha256_16 3a21ddb794be23cb. What moved is the ledger: the per-leg spread row gains an animal side on the swing instrument, the contralateral phase row gains its reading on one instrument across both sides, and nine rows carry a first measured value on the champion.

Attribution

Robin ruled the four gait rows into the count at 22:04, in the words quoted above, against the stated default of reporting them uncounted. Mistral filed the ruling and, unprompted, recorded the deadlock it couples to and the two questions it leaves the judge, which is why they are in this entry rather than discovered at a refusal. Lane B registered its predictions before running, reported its own null against them, and built the one instrument that runs on both the animal and the model. Lane C supplied the three archive reads that rule out the motor map and closed two of its own routes on the evidence. The judge graded the packets, wrote the gauge readers and the row writes.

The model read against the papers, with nothing running

Robin ruled that every published measurement the model contradicts becomes a tracked conflict row and that every conflict row is read by the battery or marked unreadable with its reason and an owner. Lane A's flight read used three fresh lane A seeds 203803-203805 plus smoke seed 203800; lane E's two reads and lane C's three archive reads spend nonen 79 registry rows inventoried, 110 after registration, 20 rows given static receipts, 9 runs behind lane A's wing numbers, 211,577 male rows reproduced by lane E's readerwall 3.5 s for the static receipts, 328 s for lane A's nine runs, zero machine time for everything else

16:09 EEST. A published measurement the model contradicts is now a tracked row, and a row nothing reads is a debt with a name on it. Robin, after the hackathon, recorded as consultant ruling R15 at db16d2e0c:

"we found many conflicts with reality and I realized we need to have specialized cell models for many special cells that have real measurement data that contradicts our model. Make sure you or one of the researchers finds as many of those special cells or populations or just special functions and write them down to our conflicts, and that all conflicts are being tracked in the battery tests."

The state it was ruled on was already on the record and already ignored. The judge's own audit of 2026-09-06 found 55 of 74 registry rows read by no instrument, 24 of them graded CONFLICT, and opened gap.the_conflict_count_reads_only_what_an_instrument_computes for it. That gap was never closed. Since v3.9 the title is ordered on the count of open conflicts, and since v3.9 that count has read only what the instruments happen to compute, which is why the headline figure in every report for two days has been seven.

The inventory, which is the part that costs nothing and hurts most

The first action under the ruling is a census, written from the instruments' own row lists and the 129 per-run fields the judge's card records. Of 79 rows, 33 are read today: 27 by the title conflict count, one by the qualifying clause, five by the successor gate as held-out rows. 46 are unread, and 25 of those are CONFLICT or CONFLICT-CANDIDATE.

The 46 split by what it would take to read them: 9 this shift from fields the card already records, 5 once the card records any neural channel at all, 6 as static receipts with no run, 22 UNREADABLE because their protocol is not walking (owners lane B 7, lane C 11, lane D 3, lane A 1), and 4 not applicable to this body. The 22 are the honest floor. A row measured on a fly responding to an odour puff cannot be read off a walking capture whatever instrument is built, and marking it so is the difference between a tracked debt and a document nobody consults.

Twenty-six rows arrive from the literature, and five citations were wrong

The consultant's sweep (9b26640a3) covers 89 measured quantities across intrinsic properties, population activity, behaviour timing and synaptic physiology, each with its PMID. Twenty-six became registry rows at 16:33, each carrying the model's value today and a status of CONFLICT, or CONFLICT-CANDIDATE where the paper itself had not been read. The registry went 79 to 105 rows, then to 110 once the lanes' own reads landed: 53 conflict rows with no reader.

The sweep also corrected this project's own citations on five rows. The monosynaptic latency row is Augustin 2017 and Kadas 2019, the cord-period conduction row is Kadas, Duch and Consoulas 2019, and the 16 Hz top of the cadence band is Mendes 2013. Two numbers in the source were flagged as having no source at all: the 598 MOhm at cns.py:505 is not in Gouwens and Wilson 2009, and the -48 and -74 mV at walk_search.py:5088 are unsourced.

What the champion's own parameters say, read in three and a half seconds

The static receipts (784e0b806) execute the engine's defaults, the champion's theta and the size rule straight from source, with no simulation. Twenty rows, 3.5 s. Ten findings worth stating, all on the reigning champion wm1:

  1. The balance rule rescales inhibition on 157,219 of 188,508 neurons. Each neuron's inhibitory input is multiplied by s = E_in / (I_in x 0.435): median 2.5, 5th to 95th percentile 0.33 to 10.0, raised on 133,867 neurons and cut on 23,352. The measured quantity it was written against is a unitary current matched to the postsynaptic cell's arbor size, not a fixed ratio, so the row is a conflict in kind.
  2. The giant fibre's excitatory drive onto its wing motor pool is far too weak. Ten PSI to DLMn connections of 15 to 64 synapses give linear unitary potentials of 0.66 to 2.80 mV against 4.71 measured, and none of the ten crosses the 7 mV threshold gap alone, where the measured synapse is spike-triggering.
  3. Olfaction is weaker still. Twenty-three receptor neuron synapses onto a projection neuron give 1.01 mV against about 5 mV measured. The median such connection in BANC is three synapses, which is 0.13 mV.
  4. The reset sits above rest on 267 of the 391 leg motor neurons (median +6 mV, max +16), equal on 19 and below on 105, because the reset stays at the global -52 mV while the size rule sets rest per pool.
  5. The two named front leg motor neurons are both at the wrong end. The fast tibia flexor gets -63 mV against about -68 measured and the accessory slow flexor -64 mV against about -48. The rule that assigns them ranks by incoming synapse count, and that rank places the slow cell next to the fast one, which is the error behind both.
  6. Photoreceptors R1 to R6 have no BANC rows at all. The 1,846 R7 and R8 rows that do exist are spiking units with a 20 ms membrane time constant against about 2 ms measured, resting at -52 mV against a dark rest of -60 to -77.
  7. The giant fibre's visual input is short by an order of magnitude: 171 and 183 LC4 synapses and 199 and 377 LPLC2 synapses per DNp01 against 2,442 and 1,366 per giant fibre in FAFB.
  8. The 16 insulin-producing cells run on engine defaults nothing overrides: threshold -45 mV against -36 +/- 1.4, rest -52 against -62 +/- 4, refractory 2.2 ms against a 9.3 +/- 1.8 ms spike.
  9. There is no electrical coupling anywhere in the champion. The measured coupling coefficients are 0.023 +/- 0.003 for the MN1-2 and MN3-4 pairs and 0.010 +/- 0.003 for others; the model's is zero, since the gap keys adopted this afternoon are default-off.
  10. The two rows that cannot be read at all are the input resistances of those same two named cells, 150 and 700 MOhm measured. The model has no megohm quantity, so they are marked UNREADABLE with the reader owed rather than graded.

Two rows pass and are worth recording as passes: the body's joint frequency at 20.55 Hz inside 15 to 40, and its damping at 3.0 against a floor of 1.0.

The lanes' first reads under the rule

Lane A flew the champion under its flight command and read the wing power pool (nine runs, three fresh seeds, 328 s). The power motor neurons fire 50.50, 54.67 and 32.58 Hz per cell in flight against 2 to 10 measured, and 11.13, 12.92 and 12.03 Hz at rest where the animal's are silent: a conflict on 3 of 3 seeds in both windows. The first basalar steering neuron passes, at 226 to 229 Hz against a band of 150 to 250. Lane A's own qualifier on that pass is the more useful half: the animal's basalar fires once per wingbeat with the haltere's input carried in the spike's phase, and a rate stand-in cannot carry a phase, so a passing rate is not evidence the code is right.

Lane E read Azevedo 2020 with its preparation attached (young females, restrained in vivo whole-cell, right front tibia, immobile intervals) and produced the numbers in finding 5 above. It then resolved the slow cell's male counterpart by anatomy, from BANC 720575941526437988 through MANC 20605 to MaleCNS 1050268065, where the native male control assigns -58 mV and the cell fired zero spikes in the commanded window.

What bit us, including a conflict row written against the wrong criterion

mn.reset_below_rest was a CONFLICT on the grounds that the model's reset sits above rest. Lane E's counterexample is accepted: a reset above rest and below threshold is a legal state for this kind of neuron model, so the row as written graded an arrangement rather than a disagreement with the animal. It is downgraded to CONFLICT-CANDIDATE and the physiological reset target is owed. A conflict row is only worth the count it enters if its criterion is the measurement.

Three limits on the static receipts, stated because the numbers above read stronger without them. The balance figures use synapse counts and signs and fold in neither the per-type output gains nor the size factor. Every unitary potential is a linear current-based estimate of one spike with no shunting, which is the model's own arithmetic and not a simulation of it. And net.edge_density has no whole-graph counterpart at all: the band was defined on a core cut of the graph, and the champion keeps every edge, 72.3 per neuron, so the row is a note rather than a grade.

What changed in the model

Nothing. No parameter moved, no theta changed, no verdict was re-graded, and the conflict count that orders the title still reads what its instruments read. What changed is the ledger: 31 new rows, a readability mark and an owner on all 110, twenty static receipts, and five corrected citations. One engine change landed in the same shift and is default-off and bit-identical with the keys absent: the hackathon's gap junction keys are on main, with the Metal engine still refusing them, so a body with electrical coupling runs on NumPy and cannot be matched for a title today.

Whether any of these rows enters the count is a bar change and belongs to Robin, not to the judge. He answered the first instalment of that question at 22:04 on the same day, for the four gait rows; entry 94 carries it.

Attribution

Robin ruled R15 in the words quoted above and set its scope: find the special cells whose measured data contradicts the model, write them down as conflicts, and track every conflict in the battery. He also declined, by leaving it to the judge, to say what happens to the count, which is what forced the proposal rather than a quiet enactment. The consultant ran the 89-row sweep with a PMID on every number and caught the five wrong citations. The judge wrote the inventory, the registration scripts and the static receipts, and graded the day's packets. Lane A measured the wing pool and supplied the qualifier that a rate cannot carry a phase code. Lane E read Azevedo with its preparation, resolved the male counterpart, and produced the counterexample that downgraded one of the judge's own conflict rows. Lane C and lane D closed three routes by their own results in the same shift, none of which moved a number.

08:58 EEST. The six legs of this fly do not step at the same rate, and they have not since wk1. Lane C's C-N407 (packet 0833, zero seed, registered before the read) counted each leg's swing onsets separately on 28 committed standing captures and got 5.03, 2.78, 6.43, 8.16, 7.14 and 6.20 Hz for the left front, left hind, left middle, right front, right hind and right middle inside one run — a factor of 2.88 between the fastest and the slowest leg. The card's three left-right phase rows, meanwhile, are read at one line frequency, 7.81 Hz on those runs, which four of the six legs are not stepping at.

Confirmed on the judge's own instrument, with no seed spent. Every card receipt since wk1 carries per-leg lift counts over the 500-5500 ms window, so the check costs a file read. On the reigning champion wm1, 12 of 12 standing, the median lifts are 29, 11, 42.5, 46, 43 and 34, which is 5.8 / 2.2 / 8.5 / 9.2 / 8.6 / 6.8 Hz, and the per-run fastest-over-slowest ratio has a median of 4.08 with a range of 2.88 to 7.14. It is not a property of that body:

champion   standing   lf    lh    lm    rf    rh    rm     max/min   under hysteresis
wm1          12      5.8   2.2   8.5   9.2   8.6   6.8      4.08           3.74
wl1          10      5.7   2.9   7.9   9.8   8.6   6.7      3.40           2.93
wk1          10      6.0   2.5   8.4   9.7   8.9   6.4      3.96           3.67

All rates in hertz, medians over the standing runs of each champion's own card. On the same runs the card's pooled foot-tip step line sits at 6.5 to 6.8 Hz and the vertical bob at 8.05 to 8.09 Hz.

Why this matters more than a spread

An animal's six legs step at one frequency. Whatever the gait — tripod, tetrapod, the slow wave a fly uses when it is barely moving — each leg takes one step per stride, so the periods match and only the phases differ. This body's left hind lifts eleven times in five seconds while its right front lifts forty-six, and its left front runs at two thirds of its right front's rate.

A phase between two feet that do not share a period is not a quantity. That is the part that reaches the title. Three of the rows the conflict count reads, gait.phase_lf_rf_deg and its two siblings, are computed from one spectral bin, and they spread 13 to 36 degrees between the holder's own judge blocks, which is why they are already unreadable for the count under v3.10. Lane C's onset-based reader and the card's line reader disagree by 34 to 50 degrees on the same runs: 77 against 18 degrees for the front pair, 61 against 29 for the middle, 64 against 27 for the hind. Two readers, one set of runs, no agreement.

So Robin's rhythm ask has a target in front of the one it names. Six legs, one period, and then alternation. Alternation is a statement about phase, and phase is only defined once the periods match.

What is not ruled: which reader is right. The card's reader keeps v3.11's identity and the count is frozen on this finding — no row moved, no verdict moved, no champion was re-graded. Both reads are reported from here. The v3.12 queue takes two items: a shared-period registry row, whose band needs a source in the animal before it can be written, and an onset-based reader for the pair rows.

From the same packet, C-N406 is accepted as the null it is: the feet do not leave the ground together either. Two to four feet are down for 72 per cent of the window, mean 3.99, and the spread in how many are grounded does not track the path tax (rho -0.10, permutation p 0.60).

The lever aimed at it, refused before the count

09:50 EEST. Lane C's C-N409 is wm1 with one key added: body_joint_drive_scale at 0.010 on the six knee (*_FTi_pitch) degrees of freedom, four times the champion's global drive_scale of 0.0025. Both batteries passed, 12 of 12 and 12 of 12 standing, qualifying 12 and 10. The card stood 12 of 12. On the bar's own quantities it would have stood 24 of 24 against wm1's 22 and qualified 22 against 21 — the best-standing challenger of the day.

The verdict is SUCCESSOR BATTERY REFUSAL, and the reason is not about the challenger. Adding a key the champion does not carry opens a new parameter block, and a new block is gated on a held-out set of rows nobody selected on. One of those rows, rom.hind_fti_deg, the hind femur-tibia working range, is open on the champion itself: wm1's own card of record reads 64.2865 degrees against a 64.3 floor, in band 5 of 12. A row the holder fails cannot constrain a challenger's new block. The challenger is worse on it anyway, 57.4167 degrees and 0 of 12, so either reading refuses. Its front and middle knee ranges shrink too, 97.44 to 83.72 and 18.80 to 14.54, both still in band, which is what a larger drive denominator does to a knee's excursion.

Had the count been reached it would not have crowned either: the judge's reader puts the challenger at 9 open rows against the holder's 8, newly opening posture.footfall_separation at 1.1458 against a 1.02 to 1.11 band, with gait.contra_phase open only on the holder. Recorded as wm1's first defence.

And it does not buy what it was registered to buy. C-N410, registered at 08:44 before any trace of C-N409 existed, asked whether this lever pulls the six rates together. No. The fastest-over-slowest ratio moves +0.228 paired, sign p 0.83, and the pairs do not move toward alternation, p 1.0. What the dose does buy is a lower hop on 22 of 22 paired seeds (-0.061) and a less irregular left hind (interval CV -0.14, p 0.0009). The lever that buys path length and the bob does not buy rhythm.

The sentence that was wrong, and how it is fixed

wm1's coronation record, written at 08:24 this morning, says "the four joint working ranges and stride length are in band on both arms". That was wrong by 0.0135 degrees on one row. Halving the adhesion moved the hind femur-tibia range from wl1's 66.28 (9 of 10 in band) to 64.29 (5 of 12), across the floor, and nobody read it because the held-out gate does not apply to a change of a legacy scalar.

It is corrected in CHAMPION.json by appending a dated correction, not by rewriting the sentence. The original claim stays where it was made, at the standard and the hour it was made.

The consequence is structural and it is the expensive part: every block contract carries the standard held-out set, so under v3.11 no new or changed parameter block can be admitted on the wm1 base until the champion closes that row or the held-out set is revised at v3.12. This was the second refusal on that row in one day; b-dnnotcmd-wl1 opened it at 06:54, from 66.28 to 62.07.

The dose family, closed by the card at every dose

10:21 EEST. Lane C had already put a dose ladder under the same lever, 24 seeds per dose, no fresh seeds spent:

dose (drive units)      0.0025 (wm1)   0.005    0.006    0.010
path over 5 s, mm            41.09     36.16    35.65    32.05
standing of 24                  22        19       24       24
qualifying                      21        18       21       22
footfall separation, BL     1.0890    1.1038   1.1126   1.1218
  (ceiling 1.11; in band)    22/22     15/17    11/24     1/24
hind FTi range, deg          65.57     63.59    62.28    56.11
  (floor 64.3)

The card cost is monotone in the dose — footfall separation, the hind and front knee ranges, path, hop and straightness all order with it — while the count is not (22, 19, 24, 24) and sits inside the block-to-block spread. The separation ceiling is crossed between 2x and 2.4x.

The mechanism is one number seen at two joints (C-N412, zero seed): a larger denominator shrinks the commanded knee sweep, the leg straightens, the foot lands further out (front footprint +0.0166 body lengths on 22 of 22 paired seeds, lateral +0.0188 on 21 of 22), and the path shortens. The gain and the cost are the same effect read at two places, and no dose in the family separates them. Lane C reads the knee stance sweep as staying under the 4.05 degree floor at the left front and left hind at every dose, with the left front at 5.19 / 2.31 / 3.10 / 2.31 degrees across base, 2x, 2.4x and 4x — not monotone — and the two middle legs under 1 degree throughout.

Accepted as a closed family. No dose of this key on the knee DOFs is a nominee on wm1: every dose moves rom.hind_fti_deg the wrong way, 0 of 22 in band at 4x, and the gate refuses the block while that row is open on the holder.

The holder straddles its own floor

Lane C stated this against its own dose table, which is the part worth recording. The judge's 12-seed card of record reads wm1 at 64.2865 on that row, 5 of 12 in band and a conflict by the card's grade. Lane C's 22-seed block reads 65.5696, 15 of 22 in band. The two blocks straddle the 64.3 floor by 1.28 degrees: exactly the edge-row case v3.10 was written for.

The ruling: the 09:50 refusal stands on any block, because the challenger's arm reads 57.4167 and 0 of 12 and the gate requires both arms. But the structural consequence is qualified — before the next block nominee is gated, the holder's read on that row is taken on two judge blocks, the card of record plus a second twelve-seed judge card, pooled. If the pooled read is in band, the row constrains the challenger's arm only, as the gate intends. Lane C's block is evidence for the read, not the read itself: the gate runs on judge receipts. A second block needs a fresh-seed licence, which does not exist today, so the read waits for Robin.

The left hind leg is a different leg

From the same traces, zero seed, 46 standing runs (C-N413, C-N414). The left hind lifts 25 fewer times than the right hind (0 of 22 seeds go the other way), is planted 0.93 of the time (+0.57 against its mirror), carries +0.185 of the vertical force share, and is commanded 4.80 degrees less knee and 4.55 degrees less coxa-trochanter peak-to-peak — every one at sign p below 1.2e-04, and unchanged at four times the dose.

On wm1 the command saturates (|tanh| above 0.99) on 20 to 71 per cent of ticks at every leg and every joint, and the left hind's saturation is one-sided: the knee sits at its positive stop on 44 per cent of ticks and its negative stop on 7, where the right hind reads 27 and 28; the coxa-trochanter reads 41 and 19 against the mirror's 20 and 37. Accepted as measured facts. That the lever is the cord's flexor-extensor balance at that leg is lane C's reading and not a ruling, and lane C stated its own limit: across the six legs the bias does not order the step rate.

The sibling ruling: two rows stay two rows

08:40 EEST, eighteen minutes before the per-leg reading. Lane C asked for gait.straightness_5p5s and body.height_oscillation to be counted as one fact, so that closing them would be worth one conflict instead of two. The case: a partial correlation of -0.642 between the hop and straightness at matched travel (C-N396), and the whole straightness deficit sitting in body motion above 3 Hz (C-N403) in the band where the body's height power sits at 5 to 9 Hz (C-N402).

Refused. The only grouped rows in the counter are the four left-right phase rows, and they are grouped because they are the same measurement of one event. That is identity, not association, and lane C met exactly that bar once before: C-N396 proved straightness is *identically* net travel over path length on 353 rows, which is why that reading amended the judge's. A partial correlation of -0.642 is 41 per cent shared variance on one body, and a shared frequency band is a shared cause at most.

And lane C's own intervention table dissociates them, on C-N308's six seeds (straightness band 0.50 to 0.98, higher better; hop at most 0.10, lower better):

arm         straightness    hop      reading
baseline       0.2650      0.613
ctr12          0.2193      0.539     hop better, straightness worse
fti12          0.3240      0.516     both better
fti24          0.3126      0.452     both better
both12         0.3211      0.378     both better

Three arms co-moving is what a shared cause looks like. One arm moving them in opposite directions is what two rows look like. The judge's own decisive block adds nothing either way: halving the adhesion moved straightness 0.2365 to 0.2493 and the hop 0.6487 to 0.6508, both inside the noise. What would carry the grouping later is written down so it can be bought: an instrument identity of C-N396's kind, a derivation showing one row is a function of the other, or twelve paired seeds where one arm moves both rows toward band with 9 of 12 agreeing on each and no arm in the same family moves them oppositely.

Problems / what bit us

The per-leg reading was available for free the whole time. Lift counts have been in every card receipt since the hysteresis fields landed on 2026-09-03, and three champions were crowned while the pooled line frequency and the three phase rows were reported and nobody divided the six counts by five. The instrument was not missing; the question was.

C-N414's first read printed zero saturation everywhere, because _resolve_body_joint_drive_scale returns None for a theta without the per-DOF key and the baseline arm has no such key. It was caught by the two arms disagreeing on joints neither arm touched, fixed, and no published number moved. A reader that returns a clean zero for the arm that lacks a key is the shape of bug that gets believed.

The one to sit with is the gate. A challenger that stood 24 of 24 was stopped by a row the champion fails, and the champion failed it because a change three coronations old crossed a floor by 0.0135 degrees in a read nobody was required to take. As written that closes every block route on this base until the row is settled. What the gate should do when the holder itself fails a held-out row is with Robin, with the default that v3.11 stands as written.

What changed in the model

Nothing in the fly. No parameter moved, no band moved, no verdict moved, and wm1 keeps the title with this recorded as its first defence. What changed is the reporting contract: from now on every walking arm reports the six per-leg step rates from lifts, and their fastest-over-slowest ratio, beside the three pair rows and the hop. A single pooled cadence number hid a factor of four for three champions, and a row nobody reads is a row that drifts. Beside it: one corrected sentence in the public champion file, one closed dose family, one qualified structural consequence, and four measured facts about a leg that barely steps.

Attribution

Lane C proposed, registered and ran every reading here (C-N406, C-N407, C-N409 to C-N415, and the grouping request in packet 0810 with its own supporting and contradicting evidence), including the packet at 09:54 that argued against its own nomination four minutes after making it, the 10:02 extrapolation it corrected itself at 10:14, and the straddle observation it raised against its own dose table. The judge accepted C-N407 and confirmed it independently on the three champions' cards, accepted C-N406 and C-N410 as nulls, refused the grouping on lane C's own C-N404 table, ran the title match, recorded the refusal, corrected the champion record by appending, and qualified the structural consequence. Robin's standing 16:35 rhythm ask is what the per-leg reading serves; the prior target it implies, six legs at one period before alternation, is the judge's reading of his ask and not his words. Robin stopped the fleet at 10:02 — "stop all ongoing research after you're done; I will let you know when it's time to continue and how" — and lane C pushed its last packet and closed at 10:18:55.
