2026-09-12full standard

Half the glue, and the fly stops falling

The title changed hands again at 08:24. wm1 is wl1 with one number halved, the tarsal adhesion gain that pulls a planted foot to the floor, and it crowns with the conflicts tied at seven by standing 22 of 24 against 19 and qualifying 21 against 17, with no seed lost in the trade and no fall on the card at all.

commit the commit this entry lands in, on main; verdict of record the dry run at a8e14f897, live receipts 3c9498346, static receipt and nomination 9982d96dc, coronation e1e35afa0theta results-wm1-theta.json (sha256 3a21ddb794be23cb61f2015746c68f739746b4b4abbc10654546ffa8696bd970), the judge's copy of lane C's lanes/C/2026-09-12-c-adhhalf-theta.json, wl1 with adh_gain 30.0813 -> 15.0407 and nothing elseseeds both arms 30532-30555 (judge block, challenger run against wl1's receipts of record); card 30556-30567 against wl1's card of record; deterministic Metal engine, joint_int exact, spike_reg 44, three workersn 24 paired battery runs per arm plus 12 card runs per armwall 93.7 and 96.9 s per battery, card in the same block; nomination to coronation seventeen minutes

08:24 EEST. The champion is wm1, lane C's body again, and this time the change is one number. adh_gain, the strength of the modelling actuator that holds a planted foot against the floor, goes from 30.0813 to 15.0407. The theta diff against wl1 is exactly ["adh_gain"]. Fifty-nine keys and the whole T4 exemption that wl1 won its title with are untouched.

What it buys is the oldest open gap in this project's ledger: the champion falls. On the bar's twenty-four paired seeds the new body stands 22 times where the old one stood 19. On the twelve-seed card it stands twelve for twelve and does not fall once, where wl1 fell twice. Qualifying runs, the ones that stand AND keep cadence, go 21 against 17.

The part that makes it a clean win rather than a trade is the seed list. Four seeds qualify for wm1 and not for wl1: 30541, 30546, 30548, 30549. Not one seed goes the other way. Every run the old champion got right, the new champion also gets right, and it adds four. The conflict count came out TIED at seven against seven, so under v3.11 the title turned on the qualifying count, which is the clause written for exactly this case: same conflicts, better walking.

The number was never measured where it was set

The value it replaces, 30.0813, came out of a parameter search that scored displacement. The search never read standing at the value. Lane C's ledger already had the dose curve on an older body (12, 11, 9 and 4 of twelve standing at 15, 22.5, 30.081 and 60), and C-N400 put the halving on the current champion base over twenty-four fresh seeds of its own, reading 20 of 24 standing against 17. The judge's own block, run against wl1's receipts of record, read 22 against 19: the same direction, a little larger.

The dose landed and nothing else did. The adhesion downforce falls from 2.586 to 1.320 times body weight on fifteen of fifteen paired standing seeds (sign p 6.1e-05) while cadence stays at 5.4545 Hz on both arms, the hop stays at 0.64, and straightness moves 0.2365 to 0.2493, which is nothing. This is a fly that walks the way it walked and falls half as often.

Three things this is not

It closes no row. All seven conflict groups that were open on wl1 are open on wm1: the body still stands 1.158 mm tall against a band of 0.80 to 0.89, the left and right legs of each pair still step 22 to 45 degrees apart where the animal's step 178 to 180 apart, the body still bobs 0.65 of its height against a ceiling of 0.10, the cord's conduction delay is still 5.71 ms against 2.8 to 3.3, and both knee rows are still out. This is a standing result, not a gait result.

The median speed of the standing runs drops, 1.93 to 1.73 mm/s on the battery. That is composition, and it deserves to be said plainly: the three extra runs that now stay up are slow ones, and a median over a bigger, more forgiving set moves down. On the card, where each arm contributes twelve runs, wm1 reads 1.9411 against wl1's 1.9079 with six of twelve in band against five of ten. Both are under the animal's 2.0 mm/s floor, and the row was unreadable for the count either way.

It does not transfer. Lane E went back to its own archived run from 2026-09-09 and found that the same halving, applied to the native full-MCNS body at its own theta, LOST standing. Half the adhesion is right for this parameter set, not a fact about adhesion. And adh_gain is our actuator, not the fly's tarsus: lane C's own C-N397 and C-N398 showed the normal force is not what brakes the body, and that doubling the adhesion drops the fly, so the mechanism by which less glue buys more standing is still open.

What it cost to be sure

Seventeen minutes from nomination to coronation, on 48 battery runs and 24 card runs, three workers, the deterministic Metal engine with exact joint integration, and the verdict of record taken from the dry run over the committed receipts rather than from the live pass. The clip is battery seed 30534, the median qualifying run of the twenty-one by speed, replayed from the capture with a parity assert against the recorded row (9.5241 mm, 11.3349 degrees of final tilt) before a frame was drawn, and published byte-exact.

commit the commit this entry lands in, on main; verdicts of record lanes/judge/2026-09-12-verdict-b-dnnotcmd-wl1.log (06:54) and lanes/judge/2026-09-12-title-v311-b-dnrest-wl1-verdict.json (07:23, receipts 610f73508)theta lanes/judge/2026-09-12-b-dnnotcmd-wl1-theta.json (canonical sha16 ae83377b5a48dc20) and lanes/judge/2026-09-12-b-dnrest-wl1-theta.json (canonical sha16 0d9841a3a84a0cdd), each wl1 with type_out_gain zeroed on a named set of descending typesseeds both arms 30532-30555 (judge block, challengers run against wl1's receipts of record); cards 30556-30567; deterministic Metal engine, joint_int exact, spike_reg 44, three workersn 24 paired battery runs per arm plus 12 card runs per arm, per matchwall about five minutes of machine time per match on three workers

06:54 and 07:23 EEST. Two challengers, two verdicts, the title unmoved. Both are lane B's and both are the same idea at two widths: take the descending neurons that carry commands this body never issues, and switch their output off.

The finding underneath is the best walking lever measured in the whole shift. The front legs of this model step 19 to 30 degrees apart where a real fly's step 178 to 180 apart, and that row has been open under every champion. Silencing the 472 descending cell types other than the walking command DNg100 (6,182 cells of 188,508) moves the front pair from 27 to 128 degrees on twelve fresh paired seeds, with standing and qualifying 12 of 12 against the control's 10 and 10. Three narrower readings then failed, which is what makes it sharp rather than lucky: the command RATE is not a lever (every rate from full to zero leaves all three pair rows where they were, so it is the command cell's OUTPUT that moves them); no SINGLE behaviour carries it (the ten behaviour groups silenced one at a time buy 15.5 degrees between them against 85 together); and the ten together miss their own registered fresh confirm, 7 of 10 paired seeds at the bar against a pre-registered 9.

The wide body is REFUSED, and not on anything anyone was looking at. The successor battery gate reads a set of rows held out of the selection: four joint working ranges and stride length. b-dnnotcmd-wl1 newly opens one of them. Its hind femur-tibia working range reads 62.07 degrees against the animal's floor of 64.3, in band on 2 of 12 runs, where wl1 sits at 66.28 and passes on 9 of 10. Nothing in the nomination selected the hind knee, which is exactly why the row is evidence. Had the count been reached the body loses that too: 14 open rows against wl1's 11, opening the abdomen's lateral excursion, a coordination row, posture variability and the front CTr range, closing only speed. So the best walk of the shift is bought by removing brain activity this body never uses, and paid for in joints nobody was watching.

The narrow body is HELD BY THE CARD, and it is the closest thing to a successor since wj1. b-dnrest-wl1 silences 240 descending labels, 649 cells, those of the ten behaviours this body never performs. Both batteries pass. It stands 21 of 24 against wl1's 19 and qualifies 18 against 17, on the bar's own seeds, the first challenger in a day to out-stand the holder. The conflict count TIES at 7 groups, the same ten rows open on both arms. It is held on one row of the title card: gait signal quality, 5 of 10 runs in band against the holder's 8, with no row improved at the veto's threshold. Under v3.7/v3.8 a body that regresses without improving does not take the title, and the row it regresses is the rhythm's own cleanliness, which is the thing the fleet was asked to improve.

Read plainly. Both verdicts say one thing from two directions: switching off descending output for behaviours the body never performs buys standing and the front pair, and pays somewhere that was not selected. Once on a held-out joint range, once on gait quality. That is a real biological result stated as a cost, and it did not need a ruling from anyone: the instrument answered it in ten minutes of machine time across two matches.

What the lanes did around it is the other half. Lane B ran its own registered dose on the muscle loop gain and dropped the route (case (c): no arm moved a phase row by that row's own between-battery spread, and the standing rise the dose showed did not survive twelve fresh paired seeds). It then closed the two knee rows to every lever it owns, across sixty arms, and corrected its own closing sentence four minutes later: the middle knee's within-stance motion already clears the band's floor, so the row needs the motion ORGANISED, not enlarged. The judge re-read lane B's twelve captures with an independent episode cut and reproduced it: the middle knees move 7.6 and 9.6 degrees inside a stance where the other four move 31 to 43, and every knee follows its command to within five per cent. Both knee rows are cord-command defects, and the quantity to move is a timing quantity.

Lane C measured that this model's foot contact carries no information about the step at all (AUC 0.50), built the gate that does know it, and watched the fly stop travelling: net displacement 9.97 to 3.70 mm, straightness 0.23 to 0.10. On this body the slipping foot IS the travel. It then read every committed run and found that straightness is identically travel over path length, so at a fixed path budget the row is a distance; at matched travel there is still room, and what predicts it is body oscillation and joint saturation, not leg phase. The route survives, in path length rather than in travel.

For the next challenger: the base is still wl1, the holder receipts are still lanes/judge/2026-09-12-title-v36-c-t4exempt-wk1-battery{1,2}.json and lanes/judge/2026-09-12-card-c-t4exempt-wk1-metal.json, and a body that silences descending output now has two measured costs to answer for by construction: the hind femur-tibia working range and the gait signal quality row.

The footage is lane B's, from its own screen seeds rather than the match block, and it is attached here because it is what these two bodies look like walking: b-dnnotcmd-81672 (the 472 types silent) and b-dnrest-81680 (the 240 labels silent), both exact-verified against their published bytes. Neither challenger is a champion and neither result is an improvement claim; the clips are evidence of the front pair moving, which is the part of this arc that survived.

04:15 EEST. The champion is wl1, lane C's body. It is wk1 with one change: the four subtypes of T4, the fly's ON-motion detectors, 6,025 cells of 188,508, are exempt from the per-neuron homeostatic balance rule. Fifty-nine keys of sixty are wk1's. Nothing in the cord, the body or the walking command moved.

The row it closes has been open since 2026-09-05, and it was our conflict, not the animal's. The connectome gives T4 a net-excitatory columnar image pool (Maisak 2013: T4 fires more to ON motion in its preferred direction), and the balance rule that made the network runnable in August rescaled inhibition onto every neuron to one ratio, which turned that pool net inhibitory on T4a, T4b, T4c and T4d. Lane E built the scoped exemption the same day the row opened; lane C measured this week that the narrowest scope that closes it is the four T4 types themselves (C-N353: the same carrier sums as the whole optic lobe's 108,764 cells, to the digit), audited every changed synapse (C-N353b: all inhibitory, all onto T4), ran it against wk1 on twelve paired seeds and moved no graded row (C-N354), and wrote the nominee file without nominating it, because on C's own seeds the exemption arm stood one run fewer. The judge matched the file, since the bar's 24 seeds decide standing, not a screen.

The verdict is the instrument's. Both batteries pass (9 of 12 and 10 of 12 standing); standing 19 of 24 against wk1's 18, floor 18; card veto no regression and no improvement; floor veto no change read on the hop or the pair phase; then the count, 7 against 8. Qualifying 17 against 16 was not needed. The dry run over the committed receipts (31449e2b5, 04:01) is the verdict of record. The live run at 03:56 had read 8 against 9: committing the challenger's receipts gave its speed row a between-block spread (0.08 mm/s) wider than its gap to the animal's 2.0 mm/s floor (0.07), so the row is unreadable under v3.10 and counted for neither arm. Both readings of the spread clause exclude the same rows. Same verdict, one row fewer on each side.

Read plainly. The row closed is static: a summed synaptic weight on the built network, not anything the fly does. The walk did not change. The same seven groups are open on both arms: body height 1.17 mm against 0.80 to 0.89, straightness 0.24 against 0.50 to 0.98, the bob 0.65 against at most 0.10, the left and right legs of each pair stepping 19, 29 and 20 degrees apart where the animal's step 178 to 180 apart (wk1 30, 25.5, 17.5), conduction delay 5.71 ms against 2.8 to 3.3, and the two knee rows lane C read tonight (C-N356: the left hind knee closes during stance where the animal's opens, both middle knees move under a degree). Speed is below the animal's on both arms, 1.93 against 1.90 mm/s. The left hind foot is still planted, 2.55 steps a second against the right's 6.27 on ten of ten card runs. Standing 19 against 18 and qualifying 17 against 16 are seed noise: four seeds went to the challenger, three to the holder, and lane C's own 24 seeds read 17 against 19 the other way. This is wk1 with its eyes wired the way the connectome says, walking the way wk1 walks.

What the coronation fixes for the next challenger is the base. Every nomination is wl1 plus a change. A body with the same seven groups open that stands more than 19 and qualifies more than 17 crowns on the count. Any left-right phase row into band, or speed at or above 2.0 mm/s readable, takes the count to 6 against 7. Two levers move the front pair and none moves the middle or hind (C-N344/N347 on the body, lane B's 51 hind claw afferents in the cord, both closed on the rows the selection asks for); the middle and hind pairs sit 140 to 160 degrees off and only the conduction delay has reached them. Lane C is reading why the middle knee does not move (C-N357 to N360). Lane B's dose axis on the claw afferents is next in the cord.

The clip is judge battery 2 seed 30555, the median qualifying run of seventeen by speed (1.91 mm/s, 5.0 steps a second, 10.51 mm, tilt 16.2 degrees, front knee 96.8 degrees); wk1 qualified on this seed too. Replay parity against the battery row: 10.5144 mm against 10.51; 16.1712 against 16.17 degrees. Twenty-four of twenty-four, on the count

The title changed hands at 15:50. wj1 is wi1 with three of lane B's changes, one cord interneuron type at half output, the walking command a tenth faster, and the brain's cholinergic input onto the hind-leg segment at half strength. 15:50 EEST. The champion is wj1, lane B's body. It is wi1 with three changes: the outgoing gain of one ventral-nerve-cord interneuron type, INXXX466, at 0.5; the walking command rate at 103.69 Hz instead of 94.26; and one new kind of change, a seam. The 8,338 cholinergic cells of the brain that project into the hind-leg segment T3 reach their 3,811 targets there through 24,888 wired connections, and every one of those connections now carries half its weight. Fifty-five keys of fifty-eight are wi1's.

What the block said

wi1 was crowned on 2026-09-07 as the first champion that falls: 19 of 24 standing on the paired judge block, five runs on the ground, accepted under Robin's rule that closing a real conflict may cost a step above a floor of 18. Since then every challenger has been matched on that same block against wi1's receipts. Today's first two, both lane B's, stood more than wi1 (22 and 20 of 24) and were held by the card: the first walked too slowly, the second sat 0.01 mm/s under the speed floor with the front femur-tibia range short as well.

The third stood on all 24. Batteries 12 of 12 and 12 of 12, where wi1 read 11 and 8. It qualified on 21 (10 and 11), where wi1 qualified on 17; its three standing non-qualifying runs all failed the cadence clause a little under 5 Hz (4.73, 4.82, 4.91). On the twelve card seeds it stood 12 of 12 too. The standing debt wi1 has carried since the 7th, gap.the_champion_falls, said it would be repaid "when a champion stands 24 of 24 on a paired judge block again". That is this record, and the row is resolved.

What it did not do

It closes nothing. Under v3.10's filter both arms carry the same eight open conflicts: body height (1.1626 mm against the animal's 0.80 to 0.89), straightness (0.3079 against 0.50 to 0.98), the vertical bob (0.63 against at most 0.10), the left-right phase group, the conduction delay the cord period implies, the hind knee's stance direction and excursion, and the static T4 sign. The instrument's ordering is batteries, floor, card, count: both batteries pass, 24 clears the floor of 18, the card's veto reads one regression against one improvement and does not hold, the conflicts tie, and the count decides, 21 against 17.

The regression is the front femur-tibia range, 77.64 degrees against wi1's 80.73 with the band starting at 81.2: 2 of 12 in band against 5. The improvement is gait signal quality, 10 of 12 against 7. Footfall separation, the row wi1 was crowned for, stays closed, 1.0993 body lengths against 1.0686 in a band that ends at 1.11, but on 10 of 12 runs against 12. It walks slower on the card (2.14 against 2.44 mm/s) and steps faster on the block (5.41 against 5.27 Hz); both rows are unreadable for the count at twelve seeds and stay so. So: a steadier fly, not a more animal-like one. Robin's goal for the day asked for a champion with fewer open conflicts than wi1's three; this body does not deliver that, and the record says so.

The seam, and how it was allowed in

row_pair_seams is not a dial wi1 had. It multiplies a named set of edge rows, here every cholinergic brain cell's connection onto T3, by one gain. The contract says a candidate that adds freedom cannot be crowned until independent constraints exercise that freedom, so before the match the judge adopted the seam as a named parameter block: one tunable coordinate, the gain, bounded 0 to 1 from lane B's own ladder (0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0); the 12,150 cell identities pinned as non-tunable; five card rows lane B had never selected on (middle and hind coxa-trochanter and femur-tibia ranges, stride length) required to pass on both arms. They did: stride length 0.4265 body lengths, middle CTr 18.16 degrees, middle FTi 18.97, hind CTr 46.73, hind FTi 64.84, all in band. The type_out_gain block passed the same gate at 14:10. Every further change to the seam passes the same gate.

Lane B's own reading of the mechanism is narrow on purpose. The dose is not monotone at two seeds (0.25 and 0.75 each reverse on one seed), and no split of the seam, by descending-neuron group, by target class or by cholinergic prefix, carries the gain: each partial cut costs travel where the whole seam at half gains it. So what is on record is the whole cholinergic drive from the brain onto T3 at half strength, and nothing finer. Why a weaker brain-to-hind-leg drive keeps this body on its feet is not measured. The standing is, on 36 judge seeds.

The clip

Seed 30550 from battery 2, the median qualifying run of twenty-one by speed rather than the best: 2.12 mm/s, 6.0 steps a second on the ten millisecond read, upright at 8.25 degrees, 11.65 mm travelled. wi1 fell on this seed. Rendered on the deterministic engine with the replay's displacement and tilt checked against the battery row (11.6498 mm against 11.65; 8.2509 against 8.25 degrees), published exact. The brain's activity is above the body in the site's layer colours, the six ground loads underneath.

For the record

Verdict of record lanes/judge/2026-09-11-title-v311-b-e2h-cmd110-achT3g050-verdict-DRYRUN.json: "CROWNS (equal conflicts 8; count higher, 21 against 17)". commit the commit this entry lands in, on main; engine at c7d79be7e; registration in 992bb54f3 before the first runtheta results-wi1-theta.json (sha256 ba18676b65b3db0747532d344cd2a2847ac8e38335bb77d3c34b29e9b7802fe7) as the fixed mechanism set, spike_reg 44; thirteen dials overridden per candidateseeds search seed 30900 for every candidate; grading on 30544-30555; rng seed 20260912 on every arm; shuffle draw 20260911n 120 candidates and 36 grading runs per arm, three arms, 468 runswall 9 to 14 s per run on the deterministic Metal engine, one worker, rising to 86 s while the machine paged; about 3 h 20 min end to end including one restart

Question. Entry 83 answered the reader's question at fixed parameters and said the symmetric half was owed. Robin, an hour later: *"can you do a run where the tuning budget is the same for this exact example we have on the site now?"* So: given equal freedom to fit, at a small budget, does the measured BANC wiring walk better than a degree-preserving shuffle and a cell-type-preserving shuffle of it?

Predicted (lanes/field/2026-09-11-null-examples/PREREG-same-budget.md, committed at 992bb54f3 before any run): *"1. The measured arm's best graded candidate qualifies on more of the twelve seeds than either shuffle's best. 2. At this budget the measured arm does NOT recover the champion's 8 of 12. 3. Whether a shuffle stands at all is not predicted."* Falsifier: *"A shuffle arm whose best graded candidate qualifies on at least as many seeds as the measured arm's best."*

Method. wi1's theta of record is the fixed mechanism set on every arm. Searched from scratch, per arm and identically: the thirteen continuous dials with declared bounds in walk_search (SPACE: campaniform gain, force reference, drive scale, joint time constant, adaptation increment, command rate; SPACE_NETWORK without short-term depression: delay, adaptation time constant, balance target, synaptic scale, graded gain, graded midpoint, graded slope). 40 uniform draws, then 80 hill-climb steps from the running best with walk_search.neighbour's step (normal, sd 0.15 of the range, clipped), one 6,000 ms run per candidate on search seed 30900, scored by displacement if the run stands (v3.2 clause) else 0. The rng seed is the same on every arm, so the 40 random candidates are the same settings on all three wirings. The three best distinct candidates per arm were graded on 30544-30555; the arm's result is the best by qualifying, then standing, then median travel. Nothing starts from the champion's values.

Result.

arm                          stands  qualifies  travel   cadence  every-foot-lifts  standing in search
measured wiring               12/12     3/12    9.92 mm  4.73 Hz     12/12 seeds        62/120
degree-preserving shuffle     12/12     0/12    3.93 mm  0.77 Hz      0/12 seeds        51/120
cell-type-preserving shuffle   9/12     0/12    6.55 mm  2.18 Hz      0/12 seeds        46/120

Prediction 1 held (3 against 0 and 0). Prediction 2 held (3 against the champion's 8). The measured winner (candidate 87) stands on every seed, travels 1.7 to 15.0 mm, and lifts every foot 10 to 17 times per run; it misses qualifying on nine seeds on cadence alone, 3.8 to 5.3 Hz around a floor of 5. The degree winner (candidate 56) travels 3.8 to 4.1 mm on every seed with at least one foot that never lifts, its drive scale at the box ceiling and its campaniform gain at the box floor: a shove, not a gait. The type winner (candidate 81) falls on three seeds (179, 179 and 75 degrees), travels 2.6 to 8.9 mm on the rest, and never has all six feet lifting. Per-seed rows, dials and search traces: lanes/field/2026-09-11-null-examples/same_budget_search.json.

Interpretation. At this budget the shuffles are not dead, which the fixed-parameter clips could not show: given their own tuning both stand and both move. What neither reaches is a step cycle in which every leg lifts, which the measured wiring reaches on every seed from the same starting draws. The type shuffle, which keeps type-to-type counts, recovers more than the degree shuffle, which keeps only degrees; that ordering is the one the null family was designed to expose. This is one search per wiring, one search seed and 156 runs each: a screen, not the stage 5 experiment at the lineage's scale, and the page says so.

Problems / what bit us. The machine paged during the degree arm (lane D and this seat both holding Metal engines, then this seat alone with the compressor at 8.8 GB), and each run slowed from 21 to 86 seconds. The search was stopped at candidate 85 of the degree arm, the runner changed to a fresh memo per run so its memory stopped growing, and it resumed from its logged rows without re-evaluating any; the pace returned to 11 to 12 seconds. The restart is a runner change, not a protocol change, and is recorded here. "Stands" admits a sliding fly, since its travel clause is 0.3 mm; the every-foot-lifts column is what separated the arms.

What changed in the model. Nothing. No theta, registry row, bar or champion record is touched. The renderer gained a dial-override option to film the winners.

Attribution. Robin, 2026-09-11 morning: asked for the same-budget run on the page's example, then "just deploy to the site and send me a report on telegram when done". The Field Engineer seat (Claude Code, on the Pro) wrote the registration, the search runner and the clips, ran the three arms, and wrote the page section and this entry. The judge did not grade this; it is not a title event.

commit the commit this entry lands in, on main; lane A executions 11eaa2efa (FL5ae), d34f9a68a (FL5af), 58f7c939a (FL5ag), 3d3e1f545 (FL5ah), e260998e3 (FL5ac)theta results-wi1-theta.json (sha256 ba18676b65b3db0747532d344cd2a2847ac8e38335bb77d3c34b29e9b7802fe7) for the walking arm; the flight arms add the FL5v support (160 of 591 background edges to b1 silenced, zeroed count roles, prescribed flight legs, the hypothesised attitude input) and, in FL5ac, the sign-preserving pitch decoderseeds 203760 (spent) for every arm; the replication on 203763 belongs to entry 81n one seed per arm, six seconds of walking or 2.5 s of flight per armwall 116 to 160 s per pair on the deterministic Metal engine, one worker

Question. Entry 81 recorded a two-second flight with silenced motor inputs, and this morning it replicated on a reserved seed (entry 81's addendum). The flight runs on its own rig: prescribed legs, a wing model, a hypothesised attitude input, and a support that silences 160 of the 591 background inputs to the wing-steering neuron b1. The shared fly is the walking champion wi1. Can the flight support be carried into that body?

Predicted. Lane A's registered order was to read the walking rig first on every flight setting, and to treat any change in ordinary walking as a failure of the setting, not of the walk. No gain was predicted.

Method. Each setting was run as a pair on spent seed 203760: the walking rig for six seconds with the setting fixed on, against wi1's exact capture; where walking survived, the flight rig with a 2 nN m kick at release 3.5 s against the FL5z tumble. Deterministic Metal, full CNS, one worker; the committed readers reproduce each decision.

Result. FL5ac: keeping the sign of the pitch code when both sensory codes floor to zero while the wings beat gives the first recovery from the kick, 2.50 s of flight against 0.57 s, roll settling in 250 ms; the same setting tips the walking rig to 80 degrees against 12. FL5ae: the b1 background cut alone, with no flight task and no decoder change, overturns ordinary walking. FL5af: the smaller accepted support of entry 81 (the 160-edge cut plus the haltere delay) also overturns ordinary walking. FL5ag: with the cut removed the walker stands and the corrected decoder loses both complete flights. FL5ah: a shorter b1 membrane time (10 ms for 20) keeps the walker upright, 9.3 degrees against 9.8, but changes its motor output from the 335 ms bin on, so it fails the identity gate before flight is run.

Reading. The flight result is real and replicated, and it belongs to a body that cannot walk; the walking champion cannot yet fly. The two are joined by b1's background inputs: silencing them frees the wing steering and removes something the walk needs. A flight fix that leaves the walking rig bit-identical, off by default and on only in flight, is the remaining route, and it has not been found. No conflict row changes; the title is untouched.

2026-09-11 Null test examples, two shuffles at the champion's settings 2 videos A reader asked whether the wiring had been compared against shuffled connectivity with everything else held the same. At the champion's own 56 settings and on its own twelve title seeds, a degree-preserving shuffle stands frozen on every seed and a cell-type-preserving shuffle lands on its back on eleven, against the champion's 8 of 12. The clips and the counts are on a new public page. The symmetric test, giving each shuffle its own tuning budget, is stage 5 and still not run.
2026-09-11full standard

Null test examples, two shuffles at the champion's settings

A reader asked whether the wiring had been compared against shuffled connectivity with everything else held the same. At the champion's own 56 settings and on its own twelve title seeds, a degree-preserving shuffle stands frozen on every seed and a cell-type-preserving shuffle lands on its back on eleven, against the champion's 8 of 12. The clips and the counts are on a new public page. The symmetric test, giving each shuffle its own tuning budget, is stage 5 and still not run.

commit the commit this entry lands in, on main; engine at c7d79be7etheta results-wi1-theta.json (sha256 ba18676b65b3db0747532d344cd2a2847ac8e38335bb77d3c34b29e9b7802fe7) plus spike_reg 44, unchanged for every armseeds 30544-30555, the second block of wi1's coronation match, all three arms; clips at 30555; shuffle draw 20260911n 12 seeds per arm, one shuffle draw per nullwall about 10 s per seed on the deterministic Metal engine, one worker; the two clips about 2 min each to render

Question. Robin forwarded a reader's question on the evening of 10 September: how much does the biological wiring contribute to the walking, and has it been compared with shuffled connectivity while keeping the neuron models and the tuning budget the same? He asked for clips of the champion beside two shuffles with every other parameter unchanged, and a page on the site to hold them. This entry is the record behind that page, `/fly/null-tests`.

Predicted. Nothing was registered before the run. This was built as an example set on request, not as a test, and it is graded as one: the counts below are a screen at one parameter set, one shuffle draw per null, one seed block.

Method. The champion wi1's theta of record, plus the title match's spike regularity of 44, on the deterministic Metal engine with exact joint integration, six seconds per run, seeds 30544 to 30555. Three arms on the same seeds: the measured BANC wiring; a degree-preserving shuffle (the post column of the 13,620,865-row edge table permuted, so every neuron keeps its in- and out-degree and its partners are random; 215 self-connections and 32,631 duplicates made, kept and counted); a cell-type-preserving shuffle (each connection's target redrawn within the target's cell type, so type-to-type counts survive; 11,504 groups, 11,352,175 connections rewired, 2,268,690 left alone because the target has no type label). Both rules are nulls.py's, copied into the screen script so nothing that builds a simulation is imported on the side. Standing is the v3.2 clause (tilt under 51.68 degrees, height over 1 mm, at least 0.3 mm travelled); qualifying adds five lifts on every foot and 5 to 16 Hz on the ten millisecond hysteresis read. The champion arm reproduces its coronation rows to the digit on all twelve seeds, which is the engine's determinism doing what the 2026-09-07 merge said it would.

Result.

arm                          stands   qualifies   median travel   median cadence
measured wiring (wi1)         8/12       8/12         8.95 mm        5.09 Hz
degree-preserving shuffle     0/12       0/12         0.03 mm        0.00 Hz
cell-type-preserving shuffle  0/12       0/12         4.21 mm        1.18 Hz

The degree shuffle is upright on every seed (final tilt 2.4 to 3.3 degrees) and never moves: 0.007 to 0.072 mm of travel, no foot lifted on eleven seeds and two lifts on one foot on the twelfth. The type shuffle pushes off and lands on its back within the first second on eleven seeds (171.9 to 173.0 degrees) and on its side on 30552 (105.3); its travel and its lift counts come from a fly kicking on its back. Two clips at seed 30555, one per shuffle, sit beside the champion's published clip on the page; receipts and per-seed rows are in lanes/field/2026-09-11-null-examples/.

Interpretation. At these settings the recipe is specific to the measured wiring, and the two nulls fail in different directions: keeping degree and losing partners silences the cord, keeping the type summary and losing the individual wiring keeps the drive and loses the balance. That is the same shape as the 2026-08-14 dual battery, where the real and shuffled cores separated on coordination and stability rather than on tempo. What it does not show is that random wiring cannot be tuned to walk: the shuffles ran the champion's numbers, not their own. The symmetric experiment, real and shuffled trained under the same procedure and budget, is stage 5 of the order of work and has not run. The reader's question was in two halves and only the first is answered.

Problems / what bit us. The first render of the degree clip labelled an upright, motionless fly "FALLS", because the verdict line only knew the standing clause's pass and fail; it was re-rendered with a three-way label and the page carries the second render. The 2026-08-14 shuffle control, where a degree-preserving shuffle of the nerve-cord cut stood and stepped in band on 5 of 8 seeds at that day's body, is stated on the page so the new result is not read as if the question had always come out this way.

What changed in the model. Nothing. No theta, registry row, bar or champion record is touched.

Attribution. Robin, 2026-09-10 evening: forwarded the reader's question and asked for "a few videos of this latest walking champion and two connectome shuffles with other parameters the same" and "one more page to our company website which is named something like null test examples". The Field Engineer seat (Claude Code, on the Pro) chose the two nulls, wrote the screen and the renderer from the judge's champion renderer, ran the arms, published the clips and wrote the page and this entry. The judge did not grade this; it is not a title event.

Amended forward, 2026-09-11 afternoon: the same-budget half of the question was run the same day; see entry 86.

Nothing moved the integrated model. Correcting the neuron selection changes the scientific conclusion: different adaptation times across the two tripods move their neural phase. The earlier experiment had changed the wrong cells.

The 100/400 ms split raises the paired tripod gap by 28.35 degrees but stands 7/12 against 10/12. A 50/400 ms split raises it by 41.43 degrees and stands 11/12; speed falls from 1.91 to 1.23 mm/s. Standing therefore varies nonmonotonically across the fixed settings. This does not identify seed noise as the cause. The parameter changes also alter the mean time constant.

Among the nine identities standing under both the 50/400 ms arm and control, the phase gap rises 37.91 degrees, within-tripod scatter rises 11.25 degrees, and speed falls 0.595 mm/s. These comparisons preserve the effect and expose its costs. A phase shift is not yet alternating, coordinated walking.

C-N257 completed its engine runs before its summary code failed. The committed reader reconstructs the verdict from the saved records; the judge verifies the record identity and recomputes the comparisons. The stored scalar and spectral summaries do not replace raw trajectories. Future gain claims need those signals and footage. No title or animal acceptance band changes.

The other closed candidates retain their failures. D's combined intervention fails cadence and height on its second spent identity; the later command-switch candidate falls. E's six-cell redistribution also falls. Their committed readers reproduce those outcomes. H100 admission is now shared on main: all lanes together are limited to 8 CPUs and 41,250 MiB; GPU submission stays disabled pending Robin's quarter-share decision. The fast-extensor comparison adds a second scoped signal. Its all-leg overlay reduces the median imbalance between the tripods' foot-lift counts from 0.28990 to 0.10849 on twelve spent identities, improving each pair and standing 12/12 against 10/12. Among the ten identities where both stand, imbalance improves by 0.18095 and speed changes -0.1715 mm/s. These are crossings of a foot-clearance threshold; balanced counts do not yet establish balanced loads or alternating steps. The original hind-only rectification hypothesis still fails. Three reader failure cases are returned to B for repair, while the complete archived values reproduce independently.

The steering endpoints C-N264–N272 provide no qualifying heading control. D's withdrawal-only body falls; its supported command contrast retains 96.70% of walking speed and therefore does not stop. E's shorter motor synaptic endpoint falls, and brain adaptation's small speed increase costs support, lifting and heave. These outcomes close the named endpoints and leave the lanes' independent research active. Complete decision and readers: exchange/2026-09-10-1505-judge-build-review.md. C-N273 supplies a steering lead after those endpoints. DNa02 input passes the registered scalar screen. Excluding the identity that falls under both inputs leaves five paired standing identities, four positive yaw differences and a median difference of 75.06 degrees. This is a BUILD lead; intact visual steering and reliable direction control remain unproved.

B's FTi combination cancels: common-standing speed changes -0.414 mm/s, below both single arms. A ThC partner preserves the lift-count effect but also costs speed, so it establishes no general rule for combining gains. The weighting profiles lose standing. A's recorded roll-pulse recovery fails at both doses, while D's R159 stops at its height gate. D's separate component read shows that co-contraction alone cannot change wi1's active stiffness at fixed load. The complete decisions, scopes and reader receipts are in exchange/2026-09-10-1534-judge-build-review.md. No integrated-model or title value changes.

Robin next asked for a direct foreleg-bristle test of stepping or turning away, and for one agent to develop a working compass before integration. D owns the sensory-to-body comparison. A judge ruling that a joint was unpowered was wrong and is withdrawn. The first title battery of the night, on the adaptation constant's 100 ms rung, stood 23 of 24 and was held by the card: cadence and front knee range regress.

commit the commit this entry lands in, on maintheta results-wi1-theta.json (mn_gains size, signs measured, mn_transfer t2_remotor_manc6), unchanged; no parameter movedseeds B spent 81547 and 81548 (eight diagnostic runs); C's recorded plain seeds 50000-50023 (20 standing arms, read from disk) and spent 50000-50011 re-run for the 60-arm clock ladder and three 48-arm ladders; no fresh seed spent; 50619 and 108524 sealedn 20 standing plain arms read under two contact instruments; 61 standing arms for the yaw fit; 391 mapped motor rows and 34 femur reductor cells for the census; 8 engine runs for B's probes; 60 arms for C's clock ladder; 360 leg-pair phase measurements; 48 arms each for the inhibition, delay and seam ladders; 180 arms for B's bound-edge screen; 48 arms for C's hemilineage timing ladder; 36 and 60 arms for C's six-input scaffolds; 48 arms for B's reciprocal inhibition; 72 arms for C's hand-built tapes; 108 arms for C's coupling dose; 84 arms for B's labelled line at parity; 48 arms for C's adaptation ladderwall zero engine seconds for every lane-C read except the clock ladder (686 s) and the inhibition and delay ladders (542 s, 560 s and 607 s) and B's screen (about 2,450 s); about a minute per run for B's eight probe runs on the deterministic Metal engine

Question. The shared fly walks at 1.9 to 3.0 mm/s and walks crooked. Two lanes had measured a lopsidedness: the left legs carry more stance load on 19 of 20 seeds, and the front footprint sits 0.2 mm off centre on 24 of 24. Where is it, and is it in the body, the map, the wiring or the dynamics?

What was wrong first. At 23:5x the judge ruled that the right middle leg's thorax-coxa pitch joint had no motor neuron while the left had one, and told Robin so at 00:25. That was a muscle-table fact read as a joint fact. On the matrix the fly actually walks with, built with size gains and the T2 transfer and then normalised, that joint carries 17 motor neurons at full weight on both sides. Lane C found the error, lane B confirmed it against the delivered matrix, and the ruling was withdrawn on main at 00:3x and corrected to Robin at 01:1x.

What the map asymmetry actually is. BANC has 17 femur reductor cells on each side, all mapped, with left-right input within 3.7 per cent: the right side is neither thin in cells nor starved of drive. The one unequal mirrored axis is the middle leg's coxa-trochanter roll, delivered at 0.258 on the right against 1.0 on the left. Lane C's routing census found why: the front and hind legs put every femur reductor on that roll axis on both sides, but the middle legs route some to the thorax-coxa axes, four of six on the right and two of six on the left. The judge traced the split to its source. A transfer set, t2_remotor_manc6, re-maps six middle-leg femur reductors whose BANC manc_cell_type matches the MANC remotor type onto the pleural remotor and abductor muscle; the list is four right cells and two left, labelled TRANSFERRED under the male-transfer rule of 2026-09-04. The normaliser's max(colsum, 1.0) floor then leaves the right roll column under-normalised and divides the left one down, a 3.87 times delivered-torque difference. The floor transmits the asymmetry; it does not create it.

Is it load-bearing? Lane B lifted the right column to the left's delivered weight in memory, without editing any table, on the two spent seeds. The fly stands on both. On 81547 its tilt improves from 13.5 to 11.7 degrees; on 81548 it worsens from 9.2 to 39.9 and travels less. Lane B's earlier run had already shown that every arm removing the middle-leg handedness falls on one of the two seeds. The champion's walking is tuned around the asymmetry. Whether to keep the transfer as annotated, revert it or symmetrise it is a mapping decision and goes to Robin at noon.

The transfer, absent (B, 01:43). Lane B then ran the champion's theta with the mn_transfer key removed, the harness's own bit-identical default path, against the plain arm on the same two spent seeds, in memory, no table edited. On 81547 the fly stands either way and is slightly straighter without the transfer: tilt 13.5 to 11.3 degrees, tripod duty gap 0.362 to 0.306, the middle-leg footprint offset 0.015 to 0.006. On 81548 it falls without it: tilt 9.2 to 172.9 degrees, slip ratio 0.41 to 1.23. Lane C's assignment audit of the same night (N228, zero engine, both map extractions) says why. BANC natively gives the two middle legs six femur reductor cells each at equal weight; the transfer takes two off the left and four off the right, and it exists because the right middle leg natively has no pleural remotor and abductor motor neuron at all (the left has one). Reverting it empties that muscle again, and the fly that walks on 81548 needs it. So reverting is refuted as a shared change; keeping it leaves a 3.9 times torque deficit on one axis; lane B measured the third option, two cells from each side, in memory at 01:57: the fly stands on both seeds (tilt 13.5 to 14.7 and 9.2 to 11.5 degrees, tripod duty gap 0.36 to 0.30 and 0.35 to 0.36, travel 16.0 to 12.9 and 10.3 to 11.8 mm), viable and not better, so the noon choice is between the annotated 4-2 and a symmetric 2-2 that buys no measured gain. Eleven other side asymmetries in the map survive the transfer's removal and look like reconstruction noise (tarsus depressor 3 against 5 on the front legs and 5 against 3 on the hind).

One oscillator (C, 01:3x). Asking whether any cell of the premotor layer is rhythmic, lane C found that the layer's output is: the champion runs a single body-wide oscillation at 7.8 Hz. Sixty arms on spent seeds 50000 to 50011 (five per seed, paired on seeds standing under both conditions) gave the clock's law. Halving the synaptic delay raises the frequency by 12.8 per cent and a 12 ms delay lowers it by 15.0 per cent, while halving or doubling the body's joint stiffness moves it by 1.25 and 0.00 per cent where a mechanical resonance would move it by 29 and 41; period = 103.3 ms + 3.70 x delay, r 0.995 over a 3.85-fold range. It is a neural clock, and the four arms that fall keep the rhythm in their leg drives with the body's bounce gone, so lane C withdrew its own earlier story that the body bounces and the network follows. The clock reaches the coxa-trochanter pitch commands of all six legs within a median 18.7 degrees of one phase (360 leg-pair measurements, median coherence 0.829); across the two tripods the difference is 25.9 degrees, one seventh of the 180 a walk needs. Step frequency, 5.4 to 5.5 Hz, does not move under any knob. One phase delivered to six levators predicts, without further assumption, legs that cannot alternate, a body that heaves at the clock's frequency, feet that slip because all six push together, a walk that will not go straight, a descending command that can only scale the rhythm, and vision that moves no gait row. Lane C claims none of those as results; each is a cheap prediction. Its survivorship re-read of every visual steering arm on disk (ten tests, seven bodies, Holm-corrected) found no stable yaw sign anywhere. The fleet's question is now what would break one oscillation into six.

Fifteen knobs (C, 02:0x). Lane C then asked the two things the ledger still allowed. Premotor inhibition from half to four times its value leaves the across-tripod phase at 26.6, 25.7, 21.4 and 18.6 degrees: more inhibition tightens the lock. Coupling delay across its whole bound, 0.5 to 12 ms, leaves the coherent rungs at 29.3, 25.7 and 22.5 degrees, falling where a delay-driven coupling would rise, and confirms the clock's law out of sample within 1.4 ms at every rung. At 0.5 ms the population stops cohering at all (pair coherence 0.20, within-tripod scatter 116 degrees): the fly stays up on 11 of 12 seeds and travels 2.8 mm instead of 11.5. Delay is what holds the population together, not what could split it; by the clock's own law a delay-driven phase could never pass 97 degrees. With lane A's thirteen strength knobs of 2026-09-04 that is fifteen knobs and no per-leg phase.

The wiring's own bound (C, 02:1x to 02:3x). Lane C then read the graph the fly is built from, zero engine, each read registered before its first number. Across-tripod inhibition onto the coxa-trochanter pitch motor neurons is 1.57 times the within-tripod value at one synapse, but a leg's own inhibition is 2.5 to 3.1 times the sum from all five other legs, and no class gain in the ledger moves the one-synapse contrast by more than 0.024. At two synapses the contrast is movable, 1.05 to 2.61 against 1.50 as the champion stands, short of a half-centre, and the between-leg two-synapse coupling is net excitatory, a synchronising sign. Running that best case on the same twelve spent seeds (intersegmental inhibition at 4 and 16 times, commissural inhibition halved) leaves the across-tripod phase at 23 to 30 degrees against 25.7 plain; the strongest arm loosens the lock only by decohering it, as lane A had seen on another body. What would break one oscillation into six is not in the parameter space or in a class gain on the wiring; it is a structural decision, and it goes to Robin at noon.

The last screen, and a graph that does not care (B and C, 02:5x). Lane B then ran the last inside-the-ledger check it had registered: every remaining network coordinate at both of its bound edges, fifteen arms on the same twelve spent seeds, 180 runs, read only as reached, shifted or null. Null: nothing reaches the 120 to 240 degrees a tripod needs; four edges drop the fly on all twelve seeds; one, synaptic scale halved, stands on all twelve at 93 degrees across tripods and waits for its coherence to be read before anyone calls it a phase. Lane C, meanwhile, read the graph a third way, zero engine: a leg's premotor pool hears its own leg's afferents 2.2 to 4.0 times more than all five others, but they are 4 to 6 per cent of its input; and the linear gain from the premotor layer to the six leg pools is neutral between synchrony and tripod alternation at every frequency (ratio 1.007, six singular modes, one per leg). The loaded graph couples the six pools as near-independent channels fed one common drive; synchrony is what common drive buys, and the lock is a choice of the dynamics, not a missing wire. Lane E's read of the male build with the same instrument found no coherent clock there at all (four records, two seeds). What would give six legs six phases is a structural or engine decision, and it goes to Robin at noon with lane C's brief.

Timing, and a correction (B and C, 02:5x to 03:0x). B's shifted arm was read the way C's 0.5 ms arm was: at half synaptic weight the within-tripod scatter (109 degrees) exceeds the across (93), pair coherence falls from 0.865 to 0.524, and both sit near the 90 degrees that random phases give. That is a fly that has stopped agreeing on a rhythm, not one that has split into two tripods, and the columns that say so were written per run before the question was asked. B's connectome census then found the six CTr pools sharing premotor input equally within and across tripods, with the strongest sharing between same-side neighbours (4.56 times the rest, partner sign not read): the pairs a tripod holds in antiphase carry the most common drive. C found that the champion already runs a per-type delay map (length_by_type, 63 cell types at 1.0 ms over 413 cells), so the night's delay law is a law in the mean of a distributed delay, and the per-hemilineage timing C's brief had asked Robin for costs a search, not an engine change. N242 ran that search on the spent seeds: the 437-cell 13A inhibitory hemilineage delayed by a quarter and by half of the 128 ms period. The half-period arm stood 6 of 12 with across 41.3, within 31.6 and coherence 0.424, the twentieth knob and the same dissolution; the completion control alone (all 73 13A types at 1.0 ms) kept the across median at 26.3 but tripled the within scatter, 9.3 to 29.3, so the offset arms are read against it and not against the champion. PARTIAL by its registered rule; no arm alternated.

Six inputs, and a clock that does not need the body (C and B, 03:2x to 03:5x). The open question was whether the six pools could hold six phases if something gave them six. C tried to deliver them through the fly's own afferents by moving the legs in tripod with a body scaffold at the pools' own 7.8 Hz (N244), and then with the network's output to the muscles cut so that only the afferent stream reached the pools (N245). Neither delivered: at gains 0.5 to 8 the scaffold never produced a tripod pattern at the feet (tip amplitude 0.02 to 0.05 mm against the champion's 0.26), both runs read VOID_NO_INPUT by their registered gate, and no neural claim was made. The control that mattered came free: with the motor output cut and no scaffold the fly lies still and the clock runs on unchanged, across-tripod 23.7 degrees at coherence 0.865. The lock is intrinsic to the network; the body is not in the loop that holds it. B then wrote the reciprocal inhibition by hand, scaling the synapses of each leg's private inhibitory cells that the same-side neighbour drives (eight seams of about two thousand edges) by two, six and eighteen. The across number rose to 44, 33 and 59 degrees; the within number rose with it to 40, 81 and 62 and coherence fell to 0.54, 0.44 and 0.53. The twenty-first knob, and the same dissolution. What remains is not a knob: a six-phase input channel the fly does not have tonight, which is an engine and mapping decision.

The body is the channel, and the pools are deaf to it (C-N246, 04:06). C then built the six inputs by hand. The ledgered playback path drives the joints from a flexor/extensor tape while the network runs, receives every afferent and cannot reach the muscles. The tape was the champion's own drive statistics with a 7.8 Hz oscillation added, in tripod phase or in synchrony, at one and four standard deviations. Delivery was certified on the channels the afferents carry: joint angle across the tripods 180 degrees, within 0, load across 179 and 176, on twelve seeds of twelve, and the synchronous tapes read across 0. The pools did not move. Tripod tapes gave neural across 24.5 and 18.0 degrees at coherence 0.85 and 0.79; their matched synchronous controls gave 23.0 and 23.6. POOLS_DEAF by the registered rule, with the instrument exact on plain. The defect is now located rather than described: the afferent-to-pool coupling in this fly is too weak to re-phase the pools, or their mutual lock too strong, which is the same shape A read in flight the same hour, a pitch loop twenty times under-gained and a roll loop open. The next question is the dose.

The dose, and the census that predicted it (B 04:17, C-N247 04:57). B sized the channel first, without an engine: each leg's own afferents are 1.7 to 3.6 per cent of its CTr pool's input by synapse mass and outweigh the other five legs' afferents onto that pool ten to twenty-nine times, a labelled line rather than a wash; the direct afferent-to-motor route is small and 92 to 100 per cent excitatory, while the two-hop route reaches three quarters of each pool's input through premotor cells that are half inhibitory. A channel like that can set how hard a pool fires, not when. C then multiplied every synapse leaving the 5,200 leg afferent rows by four, sixteen and sixty-four, with the tripod tape and its synchronous twin at each gain. Four changed nothing that followed. Sixteen and sixty-four dissolved the clock in tripod and synchronous arms alike: within-tripod scatter 79 to 139 degrees and coherence 0.26 to 0.59 against the champion's 10 degrees and 0.87, and at sixty-four the tripod input left the across number 19 degrees below its synchronous twin. Registered verdict PARTIAL, since no gain followed; the mechanism is gain-induced decoherence that does not care about the pattern, the twenty-second knob. More afferent drive breaks the lock instead of steering it. What is left in the engine is B's labelled line, the excitatory direct route alone at parity; what is left for noon is the mechanism question, since gains, delays, wiring and inputs have all been tried.

The line alone, at parity (B, 05:2x). B then gained only the direct afferent-to-motor edges of the three engine-driven classes, per leg, until each leg's own afferents were half of its pool's input (gains of 27 to 58 by leg) and then twice that, with C's certified tripod tape and its synchronous twin through the same path; 84 runs on twelve spent seeds. The ungained control reproduced C's deaf pools (24.5 against 23.0 degrees across). At parity the pools heard the pattern and answered backwards: the tripod input tightened the whole-body lock, across 16 degrees, within 18, coherence 0.63, while the synchronous input loosened it, 65 and 40 degrees at coherence 0.82; at twice parity the tripod arm decohered (47, 53, 0.36). B's registered rule stamps it DECOHERENCE and B adopted the judge's description beside it: heard, not steered, the twenty-third knob. The pools change how tightly they lock, never which phase each leg gets.

The one knob that moves the clock's rate (C-N248, 05:19). The axis left untried was the cells' own adaptation constant, tau_w, one number shared by every neuron. C ran it at 20, 100, 271 (the champion) and 400 ms on twelve spent seeds, 48 runs. The period followed it on 12 of 12 seeds, 116.3 to 131.6 ms over the whole legal range (slope 0.037 ms per ms, sign p 0.0005), and the six-leg phase structure did not move anywhere. Registered PARTIAL: a 15 ms spread against a 40 ms clock bar, a weak frequency knob and no phase knob. The 100 ms rung stood 12 of 12 where the champion stood 10 of 12, rescuing seeds 50006 and 50008, with within-tripod scatter 7.4 against 10.2 degrees and coherence 0.892 against 0.865; paired, only the period change survives Holm. C filed it as a champion candidate with one key changed and no claim, and the judge took it to the v3.11 title battery on the holder's own block.

The battery (judge, 05:33 to 05:44). The judge ran the candidate through the v3.11 title match on the holder's own paired block, 30532 to 30555, with a fresh card on 30568 to 30579. It stood 23 of 24 where wi1 stands 19, the best standing of any arm ever put to the block, and it was held by the card: its step frequency fell to 4.91 Hz against the animal band's 5.0 floor (4 of 11 card runs in band against wi1's 10 of 12) and its front knee swept 68.5 degrees against a floor of 81.2 (0 of 11 against 5 of 12), with no row improved; open measured-data conflicts 9 against 5, qualifying runs 8 against 17. A longer adaptation buys standing with slower, shorter stepping. wi1 keeps the title, and the card seeds are spent.

What the walking actually is. With the joint-to-body link checked (a no-slip fit over the planted feet predicts the body's angular velocity at slope 0.928, so the legs do drive the yaw), lane C decomposed every stance into how far the foot slid through the world and how far the leg stepped. On 20 of 20 standing plain arms, under two contact instruments that agree on 86.7 per cent of ticks, 65.7 to 84.8 per cent of the champion's forward travel is its loaded feet sliding. Tarsi move at 3.4 to 6.5 mm/s in stance against 25 mm/s in swing, so the detector is finding stance. The same records show the fly stands on the tripod left-front, right-middle, left-hind alone 57.3 per cent of the time and on the other tripod alone 3.6 per cent, a duty gap of 0.358 on 20 of 20 arms. The left-heavy stance load was the left-side projection of that: the sign alternates front, middle, hind. The lean is in 13 of 15 bodies on disk and reverses only under a bilaterally symmetric knee sign flip, so it is a broken-symmetry state of the dynamics, not a lopsided map. Vision moves posture and never stepping; the descending command into the leg pools changes amplitude and never timing; an 8,220-cell premotor layer carries 87.6 per cent of motor input and is reached by 95 per cent of descending output. Nothing in this model retimes stance.

What it means for the score. Speed alone no longer says the fly walks. The judge's v3.12 proposal adds travel earned by stepping and the tripod duty gap as title rows, and puts two questions to Robin at noon: the six-cell transfer, and whether a whole-brain fly whose premotor layer carries most of the motor input should be expected to make its own gait rhythm.

Not claimed. No behavioural cause of the crooked walk is shown by a wiring census. The predictions of the one-oscillator diagnosis are predictions. No parameter moved, no fresh seed was spent, no gain is claimed, and wi1 keeps the title.

Correction, 2026-09-10 11:14 EEST. B found that C-N249 changed the wrong neurons. The judge reconstructed the production motor map and ID joins: none of its 391 ordinal motor positions was a leg motor neuron. The corrected 10,760-row membership matches B's IDs exactly. Its original 26,915-row run cannot reject per-leg detuning, determine coupling strength or show that the connectome lacks a phase mechanism. Those conclusions are withdrawn; the corrected experiment stays open. This corrects an instrument and does not improve the fly. The battery paragraph also used "longer" incorrectly: 100 ms is shorter than wi1's 270.98 ms. Every title number and the verdict stand. Evidence: lanes/judge/2026-09-10-1114-n249-scope.json; reader lanes/judge/read_n249_scope.py.

The N247 audit also reproduces: 1,035 of its 5,200 source neurons enter the default external-rate callback, contributing 28.84% of its synapses. That fraction does not describe spike traffic; neurons outside the callback still receive recurrent input. No behavioural claim or acceptance band changes.

Further correction, 2026-09-10 11:32 EEST. C traced the same wrong motor indices into N250, N252 and N253. The judge reproduces 92 left and 103 right neurons in the supposed left group, and 98 of each in the supposed right group. Neither contains a leg motor neuron. Their steering-law and heading-authority interpretations are withdrawn. Correctly addressed tests remain open; the 90-degree bound of a two-oscillator approximation does not settle them.

B's direct shared-input lesion leaves median motor coherence at 0.824 against 0.865 in the control, with amplitude at 91% and peak share at 107%. That result applies to the declared shared edges into 110 motor neurons. The next-layer lesion loses rhythm before its phase change can be interpreted. A zero-input regression exposes a reader bug, but all completed records have finite positive amplitude and peak share, and their verdicts reproduce.

Two fresh seeds do not predict twenty-four

The best arm of the joint search cleared its licensed fresh pair and the judge's new block contract, then stood 15 of 24 on the holder's paired title block against wi1's 19 and qualified 11 against 17. wi1 keeps the title. No model improvement is claimed.

commit the commit this entry lands in, on maintheta lanes/B/2026-09-09-loco-09766-theta.json (file sha 64a1b5cf, canonical winner 8c5e21a8); holder results-wi1-theta.json unchangedseeds B fresh 81572 and 81573 under license; judge paired 30532-30555 (the holder's own title block); judge 30568-30579 licensed for the card and not spentn two fresh pairs (four whole-CNS runs) and twenty-four paired title runs, single workerwall 246.4 s and 243.3 s for the two twelve-seed batteries on the deterministic Metal engine

Question. Lane B's joint search over 11,578 type output gains, nine exceptional cells and 17 muscle gains produced loco-09766, the centre of its best family. On its two selection seeds it had fewer grouped constraint conflicts than the champion wi1 (7 against 9 on 81548, 7 against 7 on 81547). Does that hold on seeds nobody selected on, and does it hold on the block the title is decided on?

What happened, in order. At 22:25 the centre cleared its licensed fresh pair: on 81572 and 81573 it stood, lost no readable row, and counted 7 grouped open conflicts against the holder's 11 and 9. That made it the BUILD lead of the joint family. The successor gate then refused a title match until the judge adopted a block contract for the three parameter blocks, with instrument receipts for 25 selection rows and five held-out rows; that was done by 22:55 and the contract passed preflight. At 23:08 the judge ran the title battery on the holder's own paired block, 30532 to 30555, so that every seed is graded on both flies.

Result, simulated. loco-09766 stands on 15 of 24 seeds and qualifies on 11 (standing, endogenous timing, every foot lifting at least five times, cadence 5 to 16 Hz). wi1 stands on 19 and qualifies on 17. The protocol's verdict is HOLDER KEEPS (count); the v3.11 floor of 18 standing seeds in 24 is also missed, so the card on 30568 to 30579 was never run and those seeds remain unspent. The centre falls on nine seeds where wi1 stands, final tilt about 172 degrees, and on four standing seeds its cadence is below 5 Hz. It qualifies alone on 30533, 30539 and 30550. Where both flies stand, only one selection row differs: the centre's walking speed median is 1.90 mm/s, below the 2.0 mm/s floor, against wi1's 2.26. The five held-out rows (middle and hind joint ranges, stride length) pass on both flies.

Reading. The centre trades standing and speed on unseen seeds for fewer conflicts on the seeds it was chosen on. Two fresh seeds standing is weak evidence against that: at the centre's observed 62 per cent standing rate, two of two stand about four times in ten. The fresh-pair clearance and the block contract did their jobs, which was to make the title battery admissible; the battery then answered the question. Nothing in the shared model changes. wi1 remains the champion of record; loco-09766 remains the lead of its family, defeated once on this block.

The films. B26 shows the centre on fresh 81573, the arm that cleared the pair (displacement 12.68 mm, tilt 11.69 degrees, parity exact to the archived row). B25 shows it on spent 81548. Both receipts verify the public bytes against the local masters.

The posture films, a mechanism and not a candidate. B27 and B28 show the wi1 holder with one added rest-offset key, CTr pitch -20 and FTi pitch -5 degrees on all six legs, on spent 81547 and 81548. Body height drops from 1.21 to 0.87 and 0.89 mm, into the animal's band, and the front pair moves from 32 to 169 and 178 degrees apart, near antiphase; the cost is speed (2.90 to 1.67 mm/s) and the frozen reader calls the fly not standing, so the judge's counter opens ten rows against the holder's five. The dose is not proposed; the relation between posture and front-pair phase is the finding.

What follows. The judge will ask Robin at noon whether a build lead should show standing on at least ten of twelve spent seeds before a title block is licensed, since a two-seed clearance costs a fresh pair and predicts little. Lane B continues on the mechanism side: the posture set point that flips the front-pair phase toward antiphase (packet 23:05) and the body side of the left-right lopsidedness lane C measured on the champion (packets 22:54 and N216). Lane D tests the centre's motor-state selection on its own spent seed (R115), because the centre remains the best-integrated candidate the joint search has produced, title or no title.

Flight motor activity in the walking model

Question. Does the walking model keep flight-power output inactive, and can a different descending command recruit it selectively?

Prediction. A's pilot required control power-pool mean below 2 Hz and sustained 2–40 Hz activity in at least half the power cells under a flight command. These are prototype selection assumptions, not measured walking bands.

Method. A ran the whole 188,508-neuron BANC network on one reused seed. The body and theta were unchanged except for DNg100 versus DNg02 or DNp31 command populations. It recorded motor activity in 5 ms bins, then kept population and wing-cell summaries over 1–6 seconds. The judge checked the 17 execution source hashes, the BANC cell census, retained wing summaries and all three native Metal receipts. The original bins and body captures were not retained, so an independent raw-trace reconstruction is not available.

Result. With the walking command, DLM1–4 averages 21.5 Hz and DLM5 19.3 Hz; the complete 24-cell power pool averages 10.175 Hz. The 40-cell steering pool averages 16.295 Hz and the 49 neck cells average 42.3673 Hz. DNg02 and DNp31 raise the power-pool mean to 34.825 and 16.600 Hz. The frozen pilot outcome is CONTROL_POWER_POOL_NOT_QUIET.

Correction. The DNg02 arm was reported as fallen because the table used the old heading-sensitive quaternion-w test. Its accepted standing_v32 flag is true and mean final tilt is 11.8 degrees. All three stored accepted standing flags are true. This is a correction of the retained record; no raw body capture was reconstructed.

Interpretation. Robin made this a shared natural-walking and flight priority. D owns reducing inappropriate power recruitment while preserving walking and a usable flight response. A continues the wing/body model; B will add the instrument prospectively to future candidate diagnostics. The blanket assertion that every neck neuron should be quiet is not established: walking Drosophila move their heads, and identified neck neurons control head posture. Neither observation validates 42.3673 Hz; it requires a cell- and state-specific reference. Walking head movements; neck motor control.

Question. Can a calibrated wing pattern support the body, and which motor adjustments must a neural controller deliver to maintain its pose?

Method. A reused the Flybody flight configuration in FlyGym 2.1.0 with MuJoCo 3.9.0. Prescribed wings beat at 218 Hz. An initial amplitude/stroke-shift trim left forward force equal to 20.6% of body weight. A then disclosed and added stroke-plane angle as a third calibration parameter, keeping both arms. The external controller updates from the previous wingbeat's mean body state. No nervous system, learned policy or neural seed runs in this control.

Result. The three-dial trim supplies 0.999775 of body weight with mean pitch torque 0.002376 nNm. Over one simulated second, maximum height error is 0.2523 mm and maximum pitch error is 2.7046 degrees. Horizontal drift is +7.4941 mm in x and -2.4176 mm in y. The frozen HOVERS label checks height and pitch only; stationary three-dimensional hover has not been established. After a 6 nNm pulse lasting 5 ms, pitch excursion peaks at 20.1728 degrees and returns within 2 degrees after 97.1284 ms. The clip shows the external body control, including the perturbation and recovery.

Limits. Twenty milliseconds is the largest passing delay on the tested grid, with a 4 Hz controller bandwidth. The 30 and 40 ms rows fail; 21–29 ms were not tested. This finite controller comparison supplies no universal neural deadline. Its cited sub-millisecond haltere result comes from Calliphora.

Power correction. The lane packet compared 44.6838 W/kg of body mass with 50–130 W/kg of muscle mass. Fry et al. assume flight muscle is 30% of body mass, so their corresponding body-mass range is 15–39 W/kg. The model's trimmed aerodynamic power is 14.57% above that reported maximum. The claimed within-range match is withdrawn; six reported hovering flies do not define a new hard physiological band. Numerical servo power is a separate quantity. Fry et al. 2005, Eq. 6 and Table 1.

One full model must retain the walking and flight boundaries

Robin's Janelia reference makes coordinated whole-body walking and flight leg posture explicit requirements. His follow-up applies every subsystem's constraints to the eventual full fly. The judge registered four requirements: flight leg posture, sensory action selection by state, whole-body walking trajectories and speed/turn-dependent leg coordination. Their numerical readers remain open; they do not add four demonstrated conflicts to the current card.

The primary sources change how those requirements can be tested. The published Flybody walking reference uses tracked 2D landmarks; body height, pitch and full joint poses were partly estimated. Its released flight and walking tasks can disable the legs and wings respectively. Those controls therefore do not establish a single controller that switches the intact body between behaviors. Ache et al.'s tethered female flies give a direct state comparison: identical frontal looming evokes escape preparation while perched and leg extension for landing during flight. Keeping legs tucked through that landing stimulus would miss the observed behavior.

The shared mission, judge contract, registry and all six goals now require applicable constraints on the same complete neural/body/controller identity. The current neural title remains wi1. New comparisons will reuse retained full-pose traces and existing walking readers, with source scope and missing coverage recorded separately. The running joint search retains its frozen rank.

Question. Could the full male connectome retain standing after a fixed neural assumption changed, and could the first full-vector search candidates retain their gains on a second development seed?

Prediction. Lane E's frozen comparison required upright support with the accepted sensory and motor adapters unchanged. Lane B's frozen gate required fewer grouped conflicts on one paired seed, no increase on the other and retained standing, leg motion, speed, cadence and footfall separation.

Method. E set subthreshold adaptation adapt_a from 2 to 0, preserving spike-triggered adaptation and all other recorded neural and body parameters. Both arms used the full 211,577-neuron, 26,028,386-edge male graph. Its accepted adapters retain 328 mapped and 53 unmapped motor rows and 663 proprioceptors; R580-R587's source limits remain. The two saved readers, source hashes and native vectors were checked independently. Both videos reproduce the candidate run and have verified public-byte hashes and renderer parity receipts.

B selected four full-dimensional vectors under its frozen rule, then ran each and wi1 on both spent identities using deterministic Metal. The judge checked the ten native receipts against the local engine log, exact theta hashes and paired result fields. No new simulation was run by the judge.

Result. The male controls fell at 170.93 and 155.64 degrees. The candidates remained upright at 22.59 and 19.28 degrees. Candidate standing is 2/2 and control standing is 0/2, but qualifying is 0/2 for both. Simulated candidate speeds are 0.6983 and 0.4322 mm/s; cadences are 3.2727 and 2.9091 Hz, below the 5 Hz floor. All six feet lift in both candidate runs. These are reused seeds, so the result selects a working prototype without establishing a fresh-seed improvement.

The next shorter adaptation-decay endpoint fell at 170.26 degrees, and critical joint damping fell at 163.76 degrees, both on spent 108524 against the retained 19.28-degree control. Those endpoints close. E continues improving useful gait while retaining the standing prototype.

All four joint-search candidates increased grouped conflicts on 81547, by 1, 2 or 3, with no readable rows lost. Three decreased conflicts on the screening seed 81548. None clears. Four of sixteen keeper IDs have been used. CUDA and Metal screening speeds for these four match within 8.1e-11 mm/s; that bounded parity result does not replace deterministic Metal keeper replay.

Interpretation. The selected search gains did not transfer to the second identity. A holder's variation between seeds does not estimate the uncertainty of a within-seed paired difference. It therefore does not invalidate the paired gate. Repeating one deterministic seed adds no independent identities. The judge approved B's proposed second-seed screening before future ranking, under a new frozen manifest and rank. The four existing failures and acceptance gates remain unchanged. Both identities remain development data; fresh evidence is still required before an improvement headline.

Question. Robin asked which visual parameters and single-neuron models can be trusted after reading a discussion of FlyVis's response predictions.

Predicted. No prospective scientific prediction or simulation was made. The question was whether the live sources and calibration labels supported the claims being made about the visual system.

Method. The judge read the primary FlyVis paper, the pinned local model configuration, the imported tape and the current Lane C input generator. Source identities are recorded in the audit JSON.

Result. The ledger had one incidental FlyVis mention and no dedicated visual input row. Six rows now distinguish fixed structure, externally fitted dynamics, conversion to spike rates, the current hand-written correlator, its amplitude and BANC visual-cell dynamics.
