commit the commit this entry lands in, on mainseeds spent 81546 for the first screen, spent 81547 for transfer, spent 81548 for the complete wide screen, spent 81549 for an unlicensed diagnostic, spent 81567 and 81568 for pair 352, and spent 81569 and 81570 for the failed front-knee vector; 81571 was spent by failed fresh invocation and 81572 remains sealed

17:38 EEST.

Direction

One Lane B process now owns the complete behavioural search. The candidate vector contains one outgoing-gain coordinate for every nonempty BANC type label, separate coordinates for exceptional cells, and one gain for each of the 17 represented muscles. Other lanes may measure constraints or test distinct fixed biology, but they do not run overlapping type, exceptional-cell or muscle searches.

The search uses full-vector directions rather than one serial experiment per coordinate. This preserves all degrees of freedom while keeping one full-CNS evaluation near the measured 11-second local runtime.

Cell subclass is retained as a coarse hierarchical fit for a faster pass. Subclass values may initialise or regularise the child type gains; they do not remove the type or exceptional-cell residuals. Robin's working count is 176, while the pinned metadata contains 183 raw nonempty subclass labels, so the runtime-supported filter must be frozen before that route is used.

Executable smoke

Lane B's corrected smoke used the whole 188,508-neuron, 13,620,865-edge CNS. The baseline reproduced exactly. Both signed directions reached all 11,578 type coordinates, nine exact-ID overrides and all 17 muscle coordinates; all 391 mapped motor rows changed in the muscle block.

Both directions stood and moved all feet, but speed fell from the holder's 2.616 mm/s to 0.872 and 1.565. The result proves executable effect and bounded runtime, not a better fly.

Exceptional cells and constraints

The first six exact IDs all came from one IN21A003 basis. A manual audit of SPECIAL-CELLS.md found three more cells whose identities must remain separately expressible. The accepted BUILD manifest therefore contains 11,604 coordinates: 11,578 type labels, nine exact IDs and 17 muscles. The six original IDs are not replaced by the three new ones.

The current biological registry contains 75 records, and the v3.11 battery can execute 26 dynamic rows plus deterministic static receipts. Those constraints are enough to grade a full finalist, but they do not yet independently exercise every new parameter block. The missing rows do not delay BUILD. They prevent a candidate from becoming champion until exact judge-owned contracts and relevant held-out reads exist.

The first wave evaluated 16 paired full-vector directions on spent seed 81546. All 32 arms reached the runtime and three passed the cheap standing, all-foot, cadence and speed-retention screen. All three replayed exactly from committed source. The full v3.11 read found that pair 4 plus, not the faster pair 14, reduced grouped open conflicts: nine to eight while speed rose from 2.286 to 2.559 mm/s. It closed cadence and front femur-tibia range but opened gait-signal quality.

That signal did not transfer to a second spent identity. On 81547 wi1 stood at 5.273 Hz and 2.901 mm/s; pair 4 plus fell to 172.28 degrees with no readable cadence or speed. The fresh pair remains sealed and there is no clip. The first wave is closed as a routing screen. Pair 4 at half dose stood but opened ten conflict groups against the holder's seven; pair 14 stood but opened eleven. Neither dose supplied a transferable keeper.

A second screen repeated those 16 directions on spent 81548. Seven of 32 arms passed the cheap retention rule; three exceeded 2.0 mm/s. Two were directions whose earlier full-battery reads had already added conflicts. The only new keeper, pair 2 minus, stood at 5.182 Hz and 2.488 mm/s in the cheap read. The full v3.11 read stayed at nine grouped open conflicts against nine for wi1. It closed speed and front femur-tibia range but opened gait-signal quality and left-right asymmetry, so it did not license confirmation. An already-run 81549 diagnostic cut nine groups to eight while speed fell from 1.955 to 1.272 mm/s, below the hard floor. Pair 2 is closed and new directions start at 17.

04:50 EEST.

Question

Does the wrong-sign visual response already exist in the synaptic current into DNa01/DNa02, or does the target cell invert it through threshold, reset or refractory dynamics?

Method

The two C-N151 visual arms were replayed once on spent seed 50614 with the whole 188,508-neuron female CNS. A default-off recorder retained the four target cells at every 0.1 ms tick from 500 through 5,500 ms: target voltage, decayed excitatory and inhibitory conductance, spike and graded increments, signed engine current, and separate direct-visual and other-network routes. All nine named 5 ms population traces reproduce the earlier run exactly.

The raw artifact is 24,929,325 bytes with SHA-256 cd8969869ae4a376895c21d761b314a11a724d0d2cc83674489320cc4f4ebdd8. The Metal source stamp is 48ebcded0df39751; the dylib SHA-256 is c40c5e1ab0f16eb13ebd1bfa6a6e69363542c313d353dfafa26e42cc0fc55ce9.

Result

The first read mixed two calculations. C-N151 normalized the arm difference separately for each target side before subtracting right from left. C-N153 used that spike sign but classified current from a raw left-minus-right double difference.

With one calculation applied to both quantities:

  • DNa01 raw spikes/current are -41 and -17,380.423; side-normalized values are -0.270457 and -0.428943.
  • DNa02 raw spikes/current are +8 and +10,454.842; side-normalized values are -0.022909 and -0.101953.

The signs agree under both matched calculations. DNa01's raw response is negative in direct visual input (-1,580.749) and all other network sources (-15,799.678). DNa02 receives opposing raw components: +38,416.709 from the direct visual route and -27,961.872 from all other network sources.

Interpretation

The data do not place a sign inversion in DNa02's threshold, reset or refractory dynamics. That inference is withdrawn. The native arrays, conductance reconstruction, exact 5 ms parity and DNa01 upstream-negative result remain.

The result covers four cells in one female CNS on one spent seed. It does not select a neuron model or establish either cell type's population behavior. A later temporal test must state one response statistic before inspecting current or spikes.

Source closure in the same pass

The compiled-body audit now discovers fifteen consumers on integrated main. The shared selector guards every live whole-position reader, including CD2-GZ and Lane D R54. Corrected historical body-position counts remain 80,784, 79,764 and 80,580, and the independent qpos and foot-tip evidence remains.

Attribution

Lane C built the native recorder, ran the exact replay and caught the statistic mismatch before the judge verdict. Lane A repaired the CD2-GZ pose reader. Lane E found the fifteenth consumer and closed the integrated audit. The judge repeated the focused tests and retained the narrower result.

  • R3 middle-to-distal: 8.3743 and 9.0693 degrees.

03:06 EEST.

Question

Does projected within-leg order contain structure that the existing distal-tip phase and tripod summaries cannot recover?

Predicted

The registered fork treated held-out prediction above a training-label permutation floor as redundancy evidence, and prediction at the floor as no detected nonlinear redundancy. The learner, features, split and 200 permutations were fixed before fitting.

Method

The input contained 3,000 real trajectories. Four existing features entered a k=31 circular-neighbour predictor: tripod contrast, step frequency, gait signal quality and contralateral distal-tip phase locking. Each of the twelve R554 leg-by-adjacency rows was predicted separately. Training labels were shuffled 200 times while test membership and missingness stayed fixed. The same calculation was then repeated with the two real-data halves reversed.

The judge read an empirical lower-tail p-value from each retained permutation distribution and applied Holm correction across the twelve rows in each split direction. This familywise read was not part of the lane's nominal fifth- percentile decision and therefore grades the result rather than changing it.

Result

Five of twelve rows beat the nominal floor in the registered direction. Seven beat it after the halves were reversed. All original five repeated; the two additional rows were split-specific.

The strongest raw empirical p-value in either direction was 1/201, or 0.004975. Multiplication by twelve at the first Holm step gives 0.059701. Zero of twelve rows therefore clears adjusted p<0.05 in either direction at this permutation resolution.

Interpretation

Existing tip and tripod summaries carry some repeatable information about five projected-order rows. The calculation does not yet establish that any row is recoverable under a familywise test, and it does not establish full redundancy. Statistical independence and information gain remain open.

The shortest next computation keeps every modelling choice fixed, increases the permutation count to 4,999 and requires the same row to clear Holm p<0.05 in both directions. No simulation or new metric is needed.

The same merge exposed a separate source failure. Lane E's body-position audit found thirteen consumers on its branch, but integrated main adds Lane A's new CD2-GZ reader as a fourteenth. Question

Why were five of the twelve projected within-leg links unreadable on the standing wi1 replay, and did the same coordinate path still support the documented known-good CPG comparison?

Predicted

The selected R555 read was expected to separate missing target cadence from joint tracking and body-axis projection. The judge instruction was: "Separate a body-axis projection loss from absent wi1 command before any theta change." No adapter failure was predicted.

Method

The existing 6 s CPG trajectory and spent wi1 seed 108520 were read through the same 32-landmark adapter used by R554. Body names were checked against their compiled MuJoCo IDs before the kinematic surfaces were calculated. The repair uses the midpoint of the retained left and right eye bodies for the horizontal heading. Fifteen focused tests cover the R554 reader, R555 localization, an arbitrary poisoned c_head row and frame invariance under global rotation and translation.

The final wi1 read held each leg's cadence bin fixed and followed the 42 joint targets through achieved actuator coordinates, MuJoCo forward kinematics with a fixed body, the recorded free root, the recorded non-leg hinges and the full pose. Twelve observed poses supplied a 42-coordinate central-difference Jacobian. No altered pose advanced physics or entered the CNS.

Result

c_head is byte-identical to rh_tarsus5 on all 60,000 CPG frames. Its thorax-relative vector points 159.53 to 168.62 degrees away from the eye midpoint heading. The retained eye midpoint stays 0.2575 to 0.2603 mm from the thorax.

The corrected CPG remains readable on 12 of 12 projected-order rows, with 9 of 12 inside the real intervals instead of 8. The wi1 replay remains readable on 2 of 12 rows, but they are both on L3 rather than R2. R554's real-fly split still passes 11 of 12 rows, its fixed-membership disruption moves 12 of 12, and all seven scores remain exactly invariant to replacing the 18 non-tip leg landmarks.

The known-good CPG benchmark changes from 3 of 7 fields inside the real-fly central 90% to 2 of 7. Posture variability changes from 0.032681 rad, inside [0.025567, 0.085916], to 0.002051 rad, below the measured range. Tripod contrast and left-right asymmetry remain inside.

All five unreadable wi1 links carry target cadence. Same-leg coordinate composition cancels three projected middle links. Adding the recorded root attitude removes one left-front proximal and one left-middle projected link. No link is lost through actuator tracking, and the 18-by-42 Jacobian has zero cross-leg terms.

Interpretation

The canonical CPG control has an additional measured conflict: its abdomen to thorax angle varies too little. The earlier in-range value measured right-hind foot motion in the coordinate frame, not body posture. The correction does not regrade wi1 because the title card derives heading from the captured body quaternion rather than adapt_and_score.py.

The one wi1 replay localizes missing projected order after the joint target. It does not estimate a population rate and does not justify a theta change.

Problems

The exporter preserved a documented body name after MuJoCo fused that body out. The internal index was negative, and ordinary NumPy indexing made the failure look like valid finite data. The old Lane D adapter-equivalence checks used the same false heading on both sides, so numerical agreement did not validate the quantity's identity.

R556 reconstructs the historical comparison and restores numerical parity only after both paths use the eye midpoint. The source exporter can still emit the fused name, and four male-body audits compare whole position arrays. Their exact changed-element counts may count the right-hind tarsus twice; their qpos and foot evidence was not affected, but those counts remain to be re-read.

What changed

The shared adapter now uses the retained eye midpoint and rejects a non-finite or zero-length heading. The documented CPG count is reduced from 3 of 7 to 2 of 7. R554's simulated rows are replaced by the corrected table. The champion, theta and title bar do not change.

Robin selected walking observability and prohibited a new seed. Lane E built the R555 kinematic reader, exposed the fused-body fault before committing its first result, repaired the adapter and returned the corrected replay. The judge reproduced the seven-field change on the frozen CPG trajectory and added the frame-invariance gate.

The two numbers answer different questions. Four decided wi1 against wg1 on the evidence available at 12:49. Nine describes wi1 alone after the instrument learned to read all 26 dynamic rows available from a walking card and one deterministic network row.

What the added readers found

The four capture readers produced one closure and three conflicts on the same twelve runs used for wi1's post-coronation card:

The deterministic channel read the sign of the image-carrier input onto T4 from the built network. Both frozen arms were inhibitory on every subtype: T4a -10,278.1, T4b -18,060.1, T4c -12,425.3 and T4d -7,780.7. The animal row requires net excitation, so this adds the ninth conflict.

The other five are body height, straightness, front femur-tibia range, vertical bob and left-right phase. The pooled phase row and the front, middle and hind phase rows all disagree with the animal, but they count once because they grade one coordination family.

Why the old verdict stays

v3.10 removes a row from a match when either arm lies within that row's measured between-block spread of a band edge. That is a paired comparison and cannot be reconstructed from wi1 alone. Applying the raw count retrospectively would compare a new instrument on one arm with the old instrument on the other.

The title therefore stays with wi1 under its recorded result: four conflicts against wg1's five over the 22-row read, with standing 19 of 24 above v3.11's floor of 18. The next nomination runs through the complete executable path on both arms, including the deterministic receipt channel.

Identity and provenance

The card replay used seeds 30556 to 30567, which were already spent. All twelve runs stood. After removing the four added rows, their three added per-run fields, wall time and provenance text, every earlier scientific field was bit-identical to the committed card. The static result was generated separately on pushed main from the two frozen theta files and records the registry row contract, its source hash and both theta hashes.

12:49 EEST. The champion is wi1, lane D's body: wg1 with the claw afferent's signal passed through the phasic transform at gain 1.25, two keys changed of 56. It took the title from wg1, holder since 16:27 the previous day, and it is the first champion here that took the title while stepping worse by the count.

The decision, and who made it

The 11:55 report put one question to Robin. Both bodies matched that morning had moved the fly toward the animal on the biology card and both were held on standing alone: wh1 stood 21 of 24 against the holder's 24 and wi1 stood 19, drops of three and five against a gate of two. wi1 led on the quantity Robin's 2026-09-06 ruling had made decisive, three open conflicts against four, closing footfall separation on 10 of 10 standing card runs. Absent the gate it crowns.

Robin, 12:01: *"will allowing falling down on some of the examples accelerate our research and make us land a biologically more accurate fly faster in the future too? if so then let's do it."*

The judge's answer to the first half was yes, for one reason already on the record three times: a physiology correction dropped into a body fitted for its absence scores worse at first (the stop-rule amendment of 2026-09-01), and while the title refuses it no lane searches from a body that carries it, so corrections that each cost a few standing runs can never accumulate even where together they would repay the cost. Two had been refused that way in one morning.

The shape of the clause is the judge's, and it is a floor, not a wider distance. Born here: a gate stated as a distance from the holder ratchets, a floor does not. A champion that crowns at 19 sets 19 as the next reference, and a further correction costing five would crown at 14; a floor of 18 can be reached once and never passed. Eighteen is the count the phase rows need to be read at all (lane A measured 24 to 48 runs; twelve is not enough), it sits six above the per-battery minimum, and it admits every body held on standing this week while refusing one standing 17 or fewer.

The re-match

v3.11 named its own direct test: the same body on fresh judge seeds, both arms, since the holder stood 24 of 24 on its own block. It ran at 12:03 on 30532-30555 with the card on 30556-30567.

arm            standing   qualifying   open conflicts (16 rows)   (22 rows)
wg1 (holder)     23/24       23/24              4                     5
wi1 (challenger) 19/24       17/24              3                     4

Both conflict counts carry v3.10's filter, which made five rows unreadable for this match because each arm's median sat inside that row's own between-block spread of the band edge: cadence, speed, the pooled contralateral phase, the front femur-tibia range and the non-foot force. On both routes the one row that separates the arms is footfall separation, the lateral spread of the six footfalls in body lengths: wi1 reads 1.0686 on 12 of 12 card runs inside the animal's 1.02 to 1.11, wg1 1.1485 on 0 of 12. No champion has ever been in band on it.

The vetoes did not hold it: one regression (the pooled contralateral phase, 1 of 12 in band against 5) against three improvements (speed 9 against 5, footfall separation 12 against 0, and the vertical bob 0.025 body heights nearer the band on 14 of 18 paired seeds). Standing 19 is above the floor by one. CROWNS.

What it costs, stated because the ordering does not count it

It falls on 30533, 30547, 30550, 30552 and 30554; wg1 fell on 30542. A fly that ends on the ground a fifth of the time on flat ground disagrees with the animal, whose tracked walking sequences contain no falls, and every measurement the title is decided on is read from the standing runs only, so the falls thin the evidence as well.

The rows nothing grades moved the wrong way. On the paired block the front left-right pair steps 15 degrees apart where wg1 stepped 97 and the animal holds 178 to 180; the pooled contralateral phase, the row wg1 was crowned for moving, reads 0.2894 against wg1's 0.3113 on the same seeds; Cruse rule 1 ipsilateral on the tip read passes 3 of 12 card runs at p at or below 0.05 against wg1's 11, while the load read, which is the registry row, stays 12 of 12. Cadence is nearer the floor, 5.27 against 5.64 Hz, and one standing run at 4.82 did not qualify. The claw afferent is a tibia-position sense in the animal, so passing it through the phasic transform is a searched departure kept because it closes a measured row.

The clause carries all of that as a gap rather than in the ordering. gap.the_champion_falls opened in the coronation commit, owner lane D, expiring 2026-09-10, and past that date it blocks every coronation until a champion stands 24 of 24 on a paired block again or the expiry is renewed with a reason. The champion's record states its standing beside its title and the hall of fame publishes it.

Who did what

Robin made the decision, quoted above, and vetoed nothing else. Lane D found the mechanism on wd2 on 2026-09-06 (footfall separation in band on 5 of 5 paired seeds, 0.041 body lengths nearer the band), carried the two keys onto wg1 and nominated it with the theta frozen before the match. The judge wrote the floor's shape and number, launched the re-match on Robin's instruction, and had predicted it would crown; the numbers are the instrument's, and the 22-row hand count agrees with the sixteen-row one. The compute seat's two engine patches (one live engine per process; the decision-grade marker) were applied on main only after the match finished, so both arms ran on one code state.

What the fleet is pointed at now

Standing back from a body that carries the claw correction, which is the search the stop-rule amendment asks for before any stop; and the left-right phase group, which is the largest open disagreement with the animal and the one no champion has moved by more than the dice, now with the clause that lets a correction cost a step.

The aim published at 11:13 was dead by 11:19

The 11:13 report to Robin named one route: halve the nerve cord's presynaptic delay so the left and right legs of a segment alternate, which the animal does at 179.9 degrees and this model does at 20 to 36. Two lanes answered it inside the hour, from different sides.

Why neither of those numbers is a measurement

The champion has six committed twelve-seed blocks at one unchanged theta (sha256_16 628b58cd: two cards and four title batteries). The per-segment left-right phase median across them:

row                        block medians (deg)                 spread   band edge gap
gait.phase_lh_rh_deg   36.5  41.0  51.5  28.5  30.0  24.5        27.0          145.15

gait.phase_lf_rf_deg  134.5  95.0 138.0  92.5 123.0 109.5        45.5           61.55

Lane B's 35.5 and lane E's 32 both sit inside the champion's own hind range of 24.5 to 51.5. So do the other twelve attempts three lanes made on this row today, every one read at twelve seeds. Taking the range over six blocks as about 2.5 standard deviations, the median's standard deviation at that size is roughly 11 degrees on the hind row, and a ten-degree paired difference needs of order a hundred seeds per arm to resolve. Only a move of order a hundred degrees is visible at twelve, which is what closing the row would look like.

The conflict itself is untouched by this. The medians sit 145 degrees outside the band, five times the spread, so v3.10's unreadable-row filter does not reach them. What cannot be read at twelve seeds is a small CHANGE in the row, not the disagreement with the animal.

It also settles what one contradictory receipt is not. Lane E's R428 reported 143 degrees on the hind row for a theta that is byte-identical to the fork run today (both sha256_16 52a517fc1a55eb38, zero differing keys, because delay_region_scale replaces rather than composes). 143 sits 91 degrees above the top of the champion's own hind range, four times the block spread, so it is not a block draw; under the known middle-hind label swap it reads middle 143, which is 100 degrees above that row's range. Either the two reads labelled the legs differently, or that body moved a phase row by about a hundred degrees and two reads of the same theta today show nothing. One arm on the original seeds with today's reader separates them, and it is lane E's first item.

The second hold of the day, and what held it

wi1 is the champion with the claw afferent's phasic gain at 1.25, lane D's body. Over the 24 paired seeds it stands 19 times against the champion's 24, which is a drop of five against v3.9's gate of two, so it is held before anything else is weighed.

Everything else favoured it. Under v3.10 its open-conflict count is 3 against the champion's 4: it closes posture.footfall_separation on 10 of 10 standing card runs, median 1.0791 inside 1.02 to 1.11, where the champion reads 1.1485 on 0 of 12. The combined veto returns one regression and one improvement and does not hold. Robin's ruling of 2026-09-06 put the conflict count above the qualifying count precisely so a body like this could crown, and the boundary Mistral asked for in the same conversation, standing stays a hard gate, is what stopped it.

Both of today's nominations were held that way: wh1 at 21 of 24 standing, wi1 at 19. Neither was held by its card, and neither was held by the count. The binding constraint on this fleet today is falling over, and it is the one row the instrument reads cleanly at 24 seeds.

What bit us

This seat published a route to Robin as the fleet's aim and it was refuted in six minutes by the first lane to run it. The route was not chosen from nothing: it came from a receipt reading 143 degrees on a body that no longer exists as a separate body. The cheap check that would have caught it costs no seed and was run afterwards rather than before: hash the nominee's theta against the fork's before quoting a difference between them. Recorded here because the fleet is told to under-specify method and over-specify ambition, and a judge naming a mechanism is the failure mode that instruction exists to stop.

Who did what

Lane B ran the cord at 0.5 without inhibition and reported the cadence cost. Lane E ran it with crossed inhibition, on the fork this seat set, and called the route dead in one run; its own verdict sentence attributing the 143 to a different body cannot hold and was routed back to it rather than relayed. Lane A withdrew a registered arm rather than spend seeds on a question two blocks had answered. Lane D built and nominated wi1 on the row its own card closed. The judge ran both matches, measured the block spread on the champion's committed receipts after publishing an aim that rested on not knowing it, and refreshed every goal file at Robin's start-of-shift instruction.

Robin's instruction of 11:30 is what shaped the goals now in front of the lanes: "Under-specify the method, over-specify the ambition, and set a bar high enough that the lane has to find something you did not think of."

14:30 correction: the measured block sizes and the missing commit boundary

The 11:46 conclusion above was too broad. Halving the cord did not move the hind pair, but a later paired read showed a middle-pair direction. Lane B then repeated the paired comparison on twelve fresh seeds: the middle pair moved 51 degrees on 11 of 12 pairs, from 5.5 to 56 degrees, below its registered 80-degree bar, while speed fell from 2.81 to 1.59 mm/s on every seed. The route is held as a direction. It neither closed the grouped phase conflict nor supported the 82-degree size quoted after pooling two discordant blocks.

The 143-degree value was also resolved. It was the middle pair under the old leg-label order, not a different body's hind pair. Replaying the same frozen parameters through the corrected reader returned the same interpretation. The 11:13 report's halved-cord aim and its 143-degree premise are superseded by the paired lane-B result and this label correction.

The measured resample replaces the estimate above. Sixty distinct standing wi1 seeds from six committed receipts give 95% median widths of 40 degrees at the front, 20 at the middle and 19.5 at the hind for a twelve-seed block. A registered 30-degree change needs 24 front seeds and 6 middle or hind seeds; 50 degrees needs 8, 6 and 6. These are resamples of existing seeds, so they are a lower bound on drift across future separated blocks, not a promise about a new draw.

The audit also found a different instrument error. v3.10 and v3.11 said their repeat-spread gate used committed receipts, but its loader globbed the mutable worktree. Both wi1 decisions therefore saw their own match files before those files entered the atomic verdict commit. The replacement reads Git blobs from an explicit commit, counts an exact scientific run copy once, and proves parsed parameter equality before joining the lane nominee wrapper to the flat champion file. That join keeps all six wi1 blocks visible when the next holder receipt uses the champion file's different hash. Replaying each decision from its true parent commit excludes the same five rows as the saved verdict, so neither title decision changes.

The fixed-heading twin now accompanies each body-frame phase row. On the same twelve wi1 runs, front reads 40 degrees in the body frame and 11 with heading held fixed; middle reads 36.5 and 26.5; hind reads 16 and 40.5. The animal reference uses the body axis, so the original row remains the benchmark. The twin tests whether a change came from foot motion rather than body yaw over planted feet.

The row the instrument could not read

A challenger was nominated on closing the front knee's range, a row whose median moves 3.35 degrees between repeat blocks of one unchanged body against a nearest-edge gap of 0.45 degrees. commit the commit this entry lands in, on mainseeds wh1 batteries 30448-30471 paired against wg1's remade record on the same block; wh1 card 30508-30519 against wg1's card 30496-30507; the spread itself costs no seed, being read from six committed twelve-seed blocks of one theta

11:08 EEST. The champion is still wg1. One challenger was matched and held.

What was nominated, and what held it

wh1 is the champion with the front femur-tibia range corrected, lane A's morning body. Its whole case was one registry row, rom.front_fti_deg, and it does move that row: the card veto reads no regressions and one improvement, which is the row it was built for.

It was held before any of that was weighed. Over the 24 paired seeds wh1 stands 21 times against the champion's 24, batteries of 10 and 11 of 12, and v3.9's standing gate holds a challenger that stands three fewer. The three seeds it loses (30449, 30456, 30463) are seeds where the champion stands. A fly that tips over more often does not take the title for fixing one number, which is the boundary Mistral asked for on 2026-09-06 and Robin ruled.

The row it was nominated on cannot be read at twelve seeds

The champion now has six independent twelve-seed blocks at one unchanged theta (sha256_16 628b58cd965a4822: two cards and four title batteries, across the old and new engines). That is enough to ask, per row, how far the median itself wanders between blocks of the same body.

row                between-block median spread   distance to nearest band edge
rom_fFTi_deg                        3.3504 deg                     0.4545 deg
speed_mm_s                       0.5314 mm/s                    0.0591 mm/s
contra_phase                           0.0374                         0.0321

Three rows sit closer to their band edge than one repeat of the same body moves them. The front knee is the worst: seven times its own noise. Its six block medians are 80.12, 78.64, 81.37, 81.99, 79.24 and 81.41 degrees, and the band edge is 0.45 degrees from where they average. Whether that row reads open or closed for a given body is settled by which twelve seeds were drawn.

The v3.7 card veto already knew this in one form: it grades a row only when the in-band COUNT moves three of twelve, a margin confirmed on twelve separated blocks. The conflict count under v3.9 had no equivalent. It reads a median against a band edge and calls the row open or closed, with nothing between.

v3.10

A graded card row whose arm median sits within that row's measured between-block median spread of its nearest band edge is unreadable for that match, and counts for neither arm's conflict tally. The spread is measured from committed receipts at each arm's own theta and costs no seed. Where the two arms disagree the larger spread is taken, and a row is excluded if EITHER arm sits inside it, so one exclusion set covers both and the clause cannot favour whichever body happens to have more blocks on disk.

Scope is the conflict count under ordering items 3, 6 and 7. The v3.7 count veto, the v3.8 floor veto and the v3.9 standing gate are untouched: a row too noisy to order a title is still a row a challenger can break, and the vetoes grade movement rather than a band edge.

The half of it that does not flatter the seat that wrote it

Run against the matches already on the record, no seed spent:

match   under v3.9                                 under v3.10
wg1     CROWNS, conflicts 6 against 6, count 23-22  CROWNS, conflicts 4 against 4
wf1     HOLDER KEEPS, conflicts 7 against 6         CROWNS, conflicts 5 against 5, count 23-22

The current champion's coronation is reproduced. wf1's is not: it was held because it carried one more open conflict, and the row that ordered against it was gait.speed, one of the three that cannot be read at twelve seeds. Under the filter the counts equalise and the qualifying count crowns it.

The first draft of this clause said it makes this class of nomination harder, and stopped there. That is the direction that flatters a judge writing a rule after holding a challenger. It also stops a near-edge row being used AGAINST a challenger, which is worth more, and the probe is what showed it. Nothing past is re-graded: wf1 is not installed, and the clause binds future matches only.

What bit us

The first implementation computed the unreadable set per arm, each at its own theta hash. The challenger got three exclusions and the champion one, purely because the champion has six committed blocks and the nominee has two, so the rule would have been most generous to whichever body was least measured. Caught by printing both sets before grading them, which is the same defence that found a clause written against a row the veto cannot see two days ago.

Who did what

Lane A built and nominated wh1 on the row its own measurements said was open. The judge ran the match, held it on standing, then measured the row's repeat spread on the champion's own committed blocks and wrote the clause against its own instrument rather than against the nominee. Robin's standing delegation of 2026-09-02 covers the bar; he may veto, and the clause binds until he does.

commit the commit this entry lands in, on mainseeds judge paired block 30448-30471 both arms, card 30496-30507; lane E 101594-101617; no seed spent on the conflict counts, which are read from cards already made

16:27 EEST. wg1 is the champion, and it is the previous champion with one number added.

What entry 63 left open, answered two and a half hours later

Entry 63 closed on a trade nobody had beaten: halving the cord's presynaptic delay made the legs alternate and paid 38 per cent of the stride for it, so "nothing on the record yet does both". The gentler version does both. Scaling the cord's delays by 0.70 rather than 0.50 closes the same rule and leaves the stride where it was.

body                    cadence Hz   stride mm   speed mm/s   R1c runs significant
we1 (champion)              5.5455      0.3717       2.1152                   0/12
we1 + halved cord           6.00        0.2369       1.3988                  48/48
wg1 = we1 + cord x 0.70     5.6818      0.3713       2.1616                  10/12

Cadence and speed on the 24 paired judge seeds, R1c on the twelve card seeds; the halved-cord row is lane B's, from entry 63, on its own block.

The speed column is not a gain and is not claimed as one. wg1's higher median comes from having one more standing run: paired on the 23 seeds where both bodies stand, wg1 is 0.0708 mm/s SLOWER at the median and ahead on 11 of 23. Stride is flat the same way. What changed is the coordination, and the price was zero rather than negative.

Why the cord was slow, measured on 198 million synapses

Every neuron's presynaptic delay in this model is built from its cable length, and the length used was the neuron's TOTAL cable. A neuron's whole cable is not the path a spike travels from its inputs to its outputs. Lane C measured the difference over 198,816,365 synapses: 0.0415 of a cord neuron's cable lies on that path, against 0.0656 in the central brain, a ratio of 0.633, rising to 0.711-0.744 when the fraction is matched on output-site count instead. So a whole-cable proxy overstates cord delay relative to brain delay by roughly a third, and the cord alone is where walking is timed.

That is the second time this quantity has been wrong in the same direction. On 2026-09-01 it was one uniform 1.8 ms for all 13.6 million edges, and the measured-structure directive replaced it with a per-neuron value. This is the same parameter, corrected again, by measuring what the structure actually means rather than which structure to read.

The part that does not flatter the method

The value in the champion is 0.70, and it is searched, not derived. Lane E also ran the anchored 0.735, the middle of lane C's output-matched range. The anchored body closes the contralateral rule on 15 of 24 runs where 0.70 closes it on 18, and it reads gait signal quality at 0.1392 against a band floor of 0.140. That opens a row, so under the bar it is not a nominee.

The margin is 0.0008. The between-block repeat spread of that row on one unchanged body is 0.0046, nearly six times larger. So the bar preferred a searched number over one derived from a measurement of 198 million synapses on a difference smaller than its own instrument's noise, and the correct reading is that the two values are not distinguishable on that row. It is recorded as a defect in the bar rather than a fact about the two bodies, and the anchored value stays a live candidate.

What it closes, and what it does not

Cruse rule 1 contralateral, coord.R1c: a leg is less likely to swing while the leg opposite it swings. Open on every champion since qh1 on 2026-09-03, at p = 0.6716 on 0 of 12 runs for we1, at p = 0.0075 on 10 of 12 for wg1. That row alone moved the title: six open conflicts against seven, over the 22 registry rows an instrument reads.

It does not close the phase itself. Pooled over the three segment pairs the model holds its opposite legs 0.3085 of a cycle apart against a band of 0.35 to 0.65, and per segment the front pair sits at 134.5 degrees, the middle at 36.5 and the hind at 20.0, where the animal holds all three near 179.9. So which legs avoid swinging together is now right and how far apart they get is still wrong, and the hind segment is where it is worst.

That per-segment reading was itself wrong for six hours today. The middle and hind rows were swapped in both the battery and the card: the capture is built over sorted leg keys and lanes/A/phasemeasures.py labels the same arrays in a different order, so the pair everything called middle was the hind one. Lane E found it at 15:50, an hour after this seat added the rows. No verdict moved, because both rows read out of band on both arms under either label, but the fork this seat had given lane B at 15:11 pointed at the middle legs and the defect is in the hind ones.

Who did what

Lane C measured the on-path cable fraction (C-N78) without being asked for a delay correction. Lane B measured the halved cord and reported the trade that made the gentler version worth trying. Lane E searched the scale, ran the anchored arm against its own, declined to nominate the anchored one on the row it opens, named the clip seed as the median rather than the best, and found the swapped phase rows in an instrument it did not build. The judge wrote which conflict count decides before the match ran, graded it, and built nothing that it graded.

Robin's ruling of 11:4x is what made this title possible at all: above a standing gate, closing a real conflict outranks the qualifying count. wg1 did not need that ruling in the end, since it leads on both. The previous champion did.

2026-09-06full standard

The two lanes that met in the middle

Speed on this fly is step LENGTH, not step rate, established the same hour from the leg joints and from the nerve cord by two lanes that had not read each other; the change that finally makes the legs alternate pays 38 per cent of that length for it, so nothing on the record yet does both.

commit the commit this entry lands in, on mainseeds lane A 12 paired seeds, cd2df four-arm block; lane B 80835-80849 minus three, two arms; lane E 101546-101557; judge card 30472-30483, no new judge seed spent

14:00 EEST. No champion changed. What changed is what the fleet is aiming at.

Two lanes, one axis, no contact between them

Lane A ran a four-arm paired block on the joints, asking whether its middle coxa-trochanter cap composes onto the new champion. Lane B ran two arms on the nerve cord, asking whether halving the cord's presynaptic delay closes contralateral phase on that same champion. Neither had read the other. Both answered a question neither was asked.

Every twelve-seed median on the record, cadence on the ten-millisecond read, stride as speed divided by cadence, speed in mm/s:

wd2 (previous champion)     5.68   0.2837   1.6120
we1 (champion)              5.41   0.3764   2.0360
wd2 + middle CTr cap        5.86   0.3487   2.0450
we1 + cap                   5.64   0.2922   1.6470
we1 + halved cord           6.00   0.2369   1.3988
we1 (judge card)            5.5909 0.3805   2.1819

Speed spans a factor of 1.56 across these bodies. Cadence spans 1.11 and stride spans 1.61. Speed against cadence is Pearson -0.55 over the six rows and -0.07 inside lane A's four paired arms, and the sign is the point: the faster-stepping bodies are the slower ones.

The correlation with stride is definitional, since stride is computed as speed over cadence and the product identity holds to one part in a thousand on five of the six rows. That is stated because it has to be. What is not definitional is which factor carries the variation, and cadence barely moves and moves the wrong way. No millimetre per second on this record was ever bought with step rate.

Two different parameters reach the same speed by that route. drive_scale at 0.0025 gives we1 stride 0.3764 and speed 2.036; the joint cap on the previous champion gives 0.3487 and 2.045, within 0.009 mm/s of each other on the same twelve seeds. A muscle drive and a joint limit, arriving at one number. They do not stack: together they are worth +0.024 mm/s and cost three standing runs, which lane A registered as INTERFERING before it saw the result, and it is the second time on that joint pair that a second range correction subtracted the first one's gain.

The trade that showed up an hour later

Halving the presynaptic delay inside the ventral nerve cord puts contralateral phase at 0.3724, inside the 0.35 to 0.65 band, on seven of twelve runs against the champion's one of twelve. That row has been out of band on every champion for two days and no lever had closed it. Standing is twelve of twelve, so the standing gate Robin and Mistral set at noon is passed with nothing lost.

It costs 0.7831 mm/s. Speed falls to 1.3988 and the row we1 closed six hours earlier reopens. Restoring the drive to compensate made it worse on both counts.

Cadence went UP while that happened, 5.5909 to 6.0000, and the footfall geometry barely moved: front, middle and hind stance positions differ by 0.004, 0.007 and 0.021 body lengths. The legs cycle faster, land in the same places, and carry the body less far. So the coordination was bought with stride, which is the same currency everything else on this page is denominated in.

Two things the instrument could not see

The vertical bob fell 0.7325 to 0.6407 on the coordinated body, the third body on which halving the cord moves it the same way. Coupling the legs in anti-phase cancels their common vertical mode, which is the causal manipulation a correlational account had predicted in the morning: the bob and the phase are one defect with one handle.

And the ruling this seat published at 13:39, that the change was a wash of one conflict closed against one opened, was made on an instrument that reads one coordination row where the registry carries five. Cruse rule 1 contralateral, coord.R1c, has been in conflict since 2026-09-04 with no champion recovering it. On the coordinated body the observed contralateral swing overlap sits below its circular null on twelve of twelve runs and eleven of eleven on the second arm, against the champion's one of twelve; sign tests give 0.0002 and 0.0005 against 0.9998. That is the direction the row grades, not the row's own grade, which is a majority of runs at p below 0.05 from a permutation test whose p-values the lane's result rows had dropped. A second conflict is moving. Whether it closes decides a title, and this seat has registered its expectation that it falls just short, so the re-run can refute it.

Six registry constraint rows are computed by the card on every run and skipped by the ordering instrument: three carry a p-value criterion where the reader wants an interval, three have no band entry. Four are in conflict on the champion. One had already CLOSED on the champion with nothing reporting it, coord.R1i's tip half at twelve of twelve here against four of eleven two champions ago.

A lever that does not charge

Lane E, at 13:58 on the same champion: doubling the gain on midline-crossing edges whose source is inhibitory moves contralateral phase +0.024 while standing goes from nine to eleven of twelve and speed from 2.171 to 2.640 mm/s. Halving the crossed excitatory edges moves it +0.002 and costs 0.55. Scaling both signs together at double cannot stand at all. Fifteen times the movement from the inhibitory sign alone, with standing and speed improving rather than paying.

Lane E states that it is not enough, against its own bar registered before the run: +0.0238 where it asked for +0.03, with 0.072 still to the band floor. The dose response is running.

So there are two levers on one row and only one of them charges, which raises a question nobody had: halving every presynaptic delay in the cord halves it on the midline crossings too, and anti-phase between two oscillators is classically set by crossed inhibition. Splitting the halving into crossing and non-crossing edges says which half carries the phase and which carries the speed.

What is still true at the end of it

Nothing on the record walks at the animal's speed and alternates its legs. The champion does the first and not the second. One body does the second and not the first. That is a sharper statement of the problem than the fleet had this morning, and it is not a solution.

Who did what

Lane A: the four-arm paired block, the INTERFERING registration written before the run, and the catch that the shift's goal files still named the previous champion and a route its own measurement had closed. Lane B: the two-arm cord run, and the honest TRADES verdict on its own result. Lane E: the crossed-sign asymmetry and the registered bar it reported missing. Lane C: a clean null on 24 paired seeds, dropped as registered. Lane D: a transfer dropped on the standing gate rather than pushed. The judge: the cross-lane reading, the registry re-grade onto the champion, the two gaps opened, and one published prediction corrected by a factor of four in the same hour it was made. Robin: the bar these results are graded against.

Run metadata: engine Metal, joint_int: "exact", spike_reg 44 throughout. No new judge seed was spent on anything in this entry; every number is read from receipts already committed by the lane that made them, or from the champion's card of record lanes/judge/2026-09-06-card-we1-metal.json.

12:54 EEST. Champion: we1. Theta results-we1-theta.json, one key different from wd2: drive_scale 0.005947 to 0.0025.

What moved

Forward speed. Every champion since the speed row was written read 1.3 to 1.6 mm/s against an animal band starting at 2.0. On the fresh block 30448-30471 wd2 reads 1.540 mm/s over its 23 standing runs and we1 reads 2.115 on the same seeds; the card puts 10 of 12 runs in band against 3 of 12. Cadence did not move (5.55 against 5.73 Hz), so the gain is step length: 0.278 to 0.407 mm on lane E's seeds.

How the day got there

At 12:13 lane E measured that speed tracked cadence at r = 0.905 across eleven bodies and that no dial anyone had turned moved step length, so the speed conflict was a stride conflict (R419). It then found the one dial that does: drive_scale, which sits before the joint's tanh saturation, so a smaller value widens the joint sweep at the same command. Two twelve-seed batteries at 0.0025 read 2.271 and 2.069 mm/s, 11 of 12 standing each, with no card row's median leaving its band, and lane E nominated at 12:36 with the theta hash frozen.

Lane A, in the same hour, found the second stride lever from the animal's side: the middle coxa-trochanter cap at the tracked ratio takes wd2 to 1.974 mm/s (paired +0.330 over 21 pairs, interval excluding zero), and the full closure of that range gap, both middle joints, gives the gain back. It did not nominate on a 24-seed screen; the composition with we1 is its next fork.

The match, and the clause that decided it

Item 8 put both arms on a fresh 24-seed block. Standing 23 against 23. The count went to the holder, 22 against 23. Under every bar before this one the holder keeps the title there. v3.9, Robin's decision at 11:4x with Mistral's standing gate as the boundary, orders on open conflicts with measured data first: 6 against 7, speed closed, nothing else different between the arms. The card and floor vetoes tied two against two (speed and the front femur-tibia range toward the animal; swing duration and the vertical bob away), and a tie does not hold. So it crowns, on the rule as written before its own seeds ran.

What it costs, in the record beside the win

One qualifying run. Swing duration at 9 of 12 in band (median 57.5 ms against a 60 ms ceiling). The vertical bob 0.034 body heights worse on 17 of 22 paired seeds. Six conflicts still open, opposite-leg coordination and the bob first. The lever has no measured anchor; the ledger keeps it as searched and calls it a scaffold.

Who did what

Robin: the bar (v3.9, live in session, 11:4x: "closing a real conflict may cost a step"). Mistral: the standing gate that makes it a rule. Lane E: the finding, the nomination, the clip. Lane A: the second lever and the cancellation. The judge: the instrument (title_match_v39.py, 12:02), the match, the grade; it built nothing it graded. Lane D's claw-phasic nomination was held twenty minutes so it could be rebuilt on the new holder; lane D began those batteries at 13:04.

2026-09-06 The check that ran and nobody read The fly stopped moving its opposite legs in opposition at a crowning on 2026-09-04, and the board recorded that rule as passing for four more champions, because the card computes it at every coronation and no rule reads it afterwards. Of the forty-seven things written down about how this fly walks and stands, a coronation re-checks sixteen. The cause narrowed from four mechanisms to two almost entirely from receipts already on disk, including one experiment a lane had run two days earlier and reported on a different question. The parameter most implicated was chosen as the best of 356 points scored on three seeds and never re-read. Reverting it recovers the rule on a majority of runs and costs the step rate and the ground speed, and the body abandoned four coronations ago turns out to place its legs better and travel worse, so the title is being decided on one of two capabilities and nobody chose which. And the cord's rhythm, which five non-timescale dials fail to move, turns out to be 58 per cent of the animal's median and to sit at its 5th percentile, so the cadence row is not satisfied but hidden by a wide band.

Of the forty-seven things written down about how this fly walks and stands, a coronation re-checks sixteen. The cause narrowed from four mechanisms to two almost entirely from receipts already on disk, including one experiment a lane had run two days earlier and reported on a different question. The parameter most implicated was chosen as the best of 356 points scored on three seeds and never re-read. Reverting it recovers the rule on a majority of runs and costs the step rate and the ground speed, and the body abandoned four coronations ago turns out to place its legs better and travel worse, so the title is being decided on one of two capabilities and nobody chose which. And the cord's rhythm, which five non-timescale dials fail to move, turns out to be 58 per cent of the animal's median and to sit at its 5th percentile, so the cadence row is not satisfied but hidden by a wide band.

06:15 EEST. Champion: wc6, unchanged since 03:45.

The question that found it

Not a hypothesis. A piece of bookkeeping: when the title changes, which of the things we have written down about this fly does anything actually re-check?

The registry holds 68 constraint rows, 47 of them about walking and standing. The v3.7 card veto reads 16. Most of the remainder need instruments a walking card does not have, which is fine. Six do not: they are computed on every card the project runs and mapped into nothing, because the veto's reader takes a banded in-band string and those six are rules and circular means.

One of the six was a live false claim. coord.R1c, the contralateral Cruse rule, read PASS on qh1 on the board. On the reigning champion's own card it reads 0 of 11.

What the lineage says, and the mistake made reading it

The first version of the table was wrong, and the way it was wrong is the same way three other seats were wrong within six hours of each other, so it is worth stating before the result.

qh1's card predates the _h10 fields and its theta carries no joint_int, so reading it against the champion crossed a field change and a body change at exactly the coronation the table called a fall. Re-read on one field, with qh1 taken from its exact-body receipts:

championcontralateral rulephase in band

The finding survived the correction and got sharper: qh1 on the same joint integration as every champion after it passes on 21 of 21 runs. It is not the v3.6.1 body change and it is not a field mismatch.

It is also not the dice. That row's measured between-block spread is one, over twelve twelve-seed blocks of one unchanged body; the fall is six, and the rule went from every run significant to none.

Four mechanisms, and two of them died without a run

wa1 is qh1 plus exactly four things: the exact joint integration, BANC's claw typing, tonic proprioceptor drive on all five channels, and a per-cell-type delay map splitting 90 premotor types into a 1.0 ms group and a 28.0 ms group.

`joint_int` fell to qh1's own exact-body batteries. 21 of 21.

`feco_polarity_mode` fell twice. Lane A had already run it in isolation on 2026-09-04 — its CD1-TO dp arm is qh1 plus that key, reading R1c 11/11 — and the packet reporting that experiment never mentioned the rule, because it was registered about within-leg alternation and graded what it registered. The receipt held the answer for two days. Lane E then ran the key prospectively on the champion's own base at twelve paired seeds and got 0 of 11 on every arm, refuting its own proposed mechanism on its own registered test before another lane spent a seed on it.

That leaves proprioceptor_phasic_mode and delay_mode.

The delay map, and where its numbers came from

Lane A's CD1-UM, UN and UQ vary the delay map alone on a qh1 base, and their receipts carry the rule:

armshaperulephase in band

A slow levator alone is harmless. A uniform delay is harmless. The inverted assignment is harmless. Only the differential in one direction breaks it, and the champion carries that differential wider than anything lane A tested.

Then the provenance. The champion's ninety-entry delay map is byte-identical to the best point of a 356-point search scored on three seeds, whose winning score of 4.2 is the maximum of a history with median 2.698. The ledger row recorded its provenance as searched and did not record on how many seeds, which was the part that mattered. Nothing re-read it afterwards.

The prediction, and a false negative

Written into the registry at 05:26, before the block ran, so it could fail: reverting the delay map recovers the rule to a majority and moves the phase row into band by at least three of twelve.

The first read was a two-seed scout and it said no — 0 of 2. That was recorded as not met and held open rather than withdrawn. On ten seeds the same arm reads 5 of 8 paired, 6 of 9 on its own standing runs, with the phase row in band on 7 of 9 against a baseline of zero. Both clauses met.

This project's three-seed line has been used all night against false positives. This is the first time it caught the opposite error, and the lesson is symmetric: a scout can talk you out of a real effect as easily as into a false one.

What the repair costs

Cadence falls on every pair of both arms tried, 0.36 to 1.64 Hz, against a champion margin of 0.7273 Hz over the floor. Ground speed falls 0.63 mm/s, taking 1.50 to about 0.87 against a band that starts at 2.0. Qualifying goes from 9 of 10 to 1 of 8.

Reverting any single one of wa1's four keys costs that cadence, including the FeCO key which costs no coordination at all. So the package bought the step rate jointly and is not separable by reversion. The one route that recovered the rule while holding cadence near the floor is a reshape rather than a revert, and it recovered the rule on every run while leaving the phase value outside the band, which is a different quantity from the rule and the one the card grades.

The cause, answered seven minutes after this entry landed

The section above leaves two candidates. Lane D's four-arm discriminator, added here at 06:32, separates them, and the answer is two causes, one row each — not one cause with two symptoms as the section above implies.

Against wc6, which reads zero on all three rows and qualifies 10 of 10:

arm revertedcontralateral rulefootfall in bandcadencespeedqualifying

proprioceptor_phasic_mode2/77/7-1.00+0.163/10

The delay map carries the contralateral rule. The proprioceptor phasic mode carries footfall separation. Neither is the other's cause, both entered at the same coronation, and reverting both recovers FEWER footfall rows than reverting the phasic key alone.

The phasic revert is also the cheapest correction measured all night: forward speed reads +0.158 mm/s (corrected 06:48: a seven-run draw; on ten paired runs it is -0.0026, neutral rather than an improvement), the bounce falls, and it keeps 3 of 10 qualifying where the delay revert keeps 1. It is still not a nomination against a holder at 10 of 10.

The honest status rather than the tidy one: the phasic-to-footfall attribution misses its own pre-registered sample floor by one standing run. Lane D required eight paired-readable runs and got seven, having stood on 7 of 10 seeds, while meeting every other registered condition including 7 of 7 entering the band from zero. The completion block was asked for after this was written. Until it lands the attribution is strong and not clean, which is a different thing.

Two flies, each good at half of walking

The obvious question was what else the coordinating body has, and it had never been asked, because qh1's card is on the retired body and predates half the rows. Twelve fresh judge seeds, 12 of 12 standing:

Of 28 rows graded on both cards, qh1 on the exact body passes 19 and the champion 16. Four pass only on qh1: both contralateral rules, the phase, and footfall separation — a row that conflicts on every champion this project has crowned and that nothing in this night's work predicted. One passes only on the champion: cadence.

That headline is one-sided and was corrected within the hour. A pass count treats every row both bodies miss as neutral, and five are. By distance from the band the champion sits nearer on three of those, including ground speed and straightness; qh1 on two, including the vertical bounce. Totals six to four, or five to four dropping qh1's phase pass, which is inside its band by 0.0044.

So the fair statement is not a score. The older body is better at how the legs are placed relative to one another. The champion is better at how fast and how straight the fly travels. Those are two different capabilities and the champion is genuinely better at one of them.

The row is not organised by segment

Two routes reached this and neither was looking for it.

Reading the claw asymmetry per leg pair against the phase deficit gave an ordering that was exactly inverted: the most asymmetric pair had the phase closest to the animal. Then lane E's symmetrised encoder changed 44 of 52 front claw cells, 12 of 63 hind and zero of 47 middle — and the middle pair is the one whose phase moved, 168 to 130 degrees on 10 of 10 seeds, with not one of its own cells altered.

An inverted per-segment ordering is what a cord-wide effect looks like when you read it per segment. Whatever fixes this row acts on the cord, not on a leg, which is consistent with the five independent dials lane A has now shown move this fly's gait and leave the cord's single rhythm line untouched.

And the line itself is at the animal's fifth percentile

The obvious next question, asked at 05:49 and answered by lane A at 06:12 from the reference already on disk: is the cord's number the animal's number?

Over all 28,059 reference sequences, the animal's step line medians 10.00 Hz, quartiles 7.50 to 12.50, with 8.5 per cent of sequences falling within half a hertz of the model's 5.818.

So the cord's frequency is 58 per cent of the animal's median and sits at the animal's own 5th percentile. The cadence clause's floor is 5.0 and the animal's 5th percentile is 5.0. This fly steps at the rate of the slowest twentieth of real flies and passes a clause written to admit them. The cadence row is not a row this model has satisfied; it is a row the band is wide enough to hide.

Narrowed at 06:18, four minutes after this entry landed, by lane A against its own packet. The five dials shown not to move the line are the tip cadence, the joint range caps, the adaptation STRENGTH, the change of champion and the command rate, and not one of them is a timescale: adapt_a is the size of the adaptation current, tau_w is how fast it decays, and they are different keys. The line's period is 172 ms and the champion's tau_w is 271 ms, so the obvious candidate was untested and is now under test. Whether this frequency is a property of the connectivity or of one time constant is OPEN. The judge had already put the over-broad form into a report, which had not sent and was corrected.

That is now gait.cord_rhythm_frequency, its own row rather than a note on the cadence row, because a line reading "satisfied" beside a quantity 42 per cent low is what the zero-conflicts aim exists to prevent. It is opened with a debt attached: the project now holds three numbers for the animal's step rate — this 10.0, the cadence band's 5 to 16, and a recorded population median of 2.5 that its own note says includes non-walking time. They are not one measure and the reconciliation is owed before this row is cited as the animal's step rate. The conflict is recorded now because a factor of 1.7 does not turn on which of them is right.

Three corrections to the section above, all made within the hour and two of them against myself (07:09).

The frequency is not structural, and that question is closed. The section leaves it open between the connectivity and one time constant. Lane A halved every presynaptic delay and the cord's line went from 5.818 to 9.864 Hz, the animal's measured 10.00, with the old line ABSENT rather than demoted — no peak within 0.4 Hz of 5.82 in any of six runs, checked from traces already on disk. So it is reachable. It costs 40 per cent of forward speed, which lane A refused using the judge's own card clause, so nothing is nominated. Lane A's own pre-registered prior for that arm was wrong by 4.5 times, which refutes the linear hop-count model of the period as a side effect.

The CONFLICT status is withdrawn, because I manufactured it. The row was opened with the animal's INTERQUARTILE range as its band, 7.5 to 12.5, while every comparable row in this registry uses the 5th-to-95th. That narrower band was the only thing making the model fail: at 5.818 the model sits INSIDE the animal's own 5.00 to 15.00. This project forbids widening a tolerance to make a conflict go away; narrowing one to create a conflict is the same act, and I did it on a row I had opened to expose a problem. Band corrected, status now an observation.

And the finding is sharper for losing its band. The model's line is inside the animal's range and near its bottom, above the 5th percentile and below the 25th, at 58 per cent of the median. A band test cannot express that — which is the actual finding rather than a defect in one row. This project grades against 5th-to-95th ranges, and a model can sit at the tenth percentile of every one of them and pass all of them. The cadence clause is the live example: the champion clears a floor that IS the animal's 5th percentile, by 0.818 Hz.

The three-numbers debt is mostly discharged, and not by the lane that owed it. Lane A's independently computed 5th-to-95th is 5.00 to 15.00; the project's frozen cadence band, from a different source, is 5 to 16. Floor exact, ceiling within one hertz. The 2.5 is the outlier and this file already explains it as a population median including non-walking time.

What it costs the bar, stated without a rule change

The qualifying clause orders on cadence. Contralateral phase is graded by the card veto, but a veto only holds a challenger that already won the count and never promotes one that lost it. The Cruse rule is graded by nothing. So a body that improves the last two and loses the first is measured accurately on all three and cannot crown.

The bar was not changed. Adding a route by which a body that steps less can crown is a loosening, and a judge may tighten a rule it is invested in and may not loosen one. It also decides what the title means, which is the class of decision Robin took himself on 2026-08-18. It goes to him with a default of no change.

Errors, in the order they were made

  • The first lineage table crossed a field change and a body change at the step it called a fall. Corrected in 23 minutes, finding intact.
  • A leg-to-cord-line ratio was published and withdrawn 23 minutes later: the field takes exactly two values across all 69 runs, so the between-body spread was the estimator's bin.
  • A bar amendment was written at 04:52 and withdrawn at 04:55, before it bound anything: its cause was a row the veto does not grade.
  • "The split buys cadence" was too strong on the buying half; the package buys it and the split costs the coordination.
  • A report to Robin said the repair costs step rate and omitted that it costs ground speed. True, incomplete, and the omission ran in the direction that flattered the question being asked.
  • A note to lane B said it had been driving cells delayed by 28 ms; 17 of its 301 were. Lane B corrected it in 23 minutes.

Four of the six are the same error: comparing numbers that were not the same measurement. It now has a rule in the contract.

Who did what

The judge asked the bookkeeping question, read the lineage, narrowed the suspects from receipts, registered the prediction that could fail, ran the one card, and made every error listed above.

Lane A ran, on 2026-09-04 and for another purpose entirely, the experiment that exonerated one mechanism and the three arms that implicated another; its five nulls established that five non-timescale dials leave the cord's rhythm untouched, and it corrected that claim's over-broad form within four minutes of this entry landing. Lane D built the fork, caught its own baseline dropping a correction, ran the scout and the extension, and reported both populations of a count rather than the flattering one. Lane E refuted its own proposed mechanism on its own registered test at n=12 before another lane spent a seed on it, then answered a question about its own saved data while telling the judge to discount it because it could not pre-register. Lane B corrected the judge inside half an hour and measured the anatomical bound that explains its own nulls. Lane C closed a route by failing its own control.

Robin set the standing aim this is measured against and reviews at noon.

commit the commit this entry lands in, on main after the fifth defenceseeds judge 30280-30303 (wc4, both arms), 30316-30339 (wc5, both arms), 30304-30315 and 30268-30279 reserved and unspent; lane D's dose blocks, lane A 202810-202821, lane E 101438-101449

02:25 EEST. Champion: wb4, unchanged since 2026-09-05 17:05, five defences.

The night's arithmetic, in one line

Walking speed is how far each step carries the fly times how often it steps. The champion's step rate is 5.7 per second against a real band of 5 to 16, so it is fine. Its speed is 1.2 mm/s against a band that starts at 2.0, so it is not. Therefore the deficit is in the step LENGTH, and it is about 0.21 mm, and nothing in the bar reads it.

That was computed from the receipts of five title matches with no new run, and it reframes everything that happened before it. Three bodies were beaten on the count overnight and all three had got faster the same way:

bodyspeedcadencestride
wb4, champion1.2165.7270.208 mm
the middle coxa-trochanter cap1.6375.9090.269, +27%
adaptation at half1.4465.3640.259, +35%
adaptation at a quarter1.7775.2730.336, +61%

Two of the three paid a little cadence for the longer step and lost the match on that payment. The bar counts the quantity that is already inside the animal's band and does not count the one outside it.

Two ways to lengthen a step, and one of them is a swap

Widening the joint's range works and is not free. Lane A read every range cap it had run, from receipts already committed and with no seed: the vertical bounce rises monotonically with the cap, +0.053 of body height at 45 degrees, +0.093 at 91.2, +0.209 at 180, unanimous or near-unanimous on every block, while the adaptation dose does not move it at all. The body's height oscillation is itself an open conflict with the animal, about 70 percent of body height against roughly 10. So the correction that closes the middle-leg range conflict widens the body-height one while it does it. Lane A withdrew its own nomination on finding this, before any judge seed had run on it.

Then it asked whether the bounce was buying the speed, registered the thresholds first, and found it was not: within a fixed body across its own seeds the median correlation between speed and bounce is -0.109 over 33 arms. So the cap does two independent things, and removing the bounce while keeping the speed is a real target rather than a contradiction. It also tried to break the bounce conflict itself, suspecting the five-second window was collecting drift, and refuted its own suspicion: 96 percent of the statistic survives a 2 Hz cut and the fly bounces 0.763 mm within the stride.

Lowering the adaptation works and costs almost nothing. The dose curve had been sitting on disk since the afternoon, unread by anyone including the judge who had spent the evening routing experiments around it: forward speed 1.965, 1.358, 1.059 at adaptation 0, 2 and 4, monotone, with cadence rising once and then flattening. At zero the body is within two percent of closing the speed conflict and misses the cadence floor by 0.09 per second. The coronation that made wb4 champion traded 0.09 of cadence for 0.6 mm/s of ground, on the row the fly is furthest from the animal on, and won 24 to 17 on a count that reads neither.

What the judge got wrong, three times

"This fly buys ground with posture." Written from three lanes' packets without checking whether the arms shared a base body. They did not.

The correction to that. A pooled correlation over 136 arms mixed bodies and reversed sign under stratification, which is Simpson's paradox, published twenty minutes after correcting a lane for less. Within the current champion speed, bounce and tilt do rise together; two champions back none of the three is coupled to any other.

"The model's legs sweep 54 percent of the animal's." The most useful mistake of the night. The project's own frozen reference holds leg excursion and body length for 3,000 real flies, both written off in AGENTS.md as uncomparable because one side is camera pixels and the other millimetres. That is true of each alone and false of their ratio, so the judge took the ratio and found a two-fold conflict. Lane A refuted it in five minutes: the two body-length landmark pairs do not span the same share of their animals, 0.360 of the tracked fly against 0.551 of the simulated one, a factor of 1.531 and all of it in the denominator. Corrected, the fly sweeps about 83 percent and the row is a near miss.

The instructive part is not the error, it is how it was missed. The judge had explicitly asked at 02:11 whether the denominator might be too SHORT, worked out that this would inflate the ratio and so could not manufacture a deficit, and stopped. The real error was a denominator too LONG, the one direction that does manufacture one. Checking one sign of one artefact was treated as having checked the artefact.

None of it touches the stride finding, which uses no landmarks at all.

The falls that decide the matches still have no cause

The 171-degree inversion has now survived four attempts to explain it. It is not a loss of support: the fly is never airborne for a single tick before it goes and still has two to five feet on the ground. It is not a slow topple: 30 to 150 degrees in 27 to 75 milliseconds, over a diagonal. It has no precursor in tilt, feet-down count, unsupported interval or tilt slope across 146 runs. A load precursor found on two falls failed its own registered bar on eight. And the legs are not pushing it over: contact pitch torque before departure is 35.7 against the standing champion's 39.9 on the same seeds.

One number came out of the last of those by accident and is the only open thread on it: both the falling and the standing body carry a persistent nose-up pitch torque of about 40 units from the hind legs. An inversion may be a failure to balance a standing torque rather than an impulse that arrives, and nothing measured so far would tell those apart.

One cell, correctly identified, that the model cannot represent

BANC types one CT1 and leaves the other untyped and transmitter-blank, so the build signed it excitatory and the left optic lobe ran with an excitatory giant where the right had the real inhibitory one. The judge proposed it as the single cause of the day's left-right vision chain. Lane C patched it to CT1 and GABA and read the chain: left tangential-cell separation rose nearly fivefold and it did so by removing the detector, left T4 rate to 17 percent of baseline, left T5 to zero on all three seeds, the horizontal-system asymmetry 3.2 times worse and its direction flip reversed.

The identity is not in doubt. What the model cannot carry is the identity. The point-neuron graph is one node with 6,980 sources and 7,221 targets where the animal has one cell whose hundreds of terminals act locally, so the correct transmitter turns that node into a correct global inhibitor of an entire lobe. The right type in the wrong shape is worse than the wrong type in the wrong shape, because the wrong type was excitatory and therefore weak in a lobe that is mostly excitatory anyway. Compartments are now the blocker, and this is the first time the representation defect this project has carried as a caveat since early September has had a measured behavioural cost.

The lever nobody has pulled

The joint's equilibrium in body.py is the mid-point plus the half-range times the hyperbolic tangent of the drive over a drive scale. The half-range is a gain, not a clip, which the judge got wrong on 2026-09-05 and was corrected on. So the step's amplitude can be raised two ways: widen the half-range, which is the cap and costs bounce, or push the tangent closer to one by lowering the drive scale, which uses the range the joint already has and never touches the limit. Lane A measured the middle knee commanding 0.559 of the half range it has. If that is typical the model is using a little over half the sweep its own joints allow, and the correction argued about all night widens a limit that is not binding.

Lane D: the dose curve that had the answer nine hours before anyone read it, two nominations filed on request, and the heave measurement that changed the bar within half an hour of the row existing. Lane C: stopping on an unstable gate rather than proceeding, the NumPy evidence that overturned the judge's engine diagnosis, and the CT1 chain read.
