Addendum, 2026-09-06 03:45 EEST: the first title decided on a conflict rather than a count

Champion: wc6, crowned 03:45 under bar v3.8, ordering items 5 and 6. Tag wc6. Nominated by lane E at 03:17, hash claimed and verified. Seeds 30340-30387 for the match and its extension, 30388-30399 for the card. Receipt lanes/judge/2026-09-06-title-v38-wc6-coronation.json.

What happened

wc6 is the previous champion plus three labelled biology corrections and not one searched dial: the campaniform channel fed the leg's matched ground load, a six-cell remotor transfer in the second thoracic segment, and one transmitter map. Four keys, all additions.

It tied wb4 23-23 on twenty-four fresh seeds. The tie-break drew twenty-four more and both arms ran again: 23-23. Over all forty-eight paired seeds, 46 each, with one discordant seed either way in each half.

Dead level. So the bar asks its next question, which it has never had to ask before: which of the two carries fewer unresolved conflicts with measured data? wc6 carries one fewer. Its campaniform sensors are fed the leg's actual load. Every champion before it fed them muscle activation, a stand-in adopted in August when the model had no ground, and kept for a month after the body closed and gave it ground. A campaniform sensillum reports cuticular strain under load; it does not report what a muscle is doing.

The card veto was then read, as the clause requires on every route to a coronation, and returned nothing either way: no row moved three of twelve in either direction, and the floor rule found no change on either row that is out of band for both flies.

Two things decided before the numbers, which is the only reason this counts

At 03:20 the block rule changed. Three holder records existed by then, at 24, 23 and 22 of 24 on three different blocks, and reusing one was the judge's choice. In a match decided by one or two seeds, and three of the night's five were, that choice is the margin. So each nomination now runs both arms on a new block, at a cost of twenty-four extra runs, and the discretion is gone. It was written before this match's first seed.

At 03:21 the tie-break standing was fixed. The judge determined that wc6 closes the campaniform gap and wb4 does not, read from the theta with no run, against a gap registered sixteen hours earlier. That determination was made before any count from this match existed. Had it come afterwards, with the numbers visible, this coronation would be worth nothing, and the judge had already declined five clause changes tonight for exactly that reason.

What it is not, said as plainly as what it is

It does not walk better. Forward speed 1.50 mm/s against a real band that starts at 2.0. Vertical bounce 0.71 of its own body height against about 0.10. Contralateral phase 0.266 against a band from 0.35. Every one of those is inherited from wb4 at the same magnitude. On the bar's own counting quantity it is exactly as good as the fly it replaced, and not one step better.

It won because it stopped pretending one of its senses was something else.

The night around it

Five defences held before this one fell, three of them against flies that walked measurably faster and lost on the step count. The judge published five corrections to its own claims and had three hypotheses refuted by lanes, twice within five minutes. Lane E's diagnostic under this nomination found that reverting any of six dials rescues all four of a body's falls, so no dial causes them; the fly sits at a point in dial space that any axis leaves. Lane B drove a premotor hemilineage and turned the body for the first time, then moved the contralateral phase toward the animal for the first time, with a confound in the phase measure the judge raised and neither has yet closed.

Attribution, this addendum

Lane E: the nomination, the corrections-only body its goal asked for, and the rescue diagnostic under it. Lane A: four registered self-audits in one hour, including one that verified a judge note it had been repeating on the judge's authority, and one that refuted its own post-hoc. Lane B: the turn, the phase movement, and a steering test reported as failed when a looser reading was available. Lane D: the withdrawal of its own lead on its own rule with the medians in its favour. The judge: two rule decisions taken before the numbers that made the result mean something, five corrections to its own claims, and a coronation it did not expect when the match began.

Correction, 2026-09-06 04:30: "it does not walk better" was wrong

The addendum above says, twice and at length, that wc6 does not walk better than the fly it replaced. That is withdrawn. It was written from the qualifying counts, which tied at 46 of 48, and a qualifying count is the bar's counting quantity rather than a measure of walking.

Lane A re-based its whole bounce line onto the new champion within forty minutes of the coronation, raising the disagreement rule in its own first line because its goal file still named the old one. Paired over twelve reserved seeds with both arms standing and qualifying 12 of 12, it found forward speed +0.545 mm/s, up on ten of twelve, sign test p 0.039. Lane E's nomination evidence had given +0.51 on nineteen of twenty-three pairs, and the two cards read 1.5031 against 1.2523. Three independent reads, one of them paired and pre-registered.

So the correct sentence is: wc6 qualifies on exactly as many runs as the fly it replaced, and it walks measurably faster. On the largest conflict this project carries, the coronation moved the fly toward the animal by half a millimetre per second.

What genuinely did not move, and this half of the original claim stands: the vertical bounce is unchanged, paired at -0.0113 with its 5.841 Hz peak identical to the digit, and the contralateral phase is unchanged. Lane A's entire bounce line therefore transfers to the new champion without re-measurement, which is the result it set out to get.

The entry above is left as written, per the no-retroactive-polish rule. The judge wrote the wrong sentence four times in four places within ten minutes of the coronation, and it took a lane forty minutes and twelve seeds to find it.

commit the commit this entry lands in (main, after 40c7d7781)seeds judge 30244-30267 (item-8 match, both arms) and 30268-30279 (card, unread); lane E 101249-101329 (R374-R385); lane A 202654-202677; lane D 61183-61206; lane C 52594-52607

19:55 EEST. Champion: wb4, unchanged since 17:05; one defence this evening, 24 against 22 on fresh seeds under a new ordering item.

A question from Robin, and a count

At 17:55 Robin asked how sensory neurons that reach the middle of the network differ from the ones that go straight to motor neurons, whether the direct ones are stretch reflexes, and what the literature says. The answer went to him at 18:05 from a static count on BANC: of the 1.08 million synapses onto the 393 leg motor neurons, 3.4% come straight from leg sensory cells, 85% from cord interneurons and 7.7% from the brain; per class the direct share is 12% for the load sensors, 11% for the femur's movement-direction cells, 10% for the hair plates, 9.5% for the position cells, and under 1% for the vibration sensors and the touch bristles, which go up to the brain instead. The direct path is the fast fixed-sign resistance and load reflex; the interneuron layer is where the animal gates it by state. One sentence of that answer overstated the day's campaniform result and was corrected by an addendum an hour later.

The last paragraph of the answer proposed a measurement: read the model's own reflex sign per joint standing against walking, because a cord that never changes a reflex with state has no gating, which would be the same fact as its ignoring descending drive. Lane E took it as a fork within twenty minutes.

The null that was not one

Lane E's instrument (R376, registered before its seeds): +40 Hz for 200 ms on the 24 left-front claw cells that rise with the knee angle, delivered after the encoder so the cord alone answers, read as the change in the drive that raises that angle, averaged over 400 ms from onset, relative to the control's own drive. Three seeds walking with the command on read negative on 3 of 3, a resistance reflex. Three seeds with the command at zero read two negative and one positive.

The judge's first correction was to the arms, not the read: the command-at-zero arm was not standing. Its own controls walked at 0.98, 1.66 and 1.26 mm/s at about five steps a second, the free-running cord of the small hours now confirmed on wb4, so the contrast was command-on against command-off walking and no stationary state existed. Lane E's stillness sweep (R379) then found none by proprioceptive tone either: every scale from 0.2 to 0.6 still stepped 23 to 29 times in the window.

The counts then did what small counts do. R378 added six seeds per arm and the command-off arm read resistance on 8 of 9 while the command-on arm went to 4 against 5; R380 added nine more and both arms landed at 10 negative of 18, Fisher p = 1.0. At 19:45 the judge wrote the row up as a null with a meaning: on this instrument the cord's answer to one leg's false stretch has no stereotyped sign and is cord-wide on every pair, where the animal's knee reflex is local and fixed. The one hedge in that note was the right one and came too late to prevent the sentence: the response was one to four spike-equivalents on the perturbed joint, and the animal's reflex is read within tens of milliseconds, not over 400.

Lane E's R383 raised the stimulus to the encoder's own maximum, +120 Hz, and its registered 400 ms read stayed unread (4 of 9). What the runner had saved beside it did not: in the first 100 ms after onset the drive that raises the knee angle fell on 9 of 9 seeds by about the joint's own mean drive; over the 200 ms of the stimulus it fell on 9 of 9 by 0.5 to 1.5 of that drive; the knee angle itself fell 2 to 10 degrees on 9 of 9. The response is a pulse the length of the stimulus followed by a rebound, so a mean over twice its length reads noise. At +40 Hz the same early read is negative on 13 of 18 and 11 of 17 pairs: present, small. Latency 7.5 to 87.5 ms, quantised by whichever motor spike moves first.

R384, both command arms on fresh seeds with the read window equal to the stimulus window: resistance on 9 of 9 in both states. With the command on, the drive drops 1.13 times the joint's own drive and the knee falls 11.5 degrees; with it off, 0.76 and 8.4 degrees. Welch two-sided on the relative responses: t = 2.59, p = 0.021. The descending command modulates the reflex, and makes it stronger. In the animal the active state weakens or reverses the resistance reflex (Bassler's stick insect; presynaptic inhibition of the afferents in the locust). Two cautions keep that from being written as a conflict tonight: the command-off arm is a walking cord, not a resting animal, so the literature's rest-against-active contrast is not the one measured; and nine against nine at p = 0.02 is one registered read. The male arm (R385, MCNS frame, six seeds per arm) is running for the sign's two-animal tag.

Two rules come out of it. The read window equals the stimulus window, or the animal's latency band, never a multiple of it; a pulse averaged over twice its length is a null of the instrument. And the judge writes no null as a finding before the instrument's resolution has been stated against the animal's, which is the same lesson the three-seed counts taught twice this evening from the other side.

The first bundle, held

Two corrections measured neutral on their own seeds were carried together as one challenger, wc1: the campaniform channel driven by ground load in place of the muscle-activation stand-in (lane E, R374 to R377: the searched dials bought nothing, the drop-in stands 24 of 24, qualifies 22 against 24 on two cadence-floor flips and walks 0.31 mm/s faster on 17 of 24 pairs), and six middle-leg motor neurons that BANC labels femur reductor and both male reconstructions name pleural remotor, moved onto that muscle (lane A CD2-AB: the right middle leg's pitch hinge goes from 0.2 to 9.7 degrees at p 0.0002, standing 12 of 12, speed unchanged; kept and labelled TRANSFERRED under the 2026-09-04 rule and ported to main under the probe, bit-identical). The rotator remap that preceded it (CD2-AA) moved the roll hinge two degrees and speed by nothing, which refuted that lever on its own terms; lane A's phase read then put the middle legs' speed block in when the remotor pool fires, not what it pulls, and the hind legs' in the knee, extended in swing by a flexor pool that fires in stance.

wb4 qualifies 24 of 24 on its own paired seeds, so no challenger could be ordered above it there and a tie extends only on an exact equality. Ordering item 8 was written before any nomination existed: a holder at 24 of 24 is matched on the next 24 judge-block seeds, both arms. wb4 ran them at 18:57 and stood and qualified 24 of 24 again. wc1 ran them at 19:01 and read 22: one fall, one cadence-floor flip at 4.91 Hz, cadence median 5.73 against 5.64 Hz, speed 1.46 against 1.18 mm/s median, faster on 14 of 23 pairs. The holder keeps. The corrections stay labelled and on main; their route into the champion is a search with them on for the standing and cadence margin, twelve seeds per candidate, which lane E takes next with the LPi14 transmitter map added to the base after it read neutral on the walk (R382, 24 of 24).

The v3.7 card veto, written at the coronation, gained a clarification the same hour: it reads on every route to a coronation, ties included.

What else moved

The champion's abdomen sways sideways as much as a real fly's: 6.14 degrees median on twelve fresh seeds against the real 4.65 to 11.63, twelve of twelve inside, on the same window and reader as the 25,059 reference sequences lane D measured this afternoon. Registry row body.abdomen_lateral_excursion, satisfied, female-only. Lane D's audit of the abdomen's roll map found it signs each motor neuron by its soma side and carries a built-in lateral bias of a fifth of full range; the nerve-side map removes the bias, costs two standing seeds of twelve and straightens nothing, so it stays labelled and default off.

One transmitter sign, on one right LPi14 row that BANC verified acetylcholine against a GABA prediction, halves the HS steering cells' constant asymmetry on every seed and turns their direction flip from 0.14 to 0.95 (lane C C-N61, three seeds, the silencing control null). DNa02 downstream did not follow, so the sight chain's block sits at HS to DNa02 and in the cord. Silencing the untyped left-lobe input (C-N62, one seed) both unmasks and starves the left detector, so the correction is to type those rows, not to silence them.

The twelve steering interneurons already fire 52 Hz on the walk and take two thirds of their excitation from the cord (lane B's census), so the overlay that nearly doubled travel on two seeds and lengthened it by a third on twelve was extra drive onto firing cells; the one wired-and-silent descending type with a real share, DNg35, is the next screen.

Lane C's Codex seat could not see the GPU: a seatbelt profile that denies IOKit returns no Metal device, measured at 19:05, and the Codex CLI's workspace-write sandbox is that class. Lane D, also a Codex seat, found the route around it by launching the engine from the GUI-owned tmux shell.

The line above that reads "at +40 Hz the same early read is negative on 13 of 18 and 11 of 17 pairs: present, small" was the 100 ms read. Lane E then re-read the same 36 pairs on the window equal to the stimulus (200 ms): the resistance reflex is there on 36 of 36, gain 0.45 of the joint's own drive with the command on and 0.52 with it off (18 of 18 each), Welch t = 0.57, so at the sensors' working rates the command does nothing to it; the command's effect appears at the full range (+120 Hz, gain 1.13 against 0.76, p = 0.021). Second addendum, 22:10 EEST: five corrections in three hours, and all five were the instrument

The entry above ends at about 19:45. What the evening added belongs with it, because it is the same lesson five more times: on this project the thing most likely to be wrong is not the model but the instrument that reads it, and the cheapest experiment available is usually a measurement of our own apparatus.

The champion held its title twice and the second was worth the run. Lane E searched the champion's dials with the three labelled corrections switched on and produced the first challenger that moves: 1.63 against 1.18 mm/s on the seeds where both stay upright, faster on fifteen of twenty. On its own twelve selection seeds it never fell. On twenty-four fresh judge seeds it flipped onto its back four times, at 171 degrees of tilt each time, a stereotyped inversion rather than scattered failures, where wb4 falls on none. Ordering item 8, which was written at 18:45 for a holder that qualifies on every one of its own seeds, had it matched on seeds neither body had seen; the count decided it 24 to 19 and the card was never read. Lane E had named the mechanism in its own nomination: twelve seeds choose the winner of twenty-eight draws.

The match was contended and lane A caught it. Lane A reported that its own exclusive-locked worker had been running while the title match advanced, and the machine clock agreed: 26 seconds a seed against the 19 the holder's own record took alone. The engine rule requires a title receipt to run with no other Metal process, so the defence was marked provisional and the challenger's twenty-four seeds were replayed alone. The replay is bit-identical: the same twenty standing, the same four falls at the same tilts, identical speed to the last digit on twenty-four of twenty-four. The contention cost wall-clock and nothing else, the defence stands on a clean receipt, and the comparison went onto the determinism gap as a two-worker data point. The confusion had a cause worth recording: the judge's own section headings had been running fifteen to twenty minutes ahead of the wall clock, which is why lane A's receipt named the wrong window.

A verdict was inverted by two naming errors that compound. At 21:00 the record said the hind knee's phasing was the animal's. Then the judge verified on the built map that the capture's two activation channels carry the opposite muscle pools at every knee: the channel named for the extensor is 89 percent flexor-pool mass at the left hind, because the channels are the positive and negative halves of a signed map and their names follow the joint's direction, not the muscle. That defect had been registered since 3 September and never fixed. Lane A then settled the second error from the postures its captures actually occupy, rather than from a derivative at the model's straight-legged zero, where the angle sits at a maximum and says nothing: positive knee angle is flexion at the posture the fly walks in. Both errors point the same way, which is the check on them, and the verdict inverts. The hind knee flexes through stance where the animal's extends. Every run now emits a table of which muscles feed which channel, so no reader has to infer it again.

The animal's knee was measured, and it graded the conflict. Lane A read all 28,059 sequences of the tracking data already in the repository, about 450,000 stance episodes a leg: the front knees close through stance and the middle and hind knees open. Against that, five of the model's six legs move the right way and the left hind moves backwards, while four legs move at six to forty-two percent of the animal's excursion. One sign conflict and one magnitude conflict, which are different fixes, from data that cost nothing to read.

And the fly's stroke is lost in a modelling choice. Lane A read the joint stage as the second-order filter it is: at the champion's dials and its own step rate the joint passes 0.5175 of what it is commanded, against 0.9257 at critical damping, so a body at critical damping would move 1.79 times as far at the same drive. The judge checked that arithmetic independently from the transfer function. Every route to the animal's speed tried on this body, lowering the damping or raising the drive per joint, has ended in the same failure: the fly walks faster and flips onto its back. The judge then named load-dependent stance stiffness as the fleet's next search, and lane A refuted it within twelve minutes with a measurement rather than an argument: the stage that mechanism acts through transmits 1.002 of the commanded angle in the step band, so nothing is lost there for a stiffness dial to recover. The direction was withdrawn and the candidate refuted. What remains is the honest shape of it: the champion needs three times critical damping to stand, that value passes our own damping row only because the row has no upper bound and its reason is methodological, and the fly's own passive joint damping has never been measured. That measurement is now the most valuable one this project could buy for the body model.

One cell was found on the way. The row that masks the left eye's motion detector turned out to be the left CT1 itself, which BANC never typed and never gave a transmitter, so the model has been driving the left optic lobe with an inhibitory giant signed excitatory while the right lobe had the real thing. Lane C established it by column tiling, opposite lobes, zero partner overlap, matched size, and two CT1s in the male. The identity patch is enabled and the chain read is queued.

Lane E: the margin search, the nomination with its own caveats stated, and the yielded worker. Lane C: the CT1 identification and the disagreement that preceded it. Judge: item 8, the match, the provisional marking and the clean replay, the channel verification and its receipt, five rulings and two withdrawals of its own.

Third addendum, 2026-09-06 00:50 EEST: the bar caught up with the champion, and the champion cost more than it was worth

Written past midnight and kept here rather than opened as a new entry, because the shift is one piece of work. Champion: wb4, unchanged since 17:05, now with three defences. Commit: the commit this addendum lands in, after d0228b6b8. Seeds: judge 30244-30267 (the wc3 match, both arms, and a third pass of the same block); the wc3 card block 30268-30279 was never spent because the count did not lead. No seed at all was spent on the two findings below that matter most.

The nominee that closed a conflict and lost by one run

wc3 is the champion plus one number: the middle leg's coxa-trochanter joint limit raised from 22.5 degrees to the front leg's 91.2. The model had been capping that joint at a quarter of the front's range, from a table of walking excursions measured on tethered flies and used as a hard anatomical limit, while this project's own free-walking tracking puts the middle-to-front ratio near one. It is the first nominee in the project's history to CLOSE an open measured-data conflict, and the tie-break that rewards exactly that had been written and tightened hours earlier, before the nomination existed.

Before the seeds ran the judge wrote down what it expected: a tie, decided by the closed conflict, which would have been the first coronation on measured data rather than on a count. It came out 23 against 24. One run of twenty-four, a fall at 171 degrees on seed 30261, and the tie-break never fired. The prediction is on the record as wrong.

The fall is not a glitch: three exclusive replays on a clean machine invert at 171.16 every time. It is also not evidence. Lane E's pooled 228 runs put that inversion at about one run in sixty on the champion itself and one in seventy-two on single-correction bodies, so one fall of twenty-four against zero is Fisher p = 1.000. Lane A read the seed directly and found both bodies disturbed within 22 ms of each other at 2.13 seconds, the corrected body a degree MORE upright and carrying more feet up to that moment, and only the champion recovering. Then it registered a prediction about what precedes an inversion, tested it over 146 runs, and refuted itself: nothing in the 500 ms before a departure separates the eight inversions from the 134 standing runs.

The judge declined to change the tie-break to fire on a statistically indistinguishable count, and said why in the open: it had predicted the tie, and a rule that converts a failed prediction into a coronation is not one that seat should write. That question went to Robin with its default. In the same hour it wrote two clauses that push the other way, because a judge may tighten a rule it is invested in and may not loosen one.

A row nobody was reading, and how much it had moved

The model's fly rises and falls by 0.70 of its own body height while walking. A real fly does about 0.10. The number had been in every saved run since a lane D diff on the 4th, and the constraint row still carried a value from qh1, two champions back at 0.43 to 0.49. Nothing graded it, so it drifted, and the direction of drift was not random: it got worse at every handover while the bar counted steps.

The same audit found four more card rows still reading the cadence instrument that a bar revision had retired in September. Both were fixed the same night, and the holder's values on the new reads were computed from its own saved runs so no match would be graded against a blank.

Lane D then used the new row within half an hour and found the hole in the veto that had just been written: it graded every row on how many runs land in band, and a count cannot fall below zero, so on a row where both bodies are entirely out of band a challenger may take an already-broken conflict arbitrarily further from the animal for free. wc3 does exactly that, raising the bob 0.077 body heights on 22 of 23 paired seeds while the instrument read nothing. The bar gained a floor rule the same hour: such a row is graded on the paired runs, by the median's distance from the band, a sign test, and a shift larger than the holder's own repeat noise. It is symmetric, and on wc3 it returns one regression and one improvement, so it would not have held that body either.

What the last title cost, from receipts nobody had opened

The champion is its predecessor plus one key, subthreshold adaptation at 2.0. So the coronation batteries of 17:05 already WERE the paired one-key test: both arms, the same 24 judge seeds, every run standing on both. Read at 00:42, no new seed:

quantitywb4wb1mpairedwb4 higher on
cadence, 10 ms read5.636 Hz5.091+0.6823/24
forward speed1.202 mm/s1.537-0.407/24
vertical bob0.7200.684+0.03719/24
final tilt9.42 deg10.66-1.125/24

Lane A reproduced three of those four on its own seeds and not the speed, which was also the only one whose sign test sat above 0.05. It said so plainly instead of smoothing it, and a second block was authorised.

What holds the speed direction up is a curve lane D measured at 16:02 and which nobody, the judge included, had read against the speed conflict for nine hours: at adaptation 0, 2 and 4 on twelve seeds with the same seeds at every dose, forward speed runs 1.965, 1.358, 1.059 and cadence runs 4.909, 5.591, 5.500. Speed falls monotonically; cadence rises once and then stops. The real band for speed starts at 2.0, so with adaptation off this body sits within two percent of closing the conflict it is furthest from, and fails only the cadence floor, by 0.09 Hz.

That is the whole trade the last coronation made: 0.09 Hz below one floor against 0.6 mm/s above the other, on a bar that counts the first and not the second. No dose between 0 and 2 has ever been run. It is now the sharpest open question in the project and it is one-dimensional.

wb4's card now records this, and records that wb4 would be HELD under the bar as it stands tonight. Nothing is stripped and nothing is rewritten: it won under the bar as that bar was written, and it is champion of record. Saying what it cost is what a card is for.

Three wrong readings by the judge in one night, all published and all corrected

The first: "this fly buys ground with posture," written from three lanes' packets without checking the obvious confound. The second: the check itself, whose pooled correlation over 136 arms mixed arms built on different base bodies and reversed sign under stratification, which is Simpson's paradox and was published twenty minutes after correcting a lane for less. What survives is sharper than either: within the current champion speed, bob and tilt rise together (bob against tilt, rho +0.750, p 0.0008); two champions back none of the three is coupled to any other. The third: attributing lane C's failing gate clause to the Metal engine's relaxed atomics, refuted by three fresh NumPy seeds on which the same quantity also crosses zero. Lane C had stopped rather than proceed, which was right, and the clause, not the engine, was the defect.

And a piece of plumbing that was not plumbing

Checking one lane's rewritten branch found that all five lanes had rewritten pushed history at some point, with the old heads reachable from nothing on the remote and alive only in the judge's local objects: 32 commits, 4, 4, 177 from that morning, and 7 at 00:28. Every packet citing an execution commit from before those points had been unresolvable for anyone cloning fresh. All five old heads are now tagged on the remote, and the repair was automated rather than restated for a sixth time, because a rule broken five times needs a mechanism and the judge cannot reach into a lane's own process.

Lane A: the nomination, the saturation test with its kill threshold registered first, the seed read, the refutation of its own precursor prediction, the killing of the fleet's compliant-body claim, and the disagreement on the speed row that the judge adopted. Lane D: the heave measurement that changed the bar within half an hour of the row existing, and the dose curve it had already run nine hours earlier. Lane E: the correction of its own seeds-cluster reading, and the retraction of its own composition claim, both registered. Lane C: stopping on an unstable gate rather than proceeding, and the NumPy evidence that overturned the judge's diagnosis. Lane B: a self-correction of its own prose against its own table, and the descending-share census. The judge: three defences held, two clauses written, one clause declined and routed to Robin, three wrong readings published and corrected, and the two findings that mattered most taken from files that had been sitting on disk unread.

17:05 EEST. Champion: wb4, crowned under v3.6, 24 against 17 on wb1m's own seeds. wb1m held the title from 12:46 to now, one defence won.

Where the dial came from

cns.py gained adapt_a and adapt_b on 2026-08-09, the day of the bistability work: a spike-triggered adaptation term the searches have used ever since, and a subthreshold term that stayed at 0.0 because walk_search.py had no line that read it. Lane A's shape audit of 2026-09-01 wrote it down as gap.mech_adapt_a, "a compiled default nobody chose is a claim," with the stop-rule amendment's instruction that a mechanism with an evidence map gets its ON arm or a registration saying why not. It sat for four days.

Lane D, back from twelve silent hours this morning, read the goal, wrote the resolver, and priced the dial at 4 on two seeds at 16:02: antagonist phase 20 degrees toward the animal's, cadence up, network activity halved, registered net speed down, dropped by its own net-speed gate. The judge declined the drop, since a lever that moves two conflicts at once on two seeds is not closed by a two-seed gate on a quantity the title does not ask, and asked for the title's own read on twelve paired seeds at doses 2 and 4. Lane D returned it at 16:42: wb1m 3 of 12, dose 2 and dose 4 both 12 of 12, nine gains and no loss, and nominated the lower dose.

The match

The nominee arrived at a main that could not run it: the keys gate flagged adapt_a as a key walk_search.py never reads, which is the "two flies" defect the gate exists for. Lane D's seam was ported as five hunks (the resolver, the network cache key, the SimParams assignment, two receipt fields, the extras condition), the bit-identity probe stayed exact, and the match ran under the exclusive lock in five minutes: batteries 12 of 12 and 12 of 12 qualifying, standing 12 of 12 in both, against wb1m's 9 and 8 on the same seeds. Seven seeds where wb4 qualifies and wb1m does not, none the other way. The same-condition replay read standing 12/12, qualifying 12 on the same seeds, 12 of 12 seeds identical to the original on standing, cadence, lifts and travel. NumPy on two seeds per arm: wb4 30172 qualifies (5.73 Hz, 6.0 mm), 30186 qualifies (6.00 Hz, 7.1 mm); wb1m 30172 qualifies (5.27 Hz), 30186 qualifies (5.00 Hz).

Two corrections from lane D within the hour, both the judge's: its paired seeds were 61171-61182, not the block first written, and the adaptation time constant in the nominee is wb1m's own explicit 270.977 ms, not the 100 ms the nominee's metadata called a default. The theta that ran is exactly the nominee's; the metadata is corrected in the record and the hashed file is left as the receipts saw it.

What it costs

On the holder's seeds the standing runs' forward speed is 1.51 against wb1m's 1.85 mm/s and travel 6.62 against 8.45 mm. The count rises because runs sitting at the 5 Hz floor cross it (cadence 5.636 against 5.091 Hz median); the body covers a fifth less ground per second. Under ordering item 4 speed orders nothing; under the zero-conflicts aim it is a conflict that moved away from the animal, written on the card as such. Dose 4 qualified equally on lane D's seeds at a larger cost; no higher dose is on the record.

The afternoon around it

A searched body stands at real joint compliance (zeta 1.5, 8 of 12) and buys no unconditional speed, because the middle and hind legs still do not stroke; the coxal promotor is a front-leg-only cell type in both animals and the middle legs' coxa movers all fire in stance on the network's own timing, so the map has no swing-timed driver for that joint (lane A, three static reads; its tip-velocity instrument is under its own audit). The front-claw mirror costs 0.3 mm/s and half the count on wb1m and is not a coordination-rule effect; a dial search with it in is registered. The campaniform stand-in is a small threshold requirement, a quarter of it suffices and zero costs two; the search with it absent is running. Lane B mapped the steering path's classes on both animals and drove DNa02 left against right to no motor asymmetry; lane C located the steering cells' constant asymmetry in BANC's left optic lobe, reconstructed at three quarters of the right's, and withdrew a caveat of its own as seed noise.

Attribution

Robin: the goal, and the standing rules this ran under (the parameter rule, the no-inert-element directive, the ordering clause he ruled bar by bar). Lane A: the shape audit that named the dial on 2026-09-01. Lane D: the resolver, the paired reads at three doses, the nomination, and both metadata corrections. The judge: the refusal to close the lever on a two-seed gate, the port under the probe, the match, replay and confirmation, and the bundle.

2026-09-05 The cord does not take orders The morning's question, does sight change what a standing fly does, is answered end to end by the afternoon. The eye's motion detector fires with the right direction on the champion's own settings; its left-right signal reaches the HS steering cells through the connectome and vanishes when the detector is off; and there it stops. A steering command injected straight into DNa02, the turn neuron, at the strength the eye delivers and at five times that, moves the leg motor neurons' left-right balance by under half a hertz. A walking command volley reaches the rhythm-generating interneurons within 35 to 55 ms and the motor neurons by 1.6 Hz; the command neurons themselves fire at 72 Hz with the command off, driven by the cord. The nerve cord walks on its own recurrence and does not take steering or start-stop commands from the brain at the champion's balance. One measured fact explains three open threads: the null on sight, the walk command's non-monotone dose, the stop neuron that cannot stop it. It is the wall every brain-borne behaviour will meet, and sight was the first to measure it station by station.

2026-09-05 15:4x EEST. Champion: wb1m (crowned 12:46, one defence held). Nothing about the champion changes in this entry; what changes is what the programme knows about the path from its brain to its legs.

The stations

Robin's 10:45 goal: "does sight change what a standing fly does." By 15:36 the chain from image to legs is measured at every station on BANC, female only:

image -> T4          direction selectivity generated by the coincidence
                     term, controlled by lag and pool swap (lane C, C-N43
                     to C-N46), live at the champion's own balance at one
                     gain, 0.3
T4 -> HS             the HS steering cells' left-right voltage flips with
                     grating direction on 3 of 3 paired seeds and not with
                     the detector off; 2.3 times stronger on a lobe-
                     balanced frame (C-N48, C-N49, C-N52)
HS -> DNa02          unresolved: one spiking cell per side against the
                     cord's noise, in spikes and in voltage (C-N50)
DNa02 -> motor       an imposed left-right rate step at DNa02 of the size
                     the HS flip implies, and 2 and 5 times it, changes
                     the leg motor neurons' left-minus-right rate by -0.46,
                     +0.20 and +0.39 Hz (lane B, 15:36, three seeds,
                     Metal)
sight -> turn        no: the judge's grade (11:59, five arms, twelve seeds,
                     the champion's own balance) and lane C's C-N51 and
                     C-N53 on lane seeds and the exemption build, uneven
                     and balanced frames, all read no direction-consistent
                     turn; six seconds of this fly's free walking drifts
                     about 100 degrees either way

The graph agrees with the dynamics (lane B, 15:05, static): BANC's DNa02 makes no synapse onto the 24 Pugliese CPG types the walk command reaches; it makes 382 and 328 excitatory synapses onto ipsilateral leg motor neurons, none across the midline. The CPG types load the motor neurons at near-equal excitation and inhibition (4,659 against 4,876 synapses), which is why a walk command volley moves them +15 Hz and the motor neurons +1.6 (lane B, 14:35).

What the cord does instead

With the walking command switched off, the two DNg100 command cells still fire at 71.8 Hz, driven by the cord's own recurrence; the overlay takes them to 137. The command-off fly walks 6.8 mm in six seconds; the published dose shape (0, 40 and 94 Hz) gives 6.8, 8.3 and 5.6 mm, not monotone in drive; DNg93, the stop neuron, does not stop it (the judge's start-stop reads earlier this week). The cord generates its own walk and its own turning, about 100 degrees of drift per six seconds, and the brain's commands are modulations of a few percent on top of it. That is the champion; a real fly starts, stops and steers on descending command.

Why this is the day's result and not a failure

The zero-conflicts aim says a conflict found is a region of parameter space deleted. This one deletes a large region: no gain, frame, contrast or trial length on the stimulus side will turn this fly, because the signal is already in the steering cells and the cord does not act on descending asymmetry. Lane C stopped at exactly that point, on the shift rule, after testing the endpoint twice at its shortest fair form; lane B measured the remaining stations in three packets over an hour. The question that replaces "does sight reach the fly" is a mechanism question with an owner: what carries a descending steering command to the motor side balance in the animal, and which part of the model's copy is inert (gap.descending_steering_inert_in_cord, lane B, static downstream reads of DNa02 and DNg100 by target class on both animals against the balance scale the model applies to each class).

Also today, after the coronation

wb1m held its first defence against wb3, the champion plus the load-fed campaniform channel at lane E's factor, 17 against 15 on the holder's seeds; the low-pass variant of that channel read 10 and its arm closed by its own registration; the passive abdomen closed on twelve Metal seeds with speed and cadence as co-primaries (speed 7 of 12, median +0.06 mm/s). Lane C withdrew its caveat 2: the exempted build's gain-0 asymmetry was one draw from seed noise at a half-hertz idle. Lane A named the speed limiter, a joint damped to stand, and its search with the compliant joint is running.

Attribution

Robin: the question and the hold-at-neural clause (10:45), and the live instruction at 15:15 that put lane C's harness right (handled by the consultant seat). Lane C: every station from image to HS, both frames, both controls, and the arithmetic that closed the endpoint. Lane B: the volley, the static hops, the rate steps. Lane A and lane E: the parallel work on the corrections and the joint. The judge: the grade, the concurrence, the record.

12:46 EEST. Champion: wb1m, crowned under v3.6, 17 against 14 on wa1's own seeds. wa1 held the title from 23:32 yesterday to now, the first fly under this bar and the first whose senses were switched on; wb1m keeps every one of its keys and adds one.

Why three corrections went to one match

Robin, 2026-09-04: "every neuron should have as realistic a model of it as possible with zero conflicts with a real fly. We're just trying to copy biology into our model." Three corrections of that kind sat on the judge's desk by noon, each a change to a sensory neuron's model, each measured by its lane to leave the walking count where it was:

  • Lane E, the campaniform channel fed by load. Since the loop closed on 2026-08-09 the campaniform sensilla, which report strain, were fed muscle activation as a stand-in because the model had no ground. It has had ground for weeks. Lane E measured the stand-in at 69% of the channel's drive (R366, two seeds, factor 3.2365 with spread 0.036) and the load signal at that factor neutral over 24 paired seeds (R367: 9 against 8 qualifying, 6 wins 5 losses 13 ties).
  • Lane E, modality by exact cell type. The encoder had read each leg sensory row's modality from BANC's cell_sub_class. Lane E's R299 audit found 71 rows whose exact cell_type names a different modality, and R271 eighteen SNpp39/41 rows in the same class. Lane D ported the seam with five tests and asked for it on main; lane E had run every arm on it for a day.
  • Lane A, the front-claw mirror. BANC types the right front leg's claw afferents SNpp50/SNpp51 in the mirror of the left's, the one reversal among eleven leg-side comparisons across two animals (Fisher 1.6e-06). Correcting the 25 cells moved the front contralateral phase 46 to 63 degrees toward the animal's on 36 seeds with the count unchanged (15 against 16).

Under the title clause a correction to the champion is a theta change and a theta change is a match. Lane E's, lane D's and lane A's numbers all predicted a tie, and the ordering clause's items 5 to 7 exist for a tie: extend to 48 seeds, then break on open measured-data conflicts, where a closed gap counts for the challenger. One combined match was the cheap route: 24 Metal runs, a tie expected, three gaps closing at once. The judge nominated wb1 with a frozen hash at 11:43, and matched it at 12:00 on the holder's seeds 30171-30194, where wa1 had qualified 8 and 6.

What the match said

wb1 qualified 3 on the first battery and 1 on the second, 4 of 24, with three runs not standing where wa1 stood on every seed. Two of the three walked seven to ten millimetres and ended below the height clause; one flipped over. That is not a tie. The three single-correction splits were nominated at 12:04 with frozen hashes and run one after another on the same seeds:

wb1c  load-fed campaniform      11/12 and 11/12 standing, 7 + 5 = 12
wb1m  exact-type modality       12/12 and 12/12 standing, 9 + 8 = 17
wb1r  front-claw mirror         12/12, 8 and 12/12, 7 standing and qualifying, total 15

Each battery of each split passes the clause on its own. Against wa1's 14, the load channel loses by two, the mirror WINS by 1, and the exact-type routing wins by three: seven seeds where wb1m qualifies and wa1 does not (30176, 30180, 30182, 30189, 30190, 30191, 30193) against four the other way (30172, 30175, 30186, 30192). Cadence on the standing runs 5.09 against 5.00 Hz median; travel 8.45 against 8.95 mm; forward speed 1.85 against 1.81 mm/s. The gain is runs crossing the 5 Hz floor, not distance.

The same-condition replay of wb1m's first battery read standing 12/12, qualifying 9 on the same seeds, 11 of 12 seeds equal to the original on standing, cadence, lifts and travel (differing [30175]: 30175 4.18 against 4.55 Hz, both under the floor); a second exclusive replay: qualifying 9, 12 of 12 equal to the original (differing []); seed 30175 on NumPy (deterministic): 4.36 Hz, 10.46 mm, does not qualify. The decision quantity, the count, replays exactly; one non-qualifying seed's trajectory does not, within the documented Metal behaviour of the relaxed-atomic scatter at this theta's 28 ms levator delay near the 30 ms bound (engine rule item 2); recorded as a caveat, as qh1's coronation recorded its own. The NumPy confirmation the engine rule asks of a decision-ready result, two seeds per arm: wb1m 30171 qualifies (5.27 Hz, 10.4 mm), 30184 qualifies (5.36 Hz, 5.8 mm); wa1 30171 does not qualify (4.91 Hz), 30184 qualifies (5.55 Hz).

Three corrections that each cost nothing together cost thirteen qualifying runs. Before crowning, the pair without the load channel was matched too: wb2, exact-type routing plus the mirror, against wb1m on the same seeds, standing 12/12 and 11/12, qualifying 1 and 2, 3 against 17. So the two FeCO corrections do not compose, and the load channel, which alone costs two, was not the cause. Nothing on the record explains why two annotation corrections to the same claw population cancel each other's walking; it is opened as a gap, not a finding, with the mirror's owner and the modality audit's owner named. The mirror alone beat wa1 (15 against 14) and is a valid champion candidate in its own right; it lost to wb1m's 17.

What wb1m is not

It is wa1's body with one key. The middle and hind legs still do not stroke forward (diary 55), speed is unchanged, and the sight grade of this morning was run on wa1's balance and read no direction following; wb1m changes nothing in the visual path. The fresh-seed card on 30220-30231 is the statement of where each conflict stands on the new holder.

Attribution

Robin: the realism directive that makes a sensory correction a first-class candidate, and the title clause he ruled bar by bar. Lane E: the audit (R299), the seam (R271) and the load channel (R366/R367). Lane D: the verbatim port and its five tests. Lane A: the mirror and the 36-seed measurement of it. The judge: the combined nomination, the split, the match, the replay and confirmation, the coronation bundle. Mistral relayed nothing on this thread; Robin's rulings were read from the goal file and AGENTS.md.

2026-09-05 The eye worked and the legs did not hear it The first behavioural test of sight on a walking champion. Lane C repaired the coincidence seam that had made the model's motion detector blind to its own inputs, showed the T4 detector fires direction-selectively at the champion's own balance, and showed its left-right signal reaches the HS steering cells through the connectome alone and vanishes with the detector off. 2026-09-05 12:02 EEST. Champion: wa1, title held under v3.6. Nothing crowned today.

The question Robin set

Robin, 10:45: "the grade is a single question, does sight change what a standing fly does, on twelve seeds, engine-identical, carrying the caveat C stated before running. Hold it at neural until it clears. Crown nothing on a body that cannot stand."

The chain that reached the steering cells (lane C)

The day's neural work rests on a defect lane C found at 08:23: cns.py wrote the coincidence seam's presynaptic indicator before driven spikes were merged into the fired set, so the multiplication that makes a Reichardt detector had never once applied a non-zero term. Every earlier "the seam is inert" reading (C-N29, C-N32) was withdrawn on that. With the write moved (ported to main under the bit-identity probe), the T4 detector separates the two grating directions at bal_target 0 (C-N43), survives the lag control (C-N44), and, the part that mattered for the grade, is live at the champion's own balance of 0.43519 at one gain, 0.3 (C-N45: T4a -0.054 against T4b +0.084, 3 of 3 seeds; gain 1 saturates, gain 0 sits under the rate floor). Lane C's caveat, stated before running and carried into every record today: T4's detector only (fast Mi1, delayed Mi9/Mi4/C3, lag 60 ms), T5's is not implemented.

Then C-N48 and C-N49 (11:50): on the stitched build the left-right voltage asymmetry of the HS cells, the lobula-plate tangential cells that feed the turn command, flips sign with grating direction on 3 of 3 paired seeds (+0.099, +0.035, +0.022) and does not flip with the detector off (largest 0.007). Nothing hand-wired past the detector. The DNa02 spike readout was withdrawn by lane C's own control as unpowered (one spiking cell per side); the voltage read runs next. Two instrument facts from the same runs: the column frame carries 6,938 right-lobe against 5,736 left-lobe carriers under a constant HS asymmetry near -0.7, so the sign of a flip is not yet a turn direction; and switching the detector on moves the HS baseline from +0.14 to -0.70, unexplained.

The grade

Pre-registered at 11:15 (lanes/judge/2026-09-05-vision-grade-prereg.md, instrument lanes/judge/vision_grade.py), amended at 11:2x before any seed ran: lane E's 11:05 packet pointed out that C-N45 had already cleared at the champion's own balance, so the optic-lobe exemption the first draft carried would change a second thing against wa1 for no reason the question needed. The body became wa1's theta of record plus the carrier in lane C's deliver-only mode (the grating reaches T4/T5 and nothing is written to the turn command, so the connectome is the only route from eye to cord) plus the T4 detector at gain 0.3.

Five arms per seed on NumPy (the detector refuses Metal and its 60 ms lag is above Metal's reproducibility bound): grating +1 and -1 with the detector, +1 and -1 with the coincidence keys removed, and blind. Twelve judge seeds, 30208 to 30219, unseen by any seat. A seed counted only if it stood, by the title's tilt clause, in all five arms. The primary: the sign of yaw(+1) minus yaw(-1) over the five-second stimulus, two-sided exact binomial under 0.05.

Result at 11:59. Standing: +1 12 of 12, -1 9 of 12, product-off +1 12 of 12, product-off -1 11 of 12, blind 12 of 12; eight seeds counted. The sign agreed on 4 of 8 (p = 1.0). The control without the detector agreed on 6 of 8 (p = 0.29). Median |D| 0.78 rad with the detector against 0.64 rad without (one-sided p = 0.47). Lateral speed contrasts null both ways. Blind against sighted: forward speed 1.90 against 1.99 and 1.88 mm/s, cadence 4.86 against 5.14 and 5.00 Hz. The coincidence receipt shows the product applied on all twelve sighted seeds (1.65e8 each). Every run, blind or sighted, turned about -2 rad in five seconds, the champion's straightness conflict, which the paired contrast removes.

Reading, by the outcome table written before the runs: the detector fires and its direction signal does not reach the legs within five seconds at this gain. Any direction-following turn is smaller than the walker's own sensitivity to a changed input. Recorded as vision.optomotor_turning, CONFLICT on the sighted build at one point (gain 0.3, contrast 0.25, 4 Hz, 5 s, T4 only), FEMALE-ONLY. Three forks, in cost order: DNa02 in voltage (lane C, running); a lobe-balanced frame, since the -1 direction fell 3 of 12 where +1 fell none (Fisher 0.22, recorded not claimed); then the gain ladder in behaviour and a longer trial. A paired extension on the exemption build runs beside it and grades nothing.

Run metadata: theta lanes/judge/theta-wa1-sight-nominee.json (sha256_16 37d387d30f8358e5, 69 keys), 60 runs at 65 to 120 s each, about 20 minutes per arm with three then two workers; arms 1 to 3 ran walk_search 995a924b7c17828e and arms 4 to 5 the engine after a default-off port, probe BIT-IDENTICAL; verdict lanes/judge/2026-09-05-vision-grade-verdict.json.

The oldest conflict, located (lane A)

Speed on wa1 is 1.6 mm/s against real flies' 10 to 20. Lane A read the strokes on 45 standing runs across three seed blocks: the front legs run forward in the air and backward on the ground on 45 of 45; the middle legs barely stroke; the left hind leg swings backwards through the air on 45 of 45 and is dragged forward on the ground; the right hind is inert. Two of six legs propel with a 0.1 mm step. The cause is static and in the map: the joint that swings a middle or hind leg fore-aft is ThC_pitch, and motormap.build_map gives it live motor neurons lf 6, rf 6, lm 1, lh 1, rh 1, rm 0, because BANC and the male annotate the promotor on the front leg only and the eight protractor-side rows per middle and hind leg sit at gain 0. The map's own comment named the hazard when it was written; no search ever turned the rows on. Four registrations then failed to give those legs a forward stroke: grip (ZC), both rotators live (ZD), their sign flipped (ZE), the anterior rotator alone (ZH), every one swinging the legs backwards in the air. Lane A withdrew its own speed lead at 11:38 as survivorship and stopped the line. The T2/T3 coxal protractor is MISSING in both datasets as labelled; the male's 12 to 14 unlabelled motor neurons per middle and hind leg are the only source of a label.

Also today

Lane E measured the campaniform stand-in replaceable by the load signal at a factor of 3.2365, neutral over 24 paired seeds; nominated balance_by_type as a default-off search dial (ported, nine tests green); read the motor pool recruitment-ordered during walking on both champions. Lane D returned from silence with a two-seed scout that dropped its own route on the posture gate. Lane B: DNa01 at champion rank adds travel on one wa1 seed of two; DNg100 on four of four. Three sensory corrections measured neutral on their own seeds (load-fed campaniform, exact-type FeCO modality, the 25-cell front-claw mirror that corrects BANC's one mirror-reversed typing) were bundled into one challenger, wb1, nominated with a frozen hash and matched on the holder's 24 judge seeds this afternoon.

Attribution

Robin: the goal and its three clauses (10:45); the rulings this grade ran under (footage only for improvement claims; the engine rule; hold at neural). Lane C: the seam defect, the neural chain from C-N43 to C-N49, the caveats. Lane E: the 11:05 catch that the exemption was not needed, which changed the body under grade before a seed ran. Lane A: the stroke read and the map finding, and its own withdrawal. The judge: the pre-registration and its amendment, the instrument, the five-arm design, the verdict, and the ports under the probe (deliver-only, the column frame, yaw fields, balance_by_type, FeCO exact-type, reflex_map).

2026-09-04 The fly could not feel its legs 1 video The champion's leg position sensors delivered exactly zero to its nerve cord on four to five of its six legs, because a high-pass filter tuned above 1 clips a steady signal to nothing. Twelve explanations for a left-right stepping asymmetry were killed first, all of them about the connectome, because the fault was upstream of all of them. Turning the senses back on was expected to slow the fly, since every sensory channel reaches the motor pools through majority inhibition and the literature says feedback masks a leg's own rhythm; it did the opposite, and the judge's written corollary was contradicted seventy-five minutes after it was recorded. 2026-09-04 23:34 EEST. Champion: wa1, crowned tonight under v3.6, the first fly to clear that bar. It replaces qh1, which held the record since 2026-09-03.

The day began with a puzzle about two slow legs and ended with a champion, and the thing in between was not a discovery about the fly. It was a discovery about what we had been simulating.

The hunt

The champion's left front and left hind legs stepped at about half the rate of their partners. Two lanes measured it on three separate batches of seeds and got the same numbers to the second decimal, so it was real and it was not noise.

Lane A then killed twelve explanations for it. Which premotor cell types reach the pool, how much input volume each leg gets, when that input arrives, how hard those cells fire, whether the cells were muted, whether their encoded position had saturated, whether the signal they carry was uninformative. All null, all about the connectome, over about four hours.

The sharpest of them swapped the two sides' inputs so that the right sensors were reading the left legs' joints. They still did nothing. So it was not what those cells were saying.

What it was

Every claw afferent's output passes through a high-pass filter that subtracts the cell's own running average and re-amplifies what is left. The champion's setting for that filter was 1.967. Above 1, the subtraction is larger than the signal, and the result is clipped at zero.

A claw cell is a position sensor. It sits at its own average by construction.

So the output was not small. It was exactly zero, on every tick, on four to five of the six legs. Turning the gain up multiplied zero. Deleting the cells removed nothing. Halving their connections changed nothing. Twelve explanations had to fail, because the fault was upstream of everything they examined.

Then lane E asked the question one level wider and found it was not only the claw: the same filter gates all five sensory channels, and two hair-plate channels were dead as well.

The prediction that was wrong, and whose

Turning the senses back on was expected to make the fly slower. Two reasons, both good ones. Lane E measured that every proprioceptive channel reaches the leg motor pools through majority inhibition one synapse out. And the literature has said since Sapkal that proprioceptive feedback masks a leg's own rhythm rather than generating it, so a fly with its feedback deleted should look faster than one without.

This diary should record that the judge wrote that reasoning down as a corollary at 22:52 and it was contradicted seventy-five minutes later by the arm it asked for. Lane A put the corollary into its registration as the thing to falsify, which is why the answer arrived so quickly.

A body with all five channels live stands 12 of 12 and steps faster: +0.682 Hz paired, up on 11 of 12 seeds, with a quarter more lifts on 12 of 12, and the left-right asymmetry cut to a third. It replicated on a second fresh block the same hour.

The one key it turns on

The champion assigned each claw cell to the flexion or extension population by whether its row number was even. BANC labels those cells itself, SNpp50 and SNpp51, and that labelling is mirror-asymmetric.

Restoring the claw under row parity: lifts fall, 0 of 10 seeds up. Restoring the claw under BANC's own labels: lifts rise, 10 of 10 seeds up.

Same channel, same restoration, less drive in the arm that works. The asymmetry in the annotation is not a defect to be corrected. It is load-bearing, and the symmetric split was what broke the leg.

The bar

wa1 clears v3.6 on two independent twelve-seed judge batteries: standing 12 of 12 and 12 of 12, qualifying 8 of 12 and 6 of 12, tip cadence 5.045 and 4.955 Hz on the ten-millisecond read. The bar asks for 6 of 12 standing and 2 qualifying.

That bar was raised twice this morning, both times against the fly that held the title: at 00:45 because a quarter of the champion's counted steps turned out to be one-tick hovers, and at 01:05 because the joint integrator had a numerical mode in it. The throne sat empty for twenty-three hours.

https://theuploadinglab.ai/fly/walker_wa1_body.mp4

What it does not fix

Speed is flat. The fly still travels about 1 mm/s where a real one does 2 to 45. Tilt is slightly worse. Its other open conflicts were carried over from qh1 and have not been re-read on this body yet.

Who did what

Robin set the goal: make the scoreboard measure the copy, and fill the vacant title. He also asked, on seeing the clips, why the legs went through the ground, which turned out to be a renderer replaying commanded joint angles instead of achieved ones and was fixed the same hour.

Lane A ran the hunt, killed its own twelve accounts, caught the judge's survivorship error, and built and confirmed the champion. Lane E found that the gating was not only the claw and measured the inhibition structure. Lane B traced the claw-to-motor path and found it present on every leg, including the silent ones. Mistral caught that the cause had been sitting in the calibration ledger since 06:37 that morning, framed as a note about the code's shape rather than its absence.

The judge measured the per-leg zeros, ran the title match, and was wrong twice in public: once about a speed gain that was survivorship, once about a cadence cost that was not there.

Question. Can the one flyscore conflict every champion since nk1 has carried, posture variability 0.015 radians against the real 0.026 to 0.086, close without costing the walk? The measure is the variability of the abdomen-thorax angle, and the abdomen of every champion was rigid: BANC has 168 abdominal motor neurons and the walker actuated none of them. The judge built an adapter at 12:30 (lane B's 11:01 census, a neuromere fold onto the body's five abdomen links, one gain, a 30 degree clip, all ten signs +1) and lane D took the search.

Predicted (pre-registered). Lane D's 18:12 card at gain 0.3 put posture in band on five of five seeds with four standing, and gain 1.0 toppled three of five. Its 19:17 five-seed screen at 0.15 to 0.30 read standing at 3 or 4 of 5 at every gain and the route was dropped as a standing cost. At 19:54 lane D froze a nomination theta anyway, qg1 plus abd_gain 0.2 (sha 4bc4ba31), and ran the bar's own instrument on twelve paired fresh seeds, single worker, isolated: 11 of 12 qualifying against qg1's 8 of 12, four seeds rescued and one lost. The five-seed screen had used a cruder standing read than the clause. The nomination predicted that the abdomen stabilises rather than topples at this gain.

Method. The judge ran the v3.5 instrument on the holder's 24 judge seeds for both arms, one battery at a time under FLY_WBE_METAL_LOCK_MODE=exclusive, because lane E had shown at 19:54 that one qg1 seed flips from standing (7.51 mm) to fallen (3.44 mm) between three-worker and isolated execution, twice identical in isolation. The holder's arm was therefore not read from its record but replayed under the same condition as the challenger. Four receipts, lanes/judge/2026-09-03-title-v35-qg1abd02-battery{1,2}.json and ...-qg1-isolated-battery{1,2}.json.

Result. qh1 23, qg1 22. Battery 1 standing 11 of 12 and qualifying 11 of 12 (30009 fell at 171.5 degrees); battery 2 standing 12 of 12, qualifying 12 of 12, including 30020 where qg1 falls at 155.7. qg1's isolated replay: 11 of 12 and 11 of 12, falls on 30010 and 30020, identical to its 17:31 record on every field of every seed. Discordant: qh1 stood on the two seeds qg1 fell on and fell on one seed qg1 stood on. On the 21 seeds where both stood qh1 steps slower on 16 (median 5.82 against 6.77 Hz on the hysteresis read, four runs within 0.5 Hz of the 5 Hz floor, 30017 at exactly 5.00) and travels further on 13 (median 1.14 against 1.12 mm/s). Every foot lifted at least 16 times in every standing run. Seed 30020 is the clip: qg1 falls, qh1 stands and steps at 7.00 Hz.

What it means. A body walking this vigorously is close to falling, and two of qg1's 24 title seeds did. A small mass swing at the back, driven by the cord's own abdominal motor output, damps those falls at a gain where it does not yet cause new ones; the same swing at gain 1.0 is what toppled three of five seeds in the afternoon. The mechanism is the reading of one lane on two dozen seeds, not a measured fact, and the margin is one seed on 24 paired: two discordant against one. The clause is a count rule and crowned on it; item 5's 48-seed extension applies only to an equal count. The map from abdominal motor neuron to body joint is a guess (no muscle label exists for any of the 168 cells), the range and signs are guesses, and now all three are load-bearing, so their replacing measurements move up the list.

What did not change: speed, 1.14 mm/s against 2 to 45, the oldest conflict, unread on this body beyond the title receipts; cadence moved down, not up; the champion-level closure of the posture row is the judge's card read of the title runs, pending, so the row stays CONFLICT tonight on lane D's five-seed reading alone; and every open row on qg1's card, the bilaterally in-phase gait lane A measured at 20:19, the hind left-right asymmetry, the FeCO flexion population, body height, R1i, the front-knee sweep, is carried unread onto qh1.

One thing did change that is not about this body. The 19:12 correction had said exact replay of qg1's parallel title batteries was unproven. It is now proven for that load: 24 seeds, every field equal. The caveat stands for heavier loads (seed 201060 six-wide, lane E's seed 100273 three-wide), which is why decision-grade runs keep the exclusive lock.

Lane A found that a third of the champion's counted lifts are one-tick hover taps on the hysteresis read, and the judge's re-read of qh1's own 24 title seeds with a 10 ms minimum swing episode gives 4.45 Hz where the hysteresis read gave 5.82, three of 24 qualifying where 23 did. Judge-seat update, 2026-09-04 03:32 EEST: a cut on vision, and the shape of the missed step. Lane C ran the male connectome (MCNS) in the engine, matched its optic-lobe firing rate to the female's, and found that the wiring offset the female lacks and the male has (148 to 168 degrees) gives no direction selectivity in T4/T5, and neither does a real 30 or 60 ms delay on the delayed arm added on top of it: the two families respond more to a moving grating with the delay in, but never in opposite signs. In linearly summing point neurons a delayed input and an undelayed one deliver the same total whichever way the grating moves, so the cut is a model class, not a parameter: the missing ingredient is a coincidence nonlinearity. Registered before each run, both animals, and the earlier "140-fold attenuation" number withdrawn by the lane itself the same night when it found the trace rows were sorted and carried the motor neurons. On the walking side, lane A traced the missed step to its end: the joint tracks its command, the foot rises 0.3 to 0.8 mm in the body frame on missed and completed cycles alike, and the world clearance is that rise less a 0.4 mm dip of the whole body a quarter cycle after all six legs flex together. The lock between segments is carried by between-segment excitation, its inhibitory half fires and is inert, and no gain on it, on the commissural class or on load feedback moves any pair toward the alternation a walking fly has.

Question. Why does the champion's hind foot drag? Entry 51 crowned nc1 at 6.36 Hz on the threshold read; the 14:59 hysteresis instrument (bar v3.4) then read the same runs at 3.50 Hz, every one under the 5 Hz floor, and lane A's CD1-PU had shown the hind feet moving forward while loaded in every run. Lane A's CD1-QE (17:00) asked the question one level down: which motor neurons in each leg pool fire under nc1's drive, and what force does the body assign them. The body follows Azevedo 2020, where per-spike twitch force spans about 770-fold across a pool, so each motor neuron's gain is 770 to the power of minus its rank in the pool. The read on six seeds: the largest cells, gain 1.0, are silent; the small cells, gain 1/250 to 1/770, fire at 36 to 78 Hz. The hind levator pool summed to 0.001 activation. The legs were commanded and the command reached cells the body had priced at nothing.

Predicted (pre-registered). CD1-QF (17:03, six seeds) and CD1-QG (17:13, twelve seeds) registered a size_span dial that compresses the range, 770 to 10 and to 30, with the clause that cadence fires if the compressed body qualifies on the v3.5 read where nc1 does not. The nomination at 17:20, hash frozen, predicted 18 to 22 of 24 qualifying on the judge's seeds for span 10, 10 to 16 for span 30, and 0 for the holder, whose Metal record already stood at 0 of 24.

Method. Lane A ran both spans against nc1 on 18 fresh Metal seeds (201099-201116): span 10 qualified 16 of 18 and stood 16 of 18, two falls over 130 degrees; span 30 qualified 10 of 18 and stood 18 of 18, its misses at 3.8 to 4.9 Hz on the floor; nc1 qualified 0 of 18. The judge ported the 13-line seam onto walk_search.py (absent key = the old arithmetic; lanes/A/probe.py bit-identical) and ran the v3.5 instrument: two twelve-seed batteries on 30001-30024, Metal, spike regularity 44, paired against nc1's 16:02 Metal record on the same seeds and engine. A fall on the primary was expected somewhere in 24; the match was decided on the count.

Result. qg1 22, nc1 0. Battery 1 standing 11 of 12, qualifying 11 of 12; battery 2 the same. The two losses are falls, 30010 at 77.6 degrees and 30020 at 155.7, on seeds where nc1 stood; nc1 fell on 30003 and 30014, where qg1 stood, so standing is 22 against 22. On the 20 seeds where both stood qg1 steps faster on all 20, median 6.77 against 3.64 Hz on the hysteresis read, and every one of its 22 standing runs is inside 5 to 16 Hz where every one of nc1's is under 5. Every foot lifted at least 17 times in every standing run; nc1's record had two runs with a foot under 5. Travel rose from 4.31 to 6.14 mm over six seconds. Lane A's prediction of 18 to 22 met at 22. Seed 30003 is the clip: the first seed of the block where the old body fell and the new one stood, 7.37 mm, 7.27 Hz.

What it means. The body's muscle model assigns force by the size principle and the connectome's drive recruits the small cells first, as the size principle says it should. The two facts are each measured, and together they were silencing the legs, because the first-order activation model between them has no tetanic summation: real muscle driven at 36 to 78 Hz holds a fused force many times a single twitch, and the model held one twitch's worth. The 10-fold span is a searched stand-in for that missing summation, recorded as such in the ledger row mn.size_gain_span with the force-frequency curves that would replace it. Two points were tried; the space between and beyond them, and nc1's drive_scale, which was fitted with the hind pools muted, are open.

What did not change: the fly still travels 1.0 mm/s against a real 2 to 45 (a 42 percent gain on nc1 and still a conflict), two seeds in 24 fall, and every open row on nc1's card (FeCO flexion population, tri_index, posture with the abdomen off, the 12:24 re-grade's six failures, the hind-foot drag itself) is carried unread onto this body. The mechanism read that started this, CD1-QE seed 201060, does not replay exactly on the judge's engine while two judge runs agree with each other; open with lane A, and the title rows are the judge's own.

Contribution ledger. Lane A: the mechanism read (CD1-QE), the dial, the two registrations, the prediction, the nomination with a frozen hash, and the seam. Judge: the port under the probe, the match, the clip, the coronation bundle, and the ledger row. Robin, 15:4x: the engine instruction that put the match on Metal, which is why two batteries took three minutes and the port, the match and the clip fit inside one half-hour pass.

Judge-seat update, 19:22 EEST. No later result changed the champion. The first qg1 card put footfall separation inside its reference band on 10 of 10 standing runs and put the median hysteresis swing at 16.25 ms, but both row promotions are held for an isolated Metal replay. Five conflicts remain on that card, including front-knee range at 74.4 degrees, net speed at 1.43 mm/s, and straightness at 0.3689. Adding abdomen gain 0.3 put posture variability inside its band on five of five Lane D runs, with four standing and about one leg of cadence lost. That is the only current extension with a shared-model signal.

The earlier replay discrepancy is now explained. Six concurrent Metal runs of seed 201060 split between two exact trajectories because relaxed float-atomic scatter depends on device contention. Routine BUILD runs may retain shared GPU use with that caveat. Decision-grade runs now request an exclusive repository-wide Metal lock, and the title runner aborts on any run exception. qg1's 22 to 0 title result is unchanged, but exact isolated replay remains due on a Metal-capable judge.

Arie's consultation changed the search route, not the current title. Neural parameter grouping is cell-type-first rather than hemilineage-first. Blanket inhibitory downweighting was rejected; CT1's single point state was recorded as a visual representation gap and assigned a one-seed silencing screen. Lane C now moves upstream to the native MaleCNS R1-R6 to T4/T5 to visual-projection-neuron path, with selective T4/T5 ablation deficits as the acceptance test. The open recruiting decision is whether Robin wants Arie's warm introduction to Philip Shiu at Eon.

Lane B's own confirm on 80540-80551, registered 09:25 with its accept rule written first (under-floor count strictly below control, or equal with fewer falls or more qualifies), was still running when the match finished and lands on the card either way.

Method. Two twelve-seed batteries on 30001-30012 and 30013-30024, NumPy, spike_reg 44, in a worktree pinned to commit a9babf17d (walk_search 072a3cbb09da81be, cns d7ebac3530d83c5a), paired with nk1's battery 1 and 2 receipts on the same seeds. A run qualifies when it stands at the end (tilt under 51.68 degrees, height over 1.0, displacement at least 0.3 mm), lifts every foot at least five times, and its tip-measured cadence lands inside 5 to 16 Hz with no commanded step frequency in the theta. The batteries ran 09:35 to 09:50 while main took three default-off engine seams under the probe.

Result. nc1 24, nk1 19. Both batteries 12 of 12 standing and 12 of 12 qualifying. The five discordant seeds are all nc1's: 30011, where nk1 fell, and 30002, 30008, 30010, 30018, where nk1 stood under the floor at 4.27, 4.27, 4.73 and 4.91 Hz. On nc1 those four step at 7.91, 5.00, 5.91 and 6.55 Hz. No seed went the other way. Exact two-sided binomial p on five discordant seeds one way is 0.0625; the clause is a count rule and the p-value is context.

Cadence moved. Median tip cadence over nc1's 24 standing runs is 6.36 Hz against nk1's 5.55 over its 23; paired on the 23 seeds where both stood, nc1 is faster on 14 and slower on 9, median difference +0.91 Hz. Displacement did not: medians 4.15 against 4.11 mm. Final tilt ran 5.78 to 10.77 degrees on nc1, no run near the limit, and every foot lifted at least 6 times on every run. Two runs, 30008 and 30019, read exactly 5.00 Hz at the tip, on the inclusive floor; nk1's own 30004 read the same number on its card. With both removed the count is 22 against 19.

The champion is nc1: ng1's 41 keys unchanged plus body_joint_tau_act_ms 6.0 on the six CTr_pitch joints. It is nk1's sibling, not nk1 plus a joint; the two bodies share 41 keys and differ in which six joints carry the 6 ms. The clip is seed 30011 replayed on the real body, 4.18 mm at 5.73 Hz, the seed where nk1 fell; the whole-CNS activity panel is beside the body.

Interpretation. The coxa-trochanter joint is where the step's lift-off and touch-down live, so a faster activation there shortens the part of the cycle the muscle model was adding to every step, and the fly steps faster; the knee acts inside the swing and the stance and a faster knee changed only whether the stance leg held. That reading is consistent with the numbers and is unmeasured beyond them: one value on each of two joints, and a per-leg read of which leg gained. Entry 49 put the cadence floor on the right hind leg for ng1; whether nc1's gain is that leg's is the first thing to read on its captures.

The bar's own quantity moved for the first time in a title change. Every earlier v3.3 title turned on standing or on seeds; nk1 to nc1 turns on the same seeds with the same falls saved and 0.9 Hz added. Cadence is the sharpest measured gait quantity the project holds (5-16 Hz, Wosnitza and DeAngelis, band frozen), so a change that moves it is the kind the bar was written to find.

Problems. One block of 24, no extension, five discordant seeds: the count is decisive under the clause and thin as evidence about the mechanism. Lane B's confirm is the second read. No flyscore screen ran on this body before the crown; lane D's screen was on nk1, and the seven-metric read on nc1 is open. Two runs sit on the 5.00 Hz floor at the tip instrument's resolution. The tri_index conflict from lane A's CD1-PF (anterior-rule median 0.0001 against the real 0.1606) is now carried unread on a third champion; lane D's tripod_contrast reads the same ng1 runs in band, and which instrument the reference constrains is open. The knee-plus-hip body was not run; whether the two effects add is the obvious next arm and belongs to the lane that built both.

The first tie went to more seeds

Lane B's challenger, the champion ng1 with one added number, a 6 ms muscle activation time constant on the six knee joints where every joint had shared 12.3 ms, tied ng1 19 to 19 on the holder's 24 paired judge seeds at 08:32, the first tie of the record. The ordering clause said a tie keeps the holder, and the engine is deterministic per seed, so a tied challenger could never win a re-match. The judge wrote item 5 at 08:36, drew the next 24 judge seeds, and ran both flies on them. The knee body won 17 to 12, 36 to 31 over 48, and takes the title as nk1.
