Question. Does r23 meet the replacement v3.2 title after standing is measured from body tilt rather than the orientation value that also changes when an upright fly turns?

Predicted (pre-registered, quoted). Both registrations predicted "NOMINATE." Each battery had to produce at least 6/12 standing runs and at least 2/12 qualifying runs. The confirmation seeds were reserved before the nomination ran.

Method (jargon defined inline). A v3.2-standing run ends with mean body tilt below 51.68 degrees, body height above 1.0 and displacement of at least 0.3. A qualifying run must also lift every foot at least five times and step at 5 to 16 Hz. The unchanged r23 theta ran on two independent twelve-seed batteries. The judge then repeated the confirmation arm from its registered commit.

Result (numbers, with variance). The nomination recorded 10/12 standing and 8/12 qualifying. The confirmation recorded 9/12 standing and 9/12 qualifying; the older orientation gate counted only 5/12 standing on those same runs. All twelve judge reruns completed and every scientific per-run field reproduced exactly. Only wall-clock duration differed. r23 therefore takes the v3.2 BANC title with its existing 5.36 Hz record cadence. The open net-speed conflict remains 0.457 mm/s because this pass changed the grading, not the animal.

Same-day path amendment. A preregistered diagnostic then measured the same twelve confirmation runs rather than a separate battery. The nine standing runs covered path at a median 8.80 mm/s, inside the real-fly 2-45 mm/s band, but netted only 0.662 mm/s; median tortuosity was 12.62. The judge repeated all twelve runs and reproduced every scientific field. The champion card now uses these title-seed figures instead of the older 0.457 mm/s and approximate upper-tail tortuosity.

Same-day heading amendment. A second preregistered diagnostic classified the same nine standing runs as WANDERING rather than the predicted CIRCLING. Their median unsmoothed yaw path was 1,226.6 degrees, median absolute net yaw was 61.7 degrees and median yaw efficiency was 0.049. The exact rerun matched. This is a raw-yaw classifier, not proof of grounded planar turns: it samples every 2.5 ms without smoothing and gates runs by final posture rather than simultaneous posture and contact.

Same-day yaw-rate amendment. A third preregistered diagnostic found a median detrended yaw-rate spectral peak of 6.91 Hz with SNR 12.71 across the same nine standing runs; all nine peaks were between 5.28 and 11.46 Hz. The judge's exact rerun matched. The registered STEP_YAW label means only that this power peak lies inside the broad 5-16 Hz title band. No phase, cross-spectrum or coherence against footfalls was measured, so the result does not establish step locking, per-step reversals, cancellation or a steering mechanism.

Same-day gated-yaw amendment. A fourth preregistered diagnostic retained a median 630.4 degrees of yaw path after 25 ms smoothing and simultaneous posture and contact gating. The exact rerun matched. Its submitted median of three reversals is rejected: the counter detects only an adjacent 2.5 ms jump across both sides of a 50 degrees/s deadzone, so it returns zero on a smooth 5 Hz synthetic reversal. A deadzone-hysteresis reanalysis of the same nine traces gives a median of 83 thresholded sign changes. The smoothed angular path is kept; reversal frequency, grounded turning and mechanism remain unresolved.

Same-day coherence amendment. A fifth preregistered diagnostic reproduced on all twelve confirmation seeds with zero errors. Across the nine standing runs, median coherence was 0.103 at the fundamental touchdown cadence. The runner's event series was mislabeled: it detects lift onset, not touchdown. Two standing runs also have yaw peaks at almost exactly twice the cadence. Only weak lift-onset coherence at the fundamental is accepted; actual touchdown, harmonic gait locking, phase and steering remain unresolved.

Interpretation. r23 had already been upright often enough to pass the new bar. The earlier gate confused turning with falling because it used one orientation component instead of the posture axis. The new title does not show that the model improved; it shows that the corrected instrument now measures the behavior the title names.

Problems / what bit us. The same judge pass rejected CD1-MK: its two arms used disjoint seeds, its registered qualifying counts were never computed, and its motor-map patch left 48 knee rows at the old sign. A corrected judge-only rerun produced 0/12 standing, which invokes the registration's unreadable arm instead of rescuing the claim. Lane B's FeCO source search also found no published numerical firing band in its sources, so those encoder rates remain assumed rather than measured.

What changed in the model. Nothing. The r23 theta and default drive path are unchanged. The champion, hall-of-fame and registry records now name the v3.2 title; the calibration ledger now separates qualitative FeCO subtype evidence from assumed numerical rates.

Attribution. Lane B registered and ran both title batteries, the fall closer and the source audit. Lane A exposed the knee-sign question and supplied the rejected CD1-MK attempt. The judge reran the confirmation and repaired the default-off sign capability before ruling.

Video. walker_r23.mp4 is the previously parity-checked r23 clip. It is reused because the theta did not change.

Forward amendment. The knee-sign question named above was answered the same evening, and the answer is worse than this entry anticipated: see entry 37.

the day the instruments got honest

Eight ledger entries, zero new claims about the fly being right, and the most productive day the project has recorded.

Eight ledger entries, zero new claims about the fly being right, and the most productive day the project has recorded. Everything that moved, moved by refutation or repair.

The standing gate could not tell a fall from a turn. Lane B split the gate's single orientation number into tilt and heading and found the gate had been failing upright flies that had merely turned: 25 percent of runs at the live champion, confidence interval 12 to 42 percent, threshold-proof because the tilt distribution has an empty 59 degree gap. Twelve of the fifteen rejected runs meet every other title clause. The fix waits on Robin because the bar text is his. Two behaviors fell out of the same split: the model fly turns, up to 126 degrees net, though nothing was built to make it turn, and it recovers from tilts near 60 degrees, though nothing was built to catch it. The fall story sharpened to early, unrecovered collapse at a median of 1.4 seconds.

The seed guard was blind to prose. Lane A's pre-execution review refused its own runner because the freshness guard handed back a burnt seed block, gap for gap. The audit found 105 seeds silently reused across 22 committed records, none touching a title. Repaired same day; the repair itself misfired once, burning four seeds a packet sentence had described as fresh, and Lane D's preflight caught that too. Three judge defects are recorded in this chain beside the lanes' finds.

Two mechanisms died by their authors' own counter-arguments. Lane A predicted its unaddressed-cell mass was concentrated; it is diffuse, so no small fix exists. It then predicted the descending command saturates into sign-collapse; the command keeps analog range everywhere, so the DNg100 conflict family lost its cheapest explanation. Both counter-arguments were written into the registrations before the runs. Lane D's Q3bv instrument, hardened through five review rounds, died at the one gate no answer-free test can reach, its own terminal ledger write, and the acceptance rules now require naming such gates in advance.

Attribution. Robin set the 45-minute judging cadence, lifted Lane A's spend limit, opened the third animal to Lane E, adopted the discovery-class taxonomy for reports, imported the writing standard, and asked the two questions that both got claimed by lanes within hours: whether the sensory encoding survives the transduction hardware, and whether the emergent turning can probe the compass. The lanes found everything above; the judge verified, merged, and broke three things along the way, each recorded.

The gap inside the gap

Lane B split the current TTM element's 246.26-fold single-impulse force deficit into about 123.1-fold that depends on the exact input/activation and an independent, exact twofold bookkeeping error: a per-leg measurement had been divided across two model sides.

★ A first principle is born here: force mismatches require separate input-transfer and maximum-scale tests
commit 19:00 judge cycleseeds no seed draw; deterministic element tests onlyn six burst durations plus one sustained-drive ceiling arm and default-off controlswall bounded deterministic reference-Mac verification; Lane A's longer CD1-KM run remained live

One enormous discrepancy can hide two ordinary mistakes.

The first measurement was memorable: one 0.1-ms model impulse produced 0.410136 µN against a published 101 ± 4.4 µN twitch from one leg. That is a 246.26-fold gap. But it mixed a question about the chosen input with a question about the equation's maximum scale.

Lane B separated them. Six finite bursts all rose correctly, then relaxed with the same 8.50-ms half-time against the nominal 6.30-ms source interval. A separate sustained drive pushed activation to 0.983047, past the frozen 0.95 gate, yet the one-side ceiling stopped at 50.5 µN. The source's 101-µN anchor was already per leg; the default had divided it between two sides.

So about 123.1-fold of the old gap belongs to this exact impulse and activation choice. The other twofold is independent bookkeeping. Neither number tells us the correct motor-neuron waveform or a biological tetanus-to-twitch ratio, but the model no longer gets to trade one defect against the other.

Lane B built and corrected the instrument. The judge reproduced the frozen gates and accepted only the narrow model-element claim. Lane A's CD1-KM run crossed the deadline still computing, which is exactly why deadlines roll forward: an unfinished registered experiment is not made certain by a clock.

A computation can repeat every event and still fail to repeat its claim.

Both Lane A tables were identical after sorting. So were the blend medians and controller split, and the joint-spread pooled null. Parallel workers returned the rows in different orders, and fixed-index bootstraps turned order into thirteen different interval endpoints across two runners. The preregistrations said exact. We did not round, widen, or explain it away. Both proposals stay outside the ledger until the reducer is deterministic.

The scientific story became smaller anyway. The old global “one fix buys two conflicts” account does not survive the committed path. Left/right asymmetry moves in the opposite direction, although its median distance from the real fly grows 2.277-fold—inside the broad real range, not a new conflict.

Lane B supplied the clean half: 0.10-ms model force onset on both the female and male adapter against a measured 0.93-ms muscle-potential anchor. Two adapters, one model defect, no claim about biological sex.

2026-08-24full standard

The order and the energy

The campaign's oldest question — why does a fly that steps go nowhere — got its mechanistic answer, and the model met real flies for the first time. Travel requires each leg's joints to fire in sequence at least ten milliseconds apart; the wiring can deliver at most about four. The connectome's drive carries more than four times the walking-band energy of the artificial program that walks — the deficit is order, not power. And measured against three thousand real fly recordings, the model now sits inside the real range on all four gait metrics while missing the real median on every one — including stepping in anti-tripod where real flies step in tripod. A day of seventy experiments, eleven withdrawals, a fifteen-agent self-audit, and one instrument fix by the judge that unblocks the next question.

★ A first principle is born here: a lane that audits itself harder than its judge does — five defects confirmed by its own commissioned skeptics, two of its own published verdicts withdrawn, before the judge read a line
commit the evening merge commit of 2026-08-24

Since the day the loop closed, one question has outlived every answer attempted on it: the fly stands, the fly steps, the fly stays. Nineteen mechanisms died on it. A champion was crowned in the middle of it, still lost. Tonight it has a mechanism — not a suspect, an account.

To travel, a leg's joints must move in order: hip, then knee, then ankle, offset by at least ten milliseconds — that number measured by dissecting the artificial program that does walk, and confirmed on five controller lineages. The connectome cannot supply it. Not because the drive is weak: the network's output carries four and a half times the walking-band power of the working program — the energy argument inverted overnight into the sharpest premise correction of the campaign. Because the drive is disordered: signals cross the motor graph in at most two synaptic hops of 1.8 milliseconds each, and nothing measured anywhere in the core — no oscillator among 7,300 scorable neurons, no rhythm in 294 motor rows, no periodicity in the drive tape — stretches that into the tens of milliseconds a gait requires. The oscillator substrate exists, sixteen thousand neurons of it, wired and silent. The network sits in the balanced asynchronous state, and that state — the same one that once saved this model from seizure — may be what forbids its rhythm. That hypothesis is now testable, because the one parameter that controls it was unreachable through an innocent truthiness bug the lane refused to hack around and the judge fixed instead.

The same day, the model met real flies. Three thousand recorded windows, the frozen scorer path, no tuning: the model walks inside the real fly's range on all four gait measures — and misses the real median on all four. It steps a quarter slow. It is nearly twice as asymmetric. And where real flies favour the tripod, the model anti-favours it, beyond its confidence interval, twice. Inside the room, wrong at the table — which is finally a target with coordinates.

The lane also turned fifteen adversarial agents on itself before the judge saw the packet, confirmed five of its own defects, withdrew two published verdicts, and disclosed that its most exciting result — an artificial half-rhythm blended into the connectome's drive restores standing, lifting and travel at once — rests on a script that was never committed and does not rebuild. That result, the one that would close the story, is therefore not in the ledger tonight. The discipline that keeps it out is the same discipline that makes everything else in this entry worth believing.

The first fly at fly cadence

It was crowned over its own failing batteries, reported in full, and over a voided judge battery whose failure turned out to be the judge's instrument, not the fly. ★ A first principle is born here: an instrument that cannot express a ledgered mechanism silently measures a different animal — when a dial is ledgered, every rig that runs thetas must honor it or declare it cannot
commit the coronation commit of 2026-08-24, tagged r23

The throne under bar v3.1 had been vacant since the bar was written. Two flies had cleared v3 on a battery and failed the confirmation; the bar answered by demanding two independent batteries at measured input statistics, and for three days nothing met it.

r23 met it four times.

The story of how starts with a defeat. Lane A spent the evening proving that the bar's own two clauses — stand often, step at fly cadence — trade off against each other across every controller ever built: correlation −0.675, no controller in both clauses, twenty-nine tried. A bar whose clauses oppose each other is not impossible, just narrow: the champion has to live on a ridge. The lane then changed how it searches — re-rank the shortlist on held-out seeds instead of trusting the chamber's maximum — and the candidate that came through was the one ranked third. The re-ranking's own top pick failed both its batteries. The ridge is real.

Then the judging nearly went wrong, in a way worth recording forever. The judge's first confirmation battery came back 4 of 12 — a clear failure — and for a few hours the record read three lane passes, one lane failure, one judge failure. But a champion's row from the lane's own battery would not reproduce on the judge's rig: same parameters, same seed, a standing fly on theirs, a fallen one on the judge's. The cause was not the fly. The judge's battery instrument had never learned to read adh_gain — the foot-adhesion dial, a ledgered mechanism for three days — so it silently ran the champion with the wrong feet. The fix took ten lines and a bit-identity probe; the re-run battery stood 9 of 12, stepping at 5.18 Hz, inside the fly band. The renderer had the mirror gap with the afferent-regularity dial, and its parity gate refused the first champion clip at 3.98 mm against a recorded 4.05 — the gate doing precisely what it was built for.

So the crown rests on four honest batteries out of five, all at measured input regularity, with the one failure printed on the card beside the passes. The champion's cadence clears the band's edge by one to five grid steps. Its true standing rate is about 0.65 against a clause that needs 0.54. It is a marginal champion, crowned by a rule that asks for replication and got it, and every number that argues against it is published in its own record.

And it is lost. The same night, the lane's own audit found that thirty results about the fly's heading had been measured through an estimator that returns confident answers for pure noise — the fly never spiralled, never turned; its body yaw drifts about one degree per run. The results were withdrawn in a block, unedited, and the correction measured properly: the champion walks at fly speed along its path, holds its heading like a compass, and its center of mass simply moves with no preferred direction — backward almost exactly as often as forward. Path speed 9.1 mm/s, inside the real fly's band. Net speed 0.457, twenty times short.

The first fly at fly cadence steps beautifully, faces forward, and arrives nowhere. What is missing is no longer a mystery of mechanics — nineteen proposed mechanisms are dead — but, the connectome accounting now says, mostly an absence: the heading-integration circuitry is 0.4% present in the model's slice of the brain, and the largest missing input to the descending layer is vision, twenty-six times larger than the compass. The throne is filled. The question it was built to force is finally clean: not "why does the fly fall" and not "why is it slow," but "what does it take for a fly that walks to go somewhere."

The space between two flies

★ A first principle is born here: interpolation over intervention — in a space where the outcome lives in parameter combinations, the way to move is between points that work, not along any single dial
commit the evening merge commit of 2026-08-23

For two days Lane A has been killing its own ideas at a rate of one every few hours. Force magnitude correlated with travel at -0.832, survived a strict family-wise correction, and died the moment it was pushed: make the fly push less hard and it travels *less*, not more. The best single parameter, camp_gain, correlated at +0.871 and then a six-fold increase moved travel by less than a fifteen-percent decrease had. Sixteen mechanisms proposed since the campaign opened; sixteen dead, most at the same place — the first time each was asked to move something rather than predict it.

Tonight the pattern itself became the finding. If no single knob moves travel, maybe travel does not live in single knobs. Lane A tested that directly: predict each controller's travel from the *whole* parameter vector of the other fifteen, using nearest neighbours, never letting the model see the arm it grades. It works — rank correlation +0.650 where chance tops out at +0.324, and it still works (+0.579) when every same-family neighbour is banned, so it is the parameters that carry the signal, not the pedigree. The judge rebuilt the entire analysis from scratch and got +0.650 to the third decimal.

Then the sharp part. The best straight line through that space — the measured direction separating good walkers from bad, bootstrap-stable at cosine 0.939 — makes travel *worse* when you step along it. And the midpoint between two working controllers can fail to stand at all, if one endpoint is fragile. Neither of those is a contradiction. Nearest neighbours interpolate among points that exist; a straight line leaves them. The space is not ordered along any line, but between two robust controllers it is locally convex — Lane A proved that too, with a midpoint that stood.

So they built the obvious thing: the midpoint between F23, the champion lineage's stander, and m3-densematch, the furthest-travelling arm that reliably stands. On the lane's twenty-four seeds it travelled 3.55 mm against F23's 2.36 — two-thirds of the way to its target, short of the pre-registered bar, and they refused to move the bar. On the judge's independent twelve, it travelled 4.73 against F23's 2.20 — *past* the bar, past its own target, standing exactly as often as the champion. First constructed parameter set in the campaign to move travel. Both batteries are honest; the seed-block variation between them is itself a measured lesson from this same packet.

The evening's other finding was about us. The lane's chamber runs had been drawing their random seeds from ranges assigned to other seats — three thousand-blocks through the judge's range, then into Lane C's, twenty-four of whose seeds C had already consumed for its permutation nulls. Nobody could see it: C's ledger sat unmerged on its branch, which was the judge's miss, and the judge's own battery two days ago had crossed into C's range as well. No seed was ever reused inside a rig, so no result is contaminated — but a partition nobody's code can read is not a partition. It is now a file, with a block per seat and everything historic closed.

Sixteen dead mechanisms bought a map. The map's first prediction — walk between the points that work — is the first thing in this campaign that worked on the first try, twice.

The fly's step irregularity — the campaign's terminal number — was measured by a detector that had never been shown a rhythmic signal. Lane A fed it ground truth and found it honest at low irregularity, saturating at 0.942, exactly the region every published value sits in. The correction goes the hard way: the true period CV is AT LEAST 1.09–1.74, and the sharpest sentence in the ledger ("this model executes steps and does not repeat them") got stronger. The same audit killed the lane's own newest discovery (the stall population — a memoryless process makes more long intervals than the fly does), found a silent index-crossing that had paired middle legs with hind stances through three experiments, and re-graded four links of the causal chain against real nulls. Ten mechanisms proposed since the campaign began; ten dead; the cause still unnamed. What survives is better instruments, and a nominated pattern one confirmation short: each leg pushing in its own private direction, and no two agreeing.

Lane C, in its second day of existence, closed the problem that blocked everything: which individual eye column each of 6,692 loom-detector inputs belongs to — released cross-brain geometry, two unit-contract bugs caught by registered gates, zero collisions — then rebuilt the visual front end onto the fly's actual measured eyes and ran the frozen pretrained dynamics through it. The reward was a conflict of exactly the right shape: every looming arm drives LPLC2 hard and every one peaks tens of milliseconds after the measured feature, at the wrong visual angle. The computation that makes a fly duck is not a weighted sum of its motion detectors. It hides in the 73% of loom-detector input nobody has mapped yet.

Lane B sat this cycle out — its self-disarmed timer was never re-armed, a seat-liveness gap, not a science one. The throne stays vacant. The judge verified Lane A's bounds from the raw traces and re-ran two of Lane C's audits live; everything reproduced.

The night's chain, each step registered before it ran: the fly is not slow (instantaneous speed 6.1–9.7 mm/s, inside the real band) — it travels 13–19× further than it gets (net/path 0.052–0.073, verified independently by the judge). It is not wandering (heading stable). It is not slipping in a way that matters (halving slip with real friction left speed flat, and a controller re-fitted to grippy feet stands 8/12 on the judge's own seeds). It is not commanded to vibrate (the network orders smooth sweeps; the body reverses 47% of ticks anyway). The joints do what they are told. The plant is not a resonator. What remains: the network executes steps and does not repeat them — per-leg period CV ~0.9 against every structural lever tried (adhesion, load-loop, motor-map boost 14×, denser connectome), none of which moved it.

Inside the network the lane found a real rhythm — 40 motor rows locked to the step cycle, leading movement by 35 ms — and then, in the experiment that defines this project's standard, silenced it against 40 randomly chosen rows and found the costs identical. The rhythm is real, leading, addressed, and functionally inert under the measured motor map. Twenty-six of the lane's own written-in-advance predictions were right, thirty-five wrong, and every wrong one is in the packet with its correction. Lane B, meanwhile, closed a dozen sensory-channel families on legal seeds (claw at rest, club weak on both animals), logged two fresh male-female disagreements, and declared its own instrument family saturated — an honest stop.

The throne stays vacant under the new v3.1 bar. The next thetas are being selected at measured input noise, and the next conflict to close has a name now: make the network repeat itself.

Run metadata: ruling committed d9bac1f, recorded in AGENTS.md as TITLE BAR v3.1; Lane C's first verification pass 619f5c6; the cycle credit 4d8425b. The previous entry (19) left this exact question open — "the judge... has recommended ADOPT to Robin" — and this is how it closed, hours later the same evening.

The question was never whether the fly was good. It was whether the bar could tell. LOADONLY-f36 was nominated by Lane A at 11:29, the first v3 nomination in project history. It then produced one of the strangest records we hold: on three independent 12-seed batteries run under our usual Poisson input noise it MET the bar (lane discovery 8/12 standing + 2 qualifying; lane confirmation 8/12 + 5; the N1 exploratory Poisson arm 6/12 + 4). On the judge's own 12-seed title match, on clean collision-free seeds 30012-30026, it stood 3/12 against a bar of 6 — a FAIL — while still putting 3 qualifying runs on the board. Pooled over five independent batteries the standing rate is 31/60 = 0.52, which is to say it sits almost exactly ON a bar of 0.50. P(<=3 of 12 | p=0.528) = 0.050: the judge's draw is at the unlucky edge of consistent and the lanes' two 8/12s are at the lucky edge. Nobody measured wrong. A 12-seed match cannot decide a rate that sits on its own threshold — the six-seed coin-flip lesson of 2026-08-18, recurring one level up.

The second thing the bar was missing is noise it could defend. The N1 mechanism (registered before any number existed, with the regularity parameter pinned to measured literature values whatever they turned out to be) delivered its anchored run at CV 0.15 (shape 44; Fisch 2012 locust chordotonal homology import — *Drosophila* itself is unmeasured, and that is stated in the anchor report rather than hidden). The pre-registered INVERTED reading fired: standing falls under measured input regularity, in both thetas, -3/12 paired.

theta          Poisson        CV 0.15 (measured)
f23            12/12          9/12
LOADONLY-f36    6/12          3/12

The interpretation was armed before the run: our afferents are strongly suprathreshold, so stochastic facilitation is not the default explanation — model selection adapted to Poisson harshness is. Every champion and chamber in this lineage was selected under noise 5-100x harsher than any measured arthropod afferent, and their balance partially rides on that dither.

Robin ruled at ~21:45, one phrase: "sounds good" — to both of the judge's recommendations. TITLE BAR v3.1, effective for all future title matches:

  1. A crown requires TWO independent 12-seed batteries, each meeting the v3 clause (standing >= 6/12 AND >= 2 qualifying) on its own.
  2. Title matches and confirmations run at the measured afferent regularity: spike_reg k=44 added to the arm's theta at battery time. The theta of record stays the theta; the noise model is a bar CONDITION.

Consequences applied the same night, including the ones that cost. The LOADONLY-f36 nomination is closed without a crown — its three passing batteries are Poisson-conditioned, and its one measured-noise battery stood 3/12. The judge's own earlier proposal, a pre-registered 24-seed Poisson decider, is superseded and cancelled: a decider run under the wrong noise model decides nothing. The throne stays VACANT. Chambers already search at CV 0.15, so the first v3.1 champion will be the first fly in this project both *selected* and *titled* under measurement-supported input statistics.

Nothing is stripped and nothing is re-graded. The three Poisson batteries stand permanently as Poisson-conditioned measurements, tagged as such. And the finding the nomination actually carried is untouched: the sensing contrast (load-only >> double-drive, 7-9 vs 1 per 24) is robust, and the cadence property survived every battery — every standing run in all three Poisson batteries stepped inside the real-fly band (judge card 5.00 / 5.55 / 5.73 Hz, minimum foot lifts 19-21), and under measured noise its median cadence was still in band (4.96 / 5.09 Hz). When this fly stands, it walks at fly cadence. No previous theta has ever done that once; this one does it every time it stays up. What it cannot do reliably is stay up: near-misses cluster right at the gate (uprightness 0.89, 0.89, 0.90, 0.85 on four failing seeds, with displacement 1.7-4.7 mm on all twelve — the fly moves every time and teeters).

Why this is the right way for it to end. Lane A proposed the two-battery rule knowing it would cost Lane A its own candidate. The judge recommended CV 0.15 knowing it would push its own nominee below the line. The guard written into the N1 registration said it in advance: a value that hurts our fly is adopted exactly like one that helps, because *smoothing noise until a title passes would be goalpost-moving in a biology costume*. Tonight was the first time that guard was tested with a crown on the table, and it held.

The third seat's first verification came back clean. Lane C (vision, on Codex, in existence since 16:24 this afternoon) submitted its first work for judging and the judge re-ran the V1 calibration under its own invocation: bit-identical to the committed artifact — DSI 0.6273615510547327, preferred direction 56.235876698617695, median correlation 0.8878353, 2.9 s cached. Artifact-packet agreement was exact across V2 (32/32, 30/32, 8/8, 7/8) and V3 (11/3/0 of 50). The V4 result is the interesting one: an exact six-speed reanalysis of the released FlyVis 1.2.0 checkpoints gives 8 of 50 passing all eight DSI-polarity inequalities, 2 of 50 passing all eight +-45 degree cardinal sectors, the two sets disjoint — 0 of 50 joint survivors. That is scoped precisely as what it is: an engineering block under Lane C's own added gate, explicitly not a refutation of Lappalainen et al. or Maisak et al. Landed in the ledger with that wording verbatim. Consequence: Phase 3 (BANC integration) stays blocked; Phase 2 proceeds by simultaneous task + neural-data ensemble training, to be registered with its freeze list before any training run. One flag carried openly: the V4 gate logic was audited at count level only, and a code-level read happens before any claim built ON that gate enters the ledger.

A new scoreboard entry that is not about the fly. Robin added cycle credit: every cycle report now names which lane provided more value that cycle, value-weighted (false beliefs removed, conflicts opened or closed, programme redirections) rather than volume-weighted. The first award went to Lane A — for a certified false PASS removed, three registry conflicts opened, the bar-instability proof, and the rule proposal that cost it its own candidate; with Lane B's specific excellence named beside it (an entire night programme re-confirmed in-block with no silent re-promotion, the skate ratio on both animals, ~20 honest COLLAPSED verdicts). The structure. Two independent research lanes now work the same repo on separate branches, competing on findings and cooperating through the merge; a judge verifies every claim by re-running it before anything touches this ledger (JUDGING.md). This entry is the first cycle's verdict — and the verdict on the verdict machinery.

Lane A: the fly did not need its own echo. The champion's campaniform sensilla — the leg's strain gauges — were being driven twice, and 80% of what they carried was a copy of the fly's own muscle commands, not ground load (the CD1 finding, registered on this ledger two days ago). Lane A resolved all three registered readings in one night: substituting matched real load for the echo is behaviourally free; the fly stands fine with the echo simply removed; and a two-dial re-search of the load-only stack met its registered bar exactly. Their overnight chamber then produced standing 10/12 with every foot lifting and all six joint ranges in the real-fly bands — the best standing-and-stepping card this project has measured under the all-lifts clause — with cadence unmoved at ~3.5 Hz. The judge re-ran every card: identical to the digit. They also re-measured champion transfer to the third fly on its repaired sensors: still 0/12, WORSE than on the broken file — the no-transfer verdict is about the fly, not the port.

Lane B: cadence passes, and the fly runs in place. Lane B built an "operating female" — graded release on one identified interneuron type, bristle rest rates, named motor-neuron force overlays, all default-off mechanisms that survive the bit-identity probe — whose standing runs pass step frequency (5.32 Hz), swing duration, contralateral phase, every joint range, and R1i — the same-side coordination rule the female had failed on all ten prior standing runs. The cost: standing 2/12, and the fly generates ~13 mm/s of path then cancels it — speed 0.36 mm/s. They also audited the graded hypothesis itself and found the blanket 13A/13B/09A set has no direct adult-fly release evidence — our strongest coordination mechanism is now formally OPEN — and reported two strict registered FAILs of their own hypotheses along the way.

The convergence, which neither lane planned. Lane A gave the fly honest load sensing and got the best standing ever with no cadence. Lane B got cadence and lost translation. The sensing stack is now coherent and the coordination instruments pass — and the fly still cannot do both at once, which is the expressible-envelope conflict answering from two independent directions: the wall is in the body.

Problems / what bit us. Lane A's final rebase orphaned every commit hash its packet cited (contents recovered 1:1, but registration-before-run must not rest on a single evening's push — lanes now push registrations when they make them). Lane A's burned-seed counts were misstated (1,152/~1,050; recount 1,075/1,170 — the finding stands, the seed blocks are genuinely not clean namespaces). Lane B ran its headline card on out-of-block seeds, caught it itself, and pre-registered the in-block repeat before the judge noticed. And the judge's first verification battery crashed on its own import bug before running — even the referee's instruments need instruments.

Attribution. Robin: the lane structure itself, the two-deadline cadence, and the directive that reports reach him where he reads. Lane A (Claude): CD1 end-to-end, the transfer re-measurement, the seed-governance finding. Lane B (Cursor): the operating female, the command-map programme, the graded-evidence audit, two honest FAILs. Judge: verification, the merge, and the rewordings where claims outran evidence.

commit arc 28219c2..HEAD, 2026-08-19theta results-f23-theta.json (verbatim, untuned) on the rebuilt MCNS substrateseeds MCNS first behaviour 9400-9411 (12 fresh, none reused)n 21 research agents; 12 MCNS runs, 6 s eachwall 2026-08-19

Question. Every connection we simulate was found by cutting a fly into 40-nanometre slices and photographing them. Gap junctions, neuropeptides, volume transmission and most of neuromodulation leave no photographable structure. How much causation are we blind to, and is omitting it any different from writing zero?

Predicted (pre-registered, quoted). The brief required each channel to be classified as one of: "(a) modelled as zero DELIBERATELY, with the cost measured; (b) modelled as zero because the mechanism is genuinely negligible for walking on our timescale; (c) modelled as zero SILENTLY, because nobody asked" — and required "unknown" to be a permitted answer, "dressing it up would be the worst outcome of this report."

Method (jargon defined inline). Twenty-one agents with a literature budget, every quantitative claim re-checked by a second agent briefed to refute it, and — the half that mattered — a measurement pass over our own three datasets asking not what the papers say but what *our* simulator currently does with each channel.

Result (numbers, with variance).

Eighteen channels. Five silent zeros nobody had asked about, four deliberate zeros never costed, six genuinely negligible within a six-second walking episode and now argued rather than assumed, and three that are not chemistry at all.

The zero Robin named first — monoamines, the dopamine, serotonin and octopamine neurons our model multiplies by zero because they act through slow metabotropic receptors with no fast sign — costs 571 neurons and 0.755% of the female model's simulated synaptic drive. Real, now measured, and smaller than it feels.

Then the number that reframes the question. We simulate 13.8% of the female's synaptic mass — 5.86 million of 42.3 million — after scoping to the nerve cord and cutting weak edges. And upstream of that, only 18% of BANC's real connections have both partners reconstructed at all. The chemistry zeros are a rounding error against the measurement zero. Any framing that presents 0.755% as our blind spot without that table is misleading, and ours had been.

Two things in our own house were worse than zero. 4,837 glia sit inside the simulated core — 14.7% of it — and 4,221 of them, having no transmitter, take the excitatory default and are instantiated as excitatory neurons. They emit 175 synapses, 0.003%, so the cost is bookkeeping rather than behaviour: "we simulate 33,004 neurons" is wrong by 14.7%, and part of the female-male size gap is glia, not biology. And BANC ships a neuropeptide_verified column on 7,025 neurons that zero lines of code have ever read — 81 of them in the core, 44 of those already muted monoamines: cells whose peptide identity we hold, whose fast sign we set to zero, and whose peptide we never read.

The premise of Robin's question inverted on measurement. On neuron types the males are better annotated than the female — 95.5% and 93.4% against 76.6% inside the rig core — and better on predicted transmitter too. What the male lacks is *confirmed* transmitter, and MANC has exactly zero, which no effort can fix: that column does not exist in the source.

The damage was not empty slots. It was invented values that nothing marked as invented. MCNS names its leg nerves ProLN, MesoLN, MetaLN, where LN is leg nerve. A lost version of our adapter read that L as *left*, filled 3,915 blank-laterality rows with "left", and wrote the same mistake into the strings the simulator parses to assign an afferent to a leg. Measured through the rig's own selectors, before and after the rebuild:

proprioceptors per leg   58 / 275 / 289 / 0 / 0 / 0
                      -> 69 / 135 / 138 / 30 / 140 / 151
load sensors per leg      4 / 4 / 4 / 0 / 0 / 0
                      ->  2 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 2
leg chordotonal groups   claw 0, hook 0, club 550
                      -> claw 93, hook 66, club 432

Three of male #2's six legs were deafferented, and claw and hook — two parameters our own sign test found decisive — were dead knobs on that animal. A search there would have reported them flat, and the flatness would have been a fact about a string.

Worse: the adapter in the repository no longer produced the file the simulator was reading. It would have written a different vocabulary for motor neurons, matching zero rows in silence. The male data could not be regenerated from the code, and the line that fabricated the laterality had no source to fix. It was reconstructed by re-deriving each column from the raw sources and identifying the lost transmitter join by reproducing the shipped file exactly.

Rebuilt, male #2 drove the simulator for the first time. On the female champion's recipe, untuned, twelve fresh seeds: he steps on every one — all six legs, 9 to 19 lifts each on the best — and stands on none, uprightness 0.006 to 0.808 against a gate of 0.90. He is on the floor the whole six seconds. That is 0/12 against a bar of 6/12, so nothing was crowned.

Interpretation. The sharpening this deserves is Robin's own framing, made exact. A zero in a weight matrix is a claim — "this edge exists and carries nothing." An unmodelled mechanism is a confession — "no instrument has looked." Both render as the float 0.0 and the code cannot tell them apart. That is the defect, and it is representational before it is mechanistic. It is also why the male file's fabricated "left" was invisible for weeks while MANC's guesses, which carry a label_guessed flag, were not.

Problems / what bit us. The rebuilt MCNS file carries a guess of its own: 358 of 591 leg chordotonal subtypes are carried across from the female's own cross-matches, at a median type purity of 0.73. It is flagged — 3,963 rows, 1.9% — and it is still a guess. And one verdict on record, "the champion does not transfer to the third fly", was measured on the broken file: three legs deafferented, two dials dead, against two intact flies. That needs re-measuring, not annotating.

What changed in the model. The MCNS adapter is rebuilt with laterality read from the column that covers neurons whose cell body sits outside the imaged volume — which is to say, the afferents — and never from a nerve name. Ten assertions now run at the end of it, every one checking what the rig *selects* rather than what the file contains. The simulator no longer multiplies "we do not know" by zero: a token that asserts ignorance takes the searched unknown path, while a real transmitter our vocabulary lacks stays muted and is counted. And 994 MB of irreplaceable data now sits on a second machine with a manifest labelling every file RAW, DERIVED, DERIVED+GUESSED or DERIVED+FABRICATED — because the last category should not exist, exists once, and is now documented rather than carried.

Attribution. The question is Robin's, and so is the framing this entry is named after: *"is not including them another choice of labeling them zero?"* He also asked the follow-up that found the adapter bug — whether the male datasets have empty slots with no guesses — and funded the literature search that produced the eighteen. The agent measured the exposure, rebuilt the adapter, and reported that the premise inverted.

Video. walker_mc1_first.mp4 — male #2's first behaviour, six hours after he got three legs' worth of sensing back. Not a champion: he steps with all six and never stands up.

commit arc 1f13188..HEAD, 2026-08-19theta results-f23-theta.json throughout (nothing about the fly changed)seeds null-program probe seed 0; cache-collision probe seed 0; F29/F30 chamber seeds as recordedn 42 agents across two adversarial sweeps; ~50 further suspects logged unverifiedwall 2026-08-19, all day

Question. This project has been burned repeatedly by code that produced plausible results while doing something nobody intended. After the fifth such burn we wrote down the heuristics that caught them. The question is whether those heuristics were ever anything more than folklore: how many silent zeros are in here right now?

Predicted (pre-registered, quoted). The sweeps were told to assume every finding was wrong until reproduced, and that "the commonest failure mode in this kind of audit is a finding that is real in the code but unreachable in practice." Both sweeps were required to report what they checked and found clean, on the grounds that an audit which only lists faults implies a coverage it did not achieve.

Method (jargon defined inline). Two adversarial passes, 42 agents, every finding re-measured from scratch by a second agent whose brief was to refute it. The first pass audited the annotation layer — what is empty in each dataset and what the simulator silently substitutes. The second hunted silent-failure classes: dead dials (a parameter that changes nothing is disconnected, not unimportant), cache collisions, selections that match zero rows, numeric rot, instrument faults, and provenance — every constant we call "measured" checked for having been transformed on the way in.

Result (numbers, with variance).

F29 never ran. A chamber whose result we had put in the constraint registry as "0 of 204 candidates reach the coordination gate — not parameter-selectable", and which one of us had cited that same morning as evidence that coordination is mechanism rather than parameters. All 204 evaluations raised the same error: the coordination function was imported inside one helper and referenced inside another, so the gate line could never see it. Each crash printed [n/204] score 0.00 pass 0/3 — character for character what a legitimately non-scoring candidate prints. Withdrawn. Every other chamber checked and clean: 324/324, 132/132, 132/132, 204/204, 204/204, 204/204.

The null program was never shuffling. eval_job.py drives the experiment that asks whether the connectome matters at all — real brain against scrambled ones. It built the shuffled network, filed it in the cache under a float key, and the simulator looked its networks up under a tuple key. The lookup could never hit, so the simulator rebuilt — from a fresh, *unshuffled* re-read of the edge file. Two of the three controls were the real brain, bit-identical to sixteen figures:

shuffle   before the fix        after
none      0.9184682749530796    0.101554076097
post      0.9184682749530796    0.021690900854
weight    0.9184682749530796    0.008671598766
sign      0.4334815501434155    0.142889974922

The sign arm survived only by accident — it scrambles a different argument, which does get passed through. Run as shipped, this would have reported that scrambling the connectome changes nothing: a manufactured refutation of the project's central claim. Nothing had run on it yet.

The root cause was one layer down. The simulator's network cache key was built from parameters only — the neuron table and the edge list, the two things the network is actually built from, appeared nowhere in it. Hand one cache two different brains and the second silently gets the first one's network: measured at 0.918 for both, where a fresh cache gives 0.847 for the shuffled one. Six scripts had each defused this by hand, one of them carrying the comment *"the cache key inside evaluate does not know the connectome, so give each arm its own dict."* Four authors disarmed the same landmine one at a time instead of removing it.

The parity rule was a ritual. Every video is supposed to reproduce its recorded displacement before it ships. The renderer computed that number on one line, printed it on the next, and never referenced it again — no reference value, no comparison, no exit code — while the publisher's docstring claimed it ran "right after the parity check". The one time this caught a wrong render (2.12 mm against a recorded 7.55), it was caught by a human reading a number off a screen. Related, and now tracked: the renderer is a hand-copy of the drive path and is fifteen mechanisms behind it.

And one of the nine was shipped the same day it was found: a new chamber wrote its result under the *previous* round's filename, and crowned its winner on uprightness alone — height was never even stored. The crowned candidate was reported 4/4 standing and is 0/4 under the project's own three-clause gate, heights 0.91, 0.65, 0.74, 0.92.

Interpretation. Not one of these changed a measured walking number. The champion scores, the coordination headline, the title cards all reproduce. What was wrong sat a layer above the numbers — in interpretations, in control premises, and in three experiments that had not yet run. That is the pattern worth naming: a silent zero rarely corrupts the past; it lies in wait for the most important thing you have not done yet. The null program is the experiment this project exists to survive, and it was the one carrying the worst defect.

Problems / what bit us. Three of our own written rules would each have caught F29 alone — *all-zero is infrastructure failure, never behaviour*; *never grep a battery card, read it whole*; *a result that flatters the project deserves the most suspicion* — and none fired, because none of them was in the code. The same lesson arrived twice more the same day. The diary's own cap of three entries a day existed only in conversation, and the moment nobody was watching it produced eight. And a set of runs an audit flagged as silently void turned out to have been pre-registered as sham controls and reported as such — the finding was overstated and was withdrawn, but the narrower defect stood: nothing in the code could tell a deliberate sham from an accidental one, because the registration lived in prose the rig never reads.

What changed in the model. Nothing in the fly. The network cache key now carries the connectome's identity. The null program hands the simulator shuffled *inputs* instead of pre-building. Parity is compared and exits non-zero, and publishing refuses without it. A chamber that scores nothing refuses to crown anything. The simulator announces what it selected, once per process, and asserts that inhibition exists — and, caught within the hour, announces it on stderr, because the first version corrupted a channel another tool parses as JSON. An announcement that breaks a machine-readable channel is its own silent failure.

Attribution. Robin asked the question that started it — "check for any other similar problems we might have overlooked since I haven't actually looked at our data or models" — and it is the reason two of the three most dangerous defects in this entry were found before they ran rather than after they published. The agent built the sweeps, found one of the nine to be a bug it had shipped that afternoon, and withdrew its own overstated finding when the pre-registration turned up.

Fixing our own bug in it revealed that the parameter to carry across was never the gain but the excitation/inhibition balance, and the analytic prediction for it overshot by half. Correct physics costs a leg

We gave the model the synapse it should have had all along — one where excitation and inhibition divide each other instead of cancelling — and the fly stopped walking. Fixing our own bug in it revealed that the parameter to carry across was never the gain but the excitation/inhibition balance, and the analytic prediction for it overshot by half. ★ A first principle is born here: map a model change on the invariant it preserves, not on the parameter it looks like
commit arc 8768020..1f13188theta results-f23-theta.json (champion, unchanged); results-round-f26.json and f28 as controlsseeds CB6/CB7 8600-8611; CB4 8600-8611 both animals; CB5 local search 8601/8604/8607; STD1 9300-9319 (all fresh)n 42 + 72 + 96 + 96 + 141 + 100 runs, 6 s eachwall 2026-08-19, morning to night

Question. Real synapses are conductances: excitation and inhibition arriving together do not cancel before they reach the membrane, they *divide* — the cell's own input resistance collapses and every signal shrinks. Our model cancelled them. We implemented the correct version (true shunting). Does the fly survive it, and do the results we have built on the shortcut survive with it?

Predicted (pre-registered, quoted). Written before the balance runs: "if the silence is a SATURATION (the network pinned high) rather than a hush, motor firing under shunting at the inherited balance will be ABOVE the cancellation baseline, not below — and the analytic bal* will bring both firing and behaviour back toward it. If firing is BELOW baseline, this hypothesis is wrong." And before the 12-seed sweep: "if firing rate is the right invariant to map on, the BEHAVIOURAL optimum sits within ±0.10 of the rate-matched value."

Method (jargon defined inline). Three instruments. A gain sweep, scaling every synapse together. A balance sweep: our network scales inhibitory weights until each neuron's excitation/inhibition weight ratio hits a target (1.10 at the operating point), and this moves that target. And a local re-search over the six network-side parameters, which is what our own cross-model mapping document says should be enough — "tens of evaluations, not hundreds" — if the mapping is right.

Result (numbers, with variance).

The first answer was wrong, and it was our own bug. Turning shunting on silenced the champion completely, a gain sweep found an optimum near 4x with saturation beyond, and that 4x went into map_theta.py as the project's first empirical constant. It lasted about six hours. The inhibitory conductance pool was never decayed — the excitatory one was, one line above it — so it accumulated without bound and pinned every neuron at the inhibitory reversal potential. The tell was a dial pointing the wrong way: more inhibition produced MORE firing, 0.00 → 324 motor spikes per tick, which is impossible. Everything measured under shunting before the fix is withdrawn, the 4x included.

With the mechanism repaired, the registered prediction came in confirmed: shunting at the inherited balance does not hush the network, it saturates it — 148 motor spikes per tick against the cancellation model's 9.3. Weight balance is not current balance. At the measured operating point of −53 mV, excitation drives on 53 mV of driving force while inhibition drives on only 17, so matched weights leave roughly a threefold excess of excitatory current.

That gives an analytic correction with no free parameter — multiply the balance target by 17/53 = 0.32 — and it overshoots, landing at half the reference firing rate. Rate-matching the measured curve gives 0.48:

balance target   1.10    0.90    0.75    0.60    0.53    0.45
motor spikes/tick 148    41.4    24.1    13.0    9.34    7.00
                                      (cancellation model: 9.32)

Twelve seeds put the rate-matched point at 9.34 against a target of 9.32. The pre-registered behavioural optimum landed at 0.60 — inside the ±0.10 window — with standing 9/12, min lifts 6, displacement 2.83 mm, against the cancellation model's 11/12, 5, 2.19. True shunting is affordable.

Then the two results that had to be re-run against a mechanism that actually divides. Coordination survives: graded release under true shunting gives a tripod index of 0.495 median, p = 0.026 against the wave benchmark of 0.302, on 12 of 12 runs — marginally stronger than the 0.485 it scored under the shortcut. Without graded release, shunting gives −0.013: uncoordinated. It is also MDN-specific — the same mechanism driven by DNg100 sits *at* the wave value (0.300, p = 0.79), not above it. MDN direction does not survive, and the re-run says why it was the wrong question: the sign flips with the synapse model (−0.079 without graded release, +0.053 with) and every arm translates under 0.25 mm in six seconds. That is not a direction measurement.

And the cost, which is the sharpest thing here. A local re-search from the mapped point — 47 evaluations, exactly what the mapping document budgets — never once produced a run in which all six legs stepped: min lifts was 0 in 112 of 141 runs. Running three known-good recipes with and without the mechanism, on the same seeds, min lifts is 4 to 21 without it and 0 in every single run with it, while cadence stays in band at 4–6 Hz. The fly still steps rhythmically. It has stopped lifting at least one leg. A factorial says conductance synapses alone are free (min lifts 13, 4, 7) and shunting is where legs start dying — and the failure is lateralised: left legs 13/7/2 while right legs hold at 23/21/21.

F30, the first search ever run on the physics we believe — conductance synapses, true shunting and graded release on every one of 220 candidates, balance free around the mapped value — scored zero.

Interpretation. The champion is tuned to a simplified synapse and does not survive being made more realistic. That is what you would expect if its parameters had been quietly compensating for the missing physics all along, and it is the honest reading: we did not lose a good fly, we found out what the good fly was standing on. The mapping idea itself came out better than it went in — the analytic term has the right sign and the wrong size, and the invariant worth carrying across a model change is the network's firing rate, not any parameter that looks like the one you changed.

Problems / what bit us. The 4x constant is the second claim this project has published and withdrawn within a day, and both times the catch was the same heuristic rather than a code review. Worth stating plainly: a dial that moves the wrong way is a bug, and it is the only alarm that fires before the result looks plausible. Separately, a mechanism that looked like a champion-maker — short-term synaptic depression, implemented since the beginning and never wired into the drive path at all — was reported at 7/20 → 18/20 standing and did not replicate: on 20 fresh paired seeds, 16/20 against 15/20, McNemar p = 0.75, and monotonically harmful above that (4/20 at U 0.05, 0/20 at 0.08). Zero qualifying runs in all 100. Refuted as registered.

What changed in the model. cns.py decays both conductance pools. map_theta.py carries a measured balance factor of 0.48 with the analytic 0.32 recorded as a lower bound. walk_search.py gains bal_target, w_syn_scale and std_U, each in the network cache key. The champion is unchanged and the probe is bit-identical throughout.

Attribution. Robin asked for the most nature-accurate outcome first and approved the graded-synapse set that makes the coordination arm possible. The agent implemented shunting, shipped the decay bug in it, caught it by its own wrong-way rule, withdrew the constant it had published that morning, and re-ran both load-bearing results against the repaired mechanism rather than leaving them resting on the shortcut.

Video. walker_mc1_first.mp4 — not this arc's fly, but the day's only new footage: male #2's first behaviour, and the first render in this project's history whose parity was checked by the machine rather than by a human reading a printed number.

2026-08-18 The second fly — a statue, a bug, real steps, and a crawl ★ posture as a measured quantity2 videos We ran the female champion's exact parameters on a second individual's wiring, a male, and announced perfect transfer of posture. It was a bug — an empty string where a null belonged had deleted every inhibitory synapse, and the statue was rigidity, not balance. Repaired, the male stepped in twelve runs out of twelve, which is the real and humbler transfer result. Then Robin watched the footage and said he was crawling. It was a bug — an empty string where a null belonged had deleted every inhibitory synapse, and the statue was rigidity, not balance. Question. Everything this project ever simulated ran on one individual fly's wiring. A second complete fly cord exists — MANC, a male. If we translate it into our rig's language and run the champion's exact parameters, does anything transfer? And if he can be made to move, can he earn a title of his own?

Predicted (pre-registered, quoted). "MW1 WALKS: standing >= 2/6 AND >= 1 standing run with all-feet lifts >= 5 -> the walking recipe TRANSFERS. Committed before any seed ran, and left unchanged when the runs were repeated after the bug. Later the same night, a second and separate registration, written before the measure existed: the new posture measure's band is [0, 0.05], and "the prediction is on record before the batteries run: the female champion passes, the male winner conflicts."

Method (jargon defined inline). A one-file adapter translates MANC into BANC's schema so the entire rig runs unchanged — every join count-verified: 23,188 traced neurons, 692,208 connections at our conserved-core cut, 307 motor neurons covering all 42 joints, the FeCO sensor subtypes matched by name, MDN present natively, DNg100 found via the published cross-individual cell matches. One honest asymmetry carried loudly: MANC annotates only 8 leg load sensors where BANC annotates 573, so a second arm rescaled the load gain by exactly that ratio — a declared dataset correction, not a fit. Later, *round M1* = the male's own search chamber (candidates scored on stand-and-step displacement across 4 seeds), then a *battery* — the fixed panel of published-fly constraints — on six seeds the chamber never touched. Then a posture audit: a render that reports, tick by tick, which body part is touching the floor and what share of ground force it carries. Then a new battery measure, nonfoot = the fraction of post-transient ticks in which any proximal leg segment (coxa, femur, tibia) or the body itself touches the ground.

Result — the part that was wrong. First light gave standing 12 of 12, both arms: the male fly, on a female-fitted recipe he had never seen, standing more reliably than the female champion stands herself (her record: 3 of 6). Steps taken: zero, in every run; the load-channel correction changed nothing, acquitting that asymmetry as the blocker. We announced that the posture solution is about fly cords, not this fly's cord.

⚠️ WITHDRAWN, same day. The adapter had filled the "verified transmitter" column with empty text instead of leaving it null. The simulator, reasonably, prefers verified over predicted whenever the field is filled — so empty text silently beat every real prediction, every male neuron fell back to the default excitatory sign, and the male cord ran without a single inhibitory synapse. A brain with no brakes saturates: every motor neuron pinned near its firing ceiling. The 12/12 was co-contraction rigidity, not balance. Withdrawn with it: the collapse at the degree-matched cut, and the density diagnosis as mechanism. The first video stays, with this note attached — we do not polish the past.

How it was caught. Three dials in a row did nothing: synapse gain (6x range, ~flat), then the balance rule (8x range, EXACTLY flat — identical to the decimal). A flat dial is a broken wire. We verified the dial worked on the female (20x swing), concluded the male truly could not respond, asked what makes balance powerless — and the answer is "when there is nothing inhibitory to scale." The human's laugh ("the male looks paralyzed, why?") started the whole chain. With inhibition restored the male fires at 24-29 motor spikes per tick, about 5x the female's level, in the tameable range.

Result — the part that stands. Repeated on fresh seeds with the bug fixed: formally MW3 — standing 1/6 misses the bar, recorded without spin. Materially, everything changed. Every one of twelve runs steps (worst-leg lifts 2-14; displacements 1.4-4.9 mm) where the broken male had zero motion of any kind. Seed 925 delivered his first genuine standing walk: 3.07 mm at upright 0.93, every foot lifting 9-22 times — parity-exact on video. The corrected transfer claim is humbler and more interesting than the withdrawn one: the stepping machinery engages across individuals — a recipe fitted to one fly's wiring drives rhythmic, all-legs stepping on another fly's wiring, twelve times out of twelve. What does not transfer is the balance margin: he steps like her early ancestors did, falling as he goes. The load-sensor asymmetry was tested again and again changed nothing — acquitted twice.

Result — his own search, and the crawl. M1's winner measured standing 1/6 — a clear title FAIL. Conflicts on his card: cadence 2.45, swing 70 ms, speed 0.25, min lifts 3, contralateral at the boundary. Per-seed, the other five never stood: 931: 0.71 mm, upright 0.95 | 932: 3.57, 0.87 | 933: 0.59, 0.07 | 934: 3.02, 0.10 | 935: 2.15, 0.72. The chamber also voted internally, and the votes are worth recording: the microscope-matched threshold (cut >= 30) scored 19 of 27 against cut >= 10's 8, even though a cut-10 candidate won the final rerank; and the artificial command neuron DNg100 beat the male's native MDN 22 to 27.

Then the audit. Share of ground force, and fraction of ticks touching, female champion seed 824 versus male M1 seed 930: foot tip 96.9% / 100.0% vs 76.1% / 88.8%; rest of the foot 3.1% / 49.6% vs 16.5% / 87.5%; proximal leg 0.0% / 0.0% vs 2.6% / 20.5%; body 0.0% / 0.2% vs 4.7% / 23.0%. He stands lower too (z 1.10 vs 1.26). On fresh seeds the registered prediction came in confirmed on both arms. Female nonfoot 0.000 — every one of her twelve runs at or below 0.004, including the ones where she falls — PASS with total margin. Male 0.436 median, spanning 0.32 to 0.52 across all of his: CONFLICT, and worse than the single audit exemplar had suggested. Per-seed, male: 936: 0.5155 | 937: 0.4359 | 938: 0.4595 | 940: 0.4991 | 941: 0.3159 | 942: 0.3636. And his signature replicated: R1i on 2 of 3 fresh standing runs at p < 0.05 (0.005, 0.030; the third 0.070) — battery PASS. Across both his batteries, 3 of 4 standing runs significant. Across both of hers, 0 of 4, p-values 0.73 to 0.83.

Interpretation. Two things separate these animals now, and they are different in kind. The R1i split is a disagreement between individuals that keeps replicating — a first-class result under the two-fly rule, tagged MALE-ONLY pass / FEMALE-ONLY fail. The posture split is a conflict with the real world: real flies bear their weight on their tarsi. He stands, but he does not stand on his feet, and he grazes the floor with body or shin about 44% of the time against her never. That is the sharpest cross-individual difference we have measured, and it is a constraint we now have to satisfy rather than a curiosity. The project's oldest fault line, the stand/walk divide, has also reappeared at a new scale: across individuals.

Problems / what bit us.

  1. An empty string is not a null. A flat dial is a broken wire. And a result that flatters the project ("perfect cross-individual transfer!") deserves the most suspicion precisely because it flatters.
  2. The body model has no self-collision. All 55 contact pairs in the compiled physics are part-versus-ground; zero are fly-versus-fly. Legs passing through the abdomen has been legal physics in every video ever rendered here, for both animals. Adding self-collision would change the physics under every existing result, so it is a registrable decision, not a patch — recorded, not done.
  3. The standing gate is blind to posture. It checks height and uprightness only, so a fly propped on its tibiae at altitude passes it. That hole existed for the whole project and was found by a human watching a video, not by any test.
  4. A deviation from the registration, recorded plainly: it promised a same-seed re-run, and the battery's own fresh-seed discipline silently picked fresh seeds instead. Accepted as the better evidence, the overwritten title files restored from git untouched, and said out loud rather than tidied away.
  5. The renderer had the connectome name hard-coded into the new video banner ("BANC female") and the data paths hard-coded too — both caught before the first male frame shipped a wrong label. 84 male motor neurons carry only generic muscle labels and stay unmapped; 62 more lacked resolvable targets. These gaps are carried, not hidden.

What changed in the model. Nothing in the fly, twice over — that is the headline: the SAME code and physiology now runs two individuals, and the repo gains the male core as a first-class substrate. The instrument gained render_split --contacts (parity-gated: 1.35/0.97 and 7.08/0.97 reproduce the records exactly) and the battery gained nonfoot, band [0, 0.05], scored on every run from now on. The rig change is capture-only and the PROBE re-verified bit-identical [1.268453802823, 1.268453802823, 0.990248627778, 1.149806329417].

The scoreboard was the problem

Three times in one day we went looking for a better fly and found a broken scoreboard instead. Six-seed titles turned out to be coin flips, so verdicts became rates on twelve dice. The search had been scoring distance while the title measured balance, so eight straight collapses were an objective mismatch and not variance — fixing it produced the first championship change in this project's history. And every chamber ever run had picked the slowest joint it was offered, because we scored standing and a slow joint is a stable joint. Score cadence instead and the search walks to 30.1 Hz, within 1.3 Hz of a number measured in fly muscle by a completely independent road.

★ A first principle is born here: an objective mismatch looks exactly like variance until you fix it — and a search cannot walk toward something you never scored

Question. Three questions, and they turned out to be one. Is six seeds enough to decide a title? Eight times a chamber winner had been reranked, looked strong, and then failed its title battery — is that variance we have not beaten, or are the chamber and the title measuring different things? And why does every chamber we run, given any range of joint frequency, pick the slowest value in it?

Predicted (pre-registered, quoted). Each fix registered before it ran. On power: "both animals sit at 4/12 standing on all seeds graded to date, so the likeliest result is that NEITHER holds a title tonight... Recorded before the runs so a double failure cannot be quietly reframed." On the objective: "if the objective was the problem, F23's winner should hold its rate into the twelve-dice match where seven predecessors did not... A chamber rate of 0.7-0.87 predicts roughly 8-10 of 12; anything near 4/12 says the collapses are variance we have not beaten." On cadence, three branches: "Gates were the constraint if the winner's f0 rises well above 15 AND its battery cadence enters band... Hard trade if candidates score but standing collapses — the body cannot do both... Body indicted if NOTHING ever scores."

---

1. Six dice were a coin flip

Method. The trigger was an accident. The posture re-runs of the second-fly work drew fresh seeds for both animals, and on those dice the two flies effectively swapped outcomes: the male's fresh battery came out standing 3/6 with two runs clearing all-feet lifts >= 5 (seed 937 min 6, seed 938 min 7) — which would have *met* the title bar his own battery had failed at 1/6. The female champion's fresh battery came out standing 1/6, speed 0.25 — which would have *failed* the form that titled her at 3/6, speed 1.03. Neither of those grants or removes anything: grading a bar on a battery that ran for another purpose is the forking-paths error, and the rule that protects her title is the same rule that denies him his. What the swap measures is the instrument. So: TITLE MATCH v2 — twelve fresh seeds per match, picked by the used-seeds discipline, verdicts as rates against one universal bar, standing >= 6/12 AND >= 2 standing runs with all-feet lifts >= 5. The old six-seed bars carried across at identical proportions, so the goalposts moved for statistical power, not for difficulty.

Result. The female p150 champion, seeds 838-865: standing 6/12 — the bar to the digit — TITLE DEFENDED, by the narrowest margin the protocol allows, all six standing runs qualifying on lifts (worst 7). Per seed (mm, upright, min lifts): 838: 4.24, 0.87, fell | 839: 2.20, 0.29, fell | 848: 3.09, 0.71, fell | 849: 1.52, 0.83, fell | 858: 3.93, 0.95, 10 | 859: 2.29, 0.96, 14 | 860: 3.00, 0.98, 11 | 861: 2.15, 0.99, 12 | 862: 2.89, 0.78, fell | 863: 4.58, 0.91, 7 | 864: 3.77, 0.96, 10 | 865: 3.87, 0.02, fell. Her fresh card: nonfoot 0.001 PASS, all six joint ranges PASS, R5 6/6, R1c 4/6 — and R1i 0/6, taking her lifetime to 0 of 10 standing runs on the same-side rule. An honest downgrade came with it: her median speed here is 0.62, so the 1.03 that titled her was seed-lucky and the lower number is the real one. The male M1 winner, seeds 943-954: standing 3/12 — FAIL. He met the other half of the bar (943 min lift 5, 949 min lift 8) and his signature held a third time: R1i significant on 2 of 3 standing runs (0.025, 0.005), lifetime 5 of 7 against her 0 of 10. His nonfoot came in at 0.458, the fourth consecutive reading in the 0.44-0.46 band: a stable trait of this animal, not noise.

The pre-registered pessimism was half wrong, recorded as such: the throne did not empty. What it cost is the point — with per-seed standing rates around 25-50%, a six-seed battery is a coin flip, and we had been reading titles off coin flips in both directions without knowing it. It took an accidental redraw that flipped *both* animals at once to make it undeniable.

---

2. The chamber and the title were measuring different things

Method (jargon defined inline). A chamber is one parameter search: N candidates x a few seeds -> top 10 -> rerank on fresh seeds -> one winner. A title match is a separate 12-fresh-seed battery graded on the CEO's bar. Historically the chamber scored distance x coordination and the title scored the rate of qualifying standing runs — two different quantities, and nobody had said so out loud. F22 was the last chamber run the old way. F23 changed one thing: the chamber's per-seed score is 1.0 only if the run passes the title's own gate (upright > 0.90, height > 1.0, displacement >= 0.3) and lifts every foot at least 5 times. Distance survives only as a 0.02-per-mm tiebreak that can never outrank a qualifying run. Budget was rebalanced from breadth to power — 130 candidates x 6 seeds instead of 320 x 3 — because a rate cannot be estimated from three dice.

Result. F22 first, because it is the cleanest statement of the problem. Chamber top scores 4.03, 3.94, 3.88 — the highest any female chamber had ever produced, against M2's best of 2.67. Title match, 12 fresh seeds (2100-2113): standing 4/12 — FAIL against a bar of 6. Card otherwise strong (6/6 ROMs, min lifts 8, R5 4/4, nonfoot 0.036, swing 35.6 PASS), conflicts on duty 0.86, cadence 3.41, speed 0.54, R1i 0/4. The eighth rerank-to-battery collapse. Put those two numbers side by side — highest chamber score ever recorded, standing rate below the champion's — and the instrument problem is undeniable. Fast joints buy distance, so F22 climbed its own objective while sliding on the one that decides titles.

F23, scoring the right thing: top chamber scores 0.87, 0.86, 0.85 — those candidates stood *and* stepped on 5 of 6 seeds, against the reigning champion's measured 6/12 = 0.50. Every one of the top six sits at f0 15-18, so the fast joint is not being tolerated for distance's sake; it survives when the objective is balance. Title match, 12 fresh seeds: standing 8/12, qualifying runs 7 — inside the predicted window.

The eight collapses were an objective mismatch, not variance. The crown was then decided by a paired decider, registered before it ran, on the same 12 fresh seeds for both flies:

The registered rule — strictly exceed, ties keep the crown — fired as written. f23 is champion: the first championship change in this project's history, its 8/12 replicated across two independent 12-seed batteries.

Stated plainly, because a card must not flatter its winner: f23 wins only on how often it stays up. Qualifying runs tie 5-5. It is *slower* than the fly it replaced. And its nonfoot score was 0.137 against p150's 0.001 — part of its standing advantage looked like it was bought exactly the way the posture measure was invented to detect. Under the rules as registered that does not block the title, and changing a bar mid-contest to exclude one specific challenger is the goalpost-moving this project forbids. So the same night produced a championship and the evidence that the championship rule is incomplete.

Then Robin watched the video: *"it's just the back legs which are pointing back and grazing the floor. otherwise pretty good."* Both halves checked out, and together they downgraded the fly's flaw and convicted the instrument. The per-leg contact audit (same drive path, parity 1.85 mm exact): foot tips carry ~95% of ground force; mid-foot segments ~4%; the body 0.8% of force but 12.7% of ticks; the hind legs' proximal segments 0.0% of force. "It drags", written into the ledger the night before, is too harsh and was corrected. The second half of his read is also numerically true — mean fore/aft position as a percentage of each leg's own range: front 28.7 / 32.4, middle 38.1 / 39.5, hind 55.7 / 72.2 — which fits the mechanism: hind legs retracted, nothing supports the rear, abdomen drops until it grazes. We have no real-fly reference for resting joint angle, so this is a within-model asymmetry, not yet a conflict, and it is now on the hunt list. nonfoot had been scoring a weightless graze identically to a fly resting on its belly, so evaluate() now records non-foot ground force as well as tick count:

f23, its own 12 title seeds:  nonfoot ticks 0.137  CONFLICT
