The champion carries 99.0% of its weight on its feet. The flaw published the night before was real and 14x smaller than reported. If posture joins the title bar it should be the force measure — that is the definition which separates "grazes the floor" from "is not standing on its legs".

---

3. Every chamber picked the slowest joint it was offered

Method. F22 and F23 were offered f0 in [15, 36] and both chose 15.0. M5 was offered [6, 36] and chose 6.0. M2 chose 8.57. Five chambers, one behaviour — and our own envelope measurement says the muscle interface clips 71% of certified-tripod stepping demand at f0 10.5, so the searches reliably settle exactly where real stepping is physically inexpressible. The proposed mechanism is a loop in our own method: standing is what we score -> a slow joint is a stable joint -> stability arrives before speed does -> the hill-climb never leaves. F25 is the F23 rate-scored chamber with exactly one change: a candidate's per-seed score is 1.0 only if the run stands AND lifts every foot >= 5 times AND its tip-measured step rate falls inside the real-fly band 5-16 Hz (cadence = steps per second a foot actually takes; the band is frozen from Wosnitza 2013 / DeAngelis 2019 and was set long before this experiment). f0 left free over [6, 36] precisely so the winner's choice *is* the readout.

Result.

chamber              f0 range offered   f0 CHOSEN
M2   (distance)          [6, 36]           8.57
M5   (rate)              [6, 36]           6.00   <- floor
F22  (distance)         [15, 36]          15.00   <- floor
F23  (rate)             [15, 36]          15.00   <- floor
F25  (rate + CADENCE)    [6, 36]          23.94
     its 16 scorers: median 27.3, range 19.0-36.0
     (the space offered a median of 22.6, so this is not sampling)

Every previous chamber sat on the floor of whatever range it was given. F25 abandoned the floor entirely. Gait conflicts we had carried for weeks are simply gone: step frequency 5.14 Hz PASS (previously 3.05-4.14, the first ever pass), swing 25.0 ms PASS, duty 0.81 PASS, contralateral phase 0.43 PASS, 6/6 ROMs PASS, all-feet lifts min 15 PASS, posture-by-force 0.007 PASS. The price is the other pre-registered branch at the same time: standing 2/12. So the honest verdict is *both* outcomes — the gates were the constraint and there is a real trade at this body's parameters.

Robin's decision, the same evening: *"we should go for real fly cadence 100% it's not impossible to get a model that works like a real fly and to get that model working so we should do it."* Title bar v3: a run qualifies only if it stands AND lifts every foot >= 5 times AND steps inside 5-16 Hz; a theta takes the title only with standing >= 6/12 and >= 2 qualifying runs on 12 fresh seeds. Nothing was weakened — the standing clause is unchanged and cadence is *added*. f23 stays champion of record under v2 (won fairly; no retroactive stripping) and the v3 throne is declared vacant.

That immediately created a debt, caught before it could bite. F25's winner had chosen zeta 0.86 — underdamped, and this project's own tier-0 caution says a resonant limb can manufacture a rhythm with no connectome in it. F26 was registered to ask whether the cadence win survives overdamping:

chamber   zeta allowed   scorers    scorer f0 (median, range)   top score
F25        0.6 - 1.2    16 / 132     27.3   (19.0 - 36.0)         0.36
F26        1.0 - 1.2    33 / 204     30.1   (21.9 - 36.0)         0.58
                        (16% vs 12%)   zeta median 1.07

Cadence-passing candidates are more common at safe damping, not less, and they score higher. The shuffle debt registered two hours earlier is discharged by construction — no cadence claim now rests on underdamping.

And then the convergence, which is the part worth pausing on. Azevedo's measured 8.5 ms spike-to-half-max-force, read as a critically damped second-order step, implies a plant ringing at 31.4 Hz. Told only "stand, lift every foot, step at 5-16 Hz", with joint frequency free over [6, 36] and no knowledge of that number anywhere in its objective, the search settled at a median of 30.1 Hz. A muscle physiology measurement and a behavioural search, arriving within 1.3 Hz of each other. Our previous champions all sat at 8.6-15.

F26 vs bar v3, 12 fresh seeds, graded exactly as the CEO wrote it: standing 3/12 (bar >= 6) FAIL, qualifying runs 2 (bar >= 2) MET. No v3 champion; the throne stays vacant, as registered. But the card is the best this project has produced on every axis except standing: cadence 5.00 PASS, swing 27.5 PASS, duty 0.77 PASS, contra 0.45 PASS, 6/6 ROMs PASS, min lifts 10 PASS, both posture measures PASS (ticks 0.039, force 0.004), R1c 2/3, R5 3/3 — nine PASSes against two conflicts (standing rate, speed) and one R1i failure. Its best run's 1.21 mm/s is the highest standing speed ever measured here. Seed 5113 missed qualifying by 0.09 Hz.

---

Interpretation. All three fixes are the same lesson at three depths: what you score is what you get, and what you grade on is what you can know. Power first — a verdict read off six dice is not a verdict. Then alignment — a search that optimises something other than the bar will keep producing winners that fail the bar, and it will look exactly like variance while it does it. Then coverage — a search cannot walk toward a property that appears nowhere in its objective, and five chambers sitting on the floor of five different ranges was our own scoreboard talking back to us, not the connectome.

The trade is now precisely quantified rather than vaguely felt: at the measured joint frequency the fly walks like a fly and falls two thirds of the time; at slow joints it stands like a statue and cannot step. Two chambers have searched everything in between. And the failure column has a shape: the non-standing seeds split into total collapses (upright 0.05, essentially all contact non-foot) and near-misses that keep clean posture. This is not a fly that walks badly; it is a fly that either walks or falls over. Every pre-F25 champion was also selected inside a region the muscle measurement excludes — that strips no title, but the lineage is now documented as a stability lineage.

Problems / what bit us. Her titled speed of 1.03 mm/s, quoted in entry 9, is now known to be a lucky draw around an honest 0.62; nothing is edited backwards, this is the forward correction. The cadence gate makes scorers rare (12-16% of candidates), so a search scoring a conjunction of three gates spends most of its evaluations on zeros. And the sharpest open risk is stated in F27's own registration: if winners ever cluster at high inhibition with low cadence, the search is buying standing by suppressing movement, and the right response is to strengthen the gate rather than believe the result.

What changed in the model. Nothing in the fly's physiology; everything in how it is searched and judged. Twelve fresh seeds, rate verdicts, one universal bar per animal. Chambers now score the title criterion directly. The posture instrument is force-weighted and reported in both forms permanently. Lineage: t025 -> p150 (phasic transduction) -> f23 (fast joint + rate-scored search), tagged FEMALE-ONLY. And cns.SimParams gains premotor_inh_gain / premotor_inh_rows: a multiplier on the inhibitory output of the leg neuromere's own inhibitory premotor populations — hemilineages 13A and 21A, 874 rows in the walking core, the exact cells the lesion work named as the cord's balance machinery, and which no search had ever been allowed to touch. Default 1.0 with an empty row set is bit-identical, probe re-verified at [1.268453802823, 1.268453802823, 0.990248627778, 1.149806329417]. Per the convention that a new dial must demonstrably respond, the manipulation test ran *before* any search (F26 winner, seed 5100, 3 s):

inh_gain 0.5   displacement 4.57 mm   upright 0.19  (falls)
inh_gain 1.0   displacement 1.77 mm   upright 0.98
inh_gain 2.0   displacement 1.02 mm   upright 0.98

Weaker inhibition buys movement and loses balance; stronger buys balance and loses movement. That is the stand/walk trade itself, with a knob on it — and the knob is a real population of real inhibitory cells rather than an abstract gain.

Attribution. The CEO decision on cadence is the hinge, and it went against the project's own short-term interest: adding cadence to the title bar guaranteed the reigning champion's successor would be harder to crown and the throne would sit empty. Robin took it anyway, in one sentence, on the F25 evidence — a fly that stands still is not a fly. He also approved the power fix ("do it") and the M2 launch ("run it"), and asked mid-run "what is F22 and F23?", which is why the naming convention is now pinned in the ledger: if the CEO has to ask, it is not a name, it is a private code. His video catch is the whole back half of section 2 — an agent reading its own number would have kept "the champion drags" in the record, because the number said 0.137 and the number was measuring the wrong thing. The agent measured the coin flip in both directions, designed the rate-scored and cadence-gated objectives, registered every prediction and the decider rule before running them, caught its own underdamping debt at the moment of the CEO's decision rather than after publishing a cadence claim, ran the contact audit, and built and probed the inhibition parameter.

Video. Video 18 is the f23 championship footage (parity 1.85 mm exact); video 20 is F25's seed 5007 (parity 2.39 mm exact, 21-33 lifts per leg) — the first fly here ever to step at real-fly cadence. Neither source render lives in this repo; both rows and their parity numbers are in VIDEOS.md.

The wall was in the body

A female recipe stood on 9 of 12 seeds — the highest rate this project has ever measured — and still took no title, because she barely stepped. Chasing why led out of the nervous system entirely: play a certified tripod gait through our own muscle interface and 70.9% of what it asks for is out of range. ★ A first principle is born here: the expressible envelope — a body can be too slow to be asked
commit df5333d (arc 56353fb..df5333d)theta results-p150-theta.json (female champion p150); results-walk-search-m2.json winner (male)seeds FTP1 title 866-879; f0 dose 7 doses x 6 seeds; p150@f0-15 title 880-892; paired decider 2012-2027 (identical for both arms)n 12 + 42 + 12 + 24 runs, 6 s each, plus two analytic sweeps with no simulation in themwall dawn to midday, 2026-08-18

Question. Every fly we have built either stands or steps, never both. We had been treating that as a nervous-system problem — the wrong wiring, the wrong gains, the wrong search. Is it?

Predicted (pre-registered, quoted). The envelope entry registered a two-way split before the dose was run: "TRADE outcome = speed rises with f0 AND standing falls -> the stand/walk trade IS the f0 axis... BLIND-SPOT outcome = speed rises and standing HOLDS -> the searches never exploited high f0 (displacement scoring crowns the first stable creeper) and a better champion sits unclaimed INSIDE the existing space."

Method (jargon defined inline). Three instruments, in order.

*The certified-tripod probe.* Take flygym's own CPG walking program — a tripod gait by construction, nothing of ours in it — and play it through our full execution stack (muscle activation, joint, actuator) at champion parameters. If the stack is faithful, a tripod goes in and a tripod comes out.

*The envelope decomposition* (envelope1.py, analytic, no simulation). Our joint is a second-order plant with a natural frequency f0 — how fast it can ring — and a damping ratio zeta (below 1 it overshoots and rings; at or above 1 it does not). To make a joint reach a commanded angle the controller has to invert the plant, which costs theta_eq = theta + (acc + 2*zeta*w0*vel)/w0^2. Both correction terms scale as 1/f0². A slow joint needs an enormous fictitious equilibrium angle to produce an ordinary fast movement, and the actuator simply cannot be sent there — the demand is clipped.

*The f0 dose* (envelope2.py): move that one number across seven values, hold everything else, both animals, 6 seeds each, graded by the same battery gates as a title match.

Result (numbers, with variance).

The record-holder first. FTP1's winner, 12 fresh seeds (866-879): standing 9/12 — the highest rate ever measured here (the reigning champion p150 defends at 6/12), nonfoot 0.000 on every run, R5 9/9. And all-feet qualifying runs 1/12 against a bar of 2: FAIL. Duty 0.93, cadence 1.73 Hz, speed 0.33 mm/s, front-leg ROMs shrunken, adhesion threshold 2.95 — 2.4x the champion's. She stands superbly by barely stepping, leaning on her feet sticking to the floor. The night's triptych: the male steps beautifully and cannot stay up (~33% standing, invariant across three different search objectives); this female stays up beautifully and barely steps; p150 is the only recipe holding both clauses at once.

Then the probe, and it was the same on all 4 seeds because playback is deterministic (n=1 would have done): disp 11.80 mm, upright 0.99, per-leg lifts [0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 1] — a fast, stable skater, with essentially no swing events at all. Tripod in, skater out. The cause prints at the top of the log: the inversion reports 70.9% of the program's flex/extension demand OUT OF RANGE.

The decomposition says why. At the champion's own f0 of 10.5 Hz, the certified tripod program demands a median |acceleration term| of 25.2 deg against a median joint half-range of 14.0 deg — the correction *alone* is 1.8x the entire range before the movement itself is added; 99th percentile ratio 12.8. Out-of-range against f0, for that program:

f0 (Hz)      6    10.5     20     30     50    120
clipped     88%    71%    44%    28%    17%     8%

It needs f0 ~ 235 Hz for under 5% clipping. Our own gentler designed program needs ~42 Hz. And the search space we had been using is f0 ∈ [6, 36] — while every champion ever crowned landed at the bottom of it: 6.0, 8.6, 10.5.

Damping is the second lever (the velocity term is 2·zeta·vel/w0), and a nearly clip-free corner turns out to exist *inside* the space we were already searching — (f0 15-20, zeta 0.4-0.6) at 2-9% clipped, against 36% in the champion corner.

The dose, female champion (native f0 10.5, zeta held at 1.09 so the joint stays overdamped throughout):

f0        6    10.5     15     20     25     30     36
stand   3/6     2/6    3/6    0/6    1/6    0/6    1/6
minlift 2.0     9.5   14.0     --   22.0     --   32.0
speed  0.30    0.54   0.40     --   0.42     --   1.37
nonfoot 0.000  0.003  0.005  0.008  0.311  0.656  0.557

The worst leg's step count rises monotonically 2 → 9.5 → 14 → 22 → 32, a 16x effect far outside the n=6 noise that makes the standing column unreadable. The male's dose is a trade immediately: standing 3/6 at f0 6 and 0-1/6 everywhere above, nonfoot 0.46 → 0.89. Same parameter, opposite bill, on the two animals.

Because f0 6/10.5/15 gave 3/6, 2/6, 3/6 standing, the entry read f0 15 as a free improvement — the BLIND-SPOT outcome — and launched a title match on it. It met the bar: 12 fresh seeds (880-892), standing 6/12, qualifying 6/6, duty 0.81 PASS where the incumbent conflicts at 0.86, and the first female standing run in project history to pass R1i (1/6, a reflex rule she had gone 0/10 on). A dead tie with the champion on every title criterion.

So a paired decider was registered before it ran — both thetas on the same 12 fresh seeds (2012-2027), challenger must *strictly* exceed, ties keep the crown with the incumbent so the rule cannot be gamed by re-rolling. p150 defends 6-3.

Interpretation. The blind-spot reading was wrong, and it was wrong for exactly the reason its own paragraph had warned about: it rested on 3/6-vs-2/6-vs-3/6, which this project had already measured to be coin flips. With seed luck cancelled at n=12, f0 15 halves standing. The registered dichotomy resolves as TRADE for the female too. What survives is the sharpest speed result she has ever produced: on identical dice, raising f0 alone multiplies standing speed 2.5x (0.36 → 0.91 mm/s) and raises stepping (min lifts 10 → 12). Nothing else in this project's history has moved her speed like that.

And then the literature closed the argument. A 30-agent sweep, every number adversarially checked against its source (20 measured-direct, 3 model-derived, 1 refuted): FTi swing excursion ~42.6 deg (Haustein 2024); swing duration 20-45 ms, mean ~31 ms, and speed-invariant (Wosnitza 2013, DeAngelis 2019 — only stance shortens). The structural point we had missed is that a swing is a half cycle, so a 31 ms swing is kinematically a ~16 Hz sinusoid, not a 5-16 Hz step rate — and because swing duration does not relax with walking speed, *there is no slow-walking regime where a slow joint suffices.* A fly creeping at 3 mm/s still throws its tibia 40 deg in 30 ms. Azevedo 2020's measured 8.5 ms spike-to-half-max-force, read as a critically damped second-order step, puts the plant at f0 = 31.4 Hz; Zumstein 2004 agrees in order.

VERDICT: our body model conflicts with measured Drosophila muscle kinetics, and has since the loop closed. Per the governing aim that is a gift — it deletes the entire f0 < 15 region that every search we have ever run was living in.

Problems / what bit us.

  1. A record with no title is still a failure of the fly, not the bar. 9/12 standing is a genuine existence proof that balance is solvable in this rig. It is also a fly that does not walk.
  2. We spent weeks attributing to the network a limit that belongs to the body. The female's speed conflict (0.3-1.0 mm/s against a 2.0 floor) is the same wall seen from the inside: at f0 8.6-10.5 with zeta 1.09 the body is *physically incapable* of the ~2700-3800 deg/s peak joint velocities real stepping demands.
  3. The escape route is the dangerous corner. The clip-free region is underdamped, and our own tier-0 note says a resonant limb can manufacture a rhythm with no connectome in it. Recorded before any of it was run: any move to zeta < 1 must carry the shuffled-connectome control.
  4. A provenance correction, tier-0. AGENTS.md listed "tau_act = 12.3 ms from Azevedo 2020" among the loop's unfitted *measured* anchors. The string "12.3" appears nowhere in that paper: 12.3 = 8.5/ln 2, their measured half-rise passed through a first-order assumption. Unfitted survives; *independently measured* does not, and it is one datum with the 31.4 Hz figure rather than two. Worse, their 8.5 ms includes conduction and NMJ delay, so real activation is faster — our number biases the body slow, in the same direction as the conflict.

What changed in the model. Nothing in the body itself — MUSCLE.md governs that, and every number above is a measurement rather than a change. What changed is where the search is allowed to look: design- side work stopped (the D7 branch fired as registered), the campaign target became the expressible envelope, and the next chamber was ordered into the forbidden corner with f0 confined to [15, 36] and zeta held at or above 1.0 — toward the measurement, and conservatively so, since 31.4 Hz sits near the top of that window.

Attribution. Robin set the standing rule that titles are decided on the CEO's bar and that bars never move mid-contest, which is what forced the paired-decider protocol to be written down before it ran rather than after 6-vs-3 was known. The agent designed and ran the probe, the two analytic sweeps, the dose and the decider, and wrote the amendment against its own earlier reading rather than editing it away.

Question. The champion crowned yesterday — the phasic fly — had pinned its new sensing dial at the ceiling we allowed. Round 19 raised that ceiling to 3.0 and re-searched from the champion. Does more phasic sensing buy a better fly?

Predicted (pre-registered, quoted). From the round-18 registration: "round 19 raises the phasic ceiling (search (0, 3.0) — the chamber voted for more), seeds from the phasic fly", with a coordination secondary "with teeth: report mean-PLV-excess and tri-index on the winner's standing seeds." The bar was written before the run and left unchanged: a challenger takes the title only if its battery beats the champion on standing (> 3/6) AND speed (> 1.03 mm/s), with all-feet lifts >= 5.

Method (jargon defined inline). The search ("chamber") drew 180 parameter sets and scored each on 3 randomly chosen simulation seeds — a seed is one roll of the dice the noisy network is run under. The top 10 were then re-run ("rerank") on 4 fresh seeds each, and the best of those went to the battery: the fixed constraint checklist, re-measured on 6 seeds no part of the search had ever seen. That last step is the practice the same day's reporting directive names in plain words — never grade the fly on dice rolls it practiced on.

Result (numbers, with variance). The rerank winner was an extreme animal: phasic 2.85, command 156 Hz, campaniform gain 48, joint f0 6.0 Hz, adhesion threshold 0.1. On its 4 rerank seeds it stood 4 of 4 — upright 0.99 / 0.93 / 0.97 / 0.94, displacement 5.15 / 5.50 / 5.69 / 5.32 mm, median 5.41 mm. That is the strongest rerank in the project's history.

Battery, per seed (seed: mm, upright): 830: 6.52, 0.99 | 831: 3.88, 0.16 | 832: 0.65, 0.19 | 833: 4.00, 0.37 | 834: 7.63, 0.73 | 835: 5.58, 0.97. Standing 2/6, speed 1.10 mm/s (1.19 and 1.01 on the two standing seeds). The speed clears the bar; the standing does not; the bar is an AND. R19 FAIL — the phasic fly keeps the title.

What stands from the chamber anyway: it pinned the phasic dial at the raised 3.0 ceiling *again* — at the halfway mark the leader was a candidate passing all 3 of its seeds with all-positive coordination excess (+0.007 / +0.033 / +0.058) at exactly phasic 3.00, and 25 of the 180 candidates ended within 0.01 of the ceiling (only 4 of 180 passed all three seeds at all). And the challenger scored the first contralateral swing-avoidance pass on both standing seeds in recent memory (R1c_tip p = 0.01 and 0.005).

Conflicts carried, stated with the fail: cadence 2.68 Hz against the real 5-16 Hz band; median swing 55 ms against a 60 ms band edge; speed 1.10 mm/s against a real-fly floor of 2.0.

Interpretation. Five of these collapses now exist, and they have the same shape: m050xDNg100, coact, the round-16 winner (battery 1/6, speed 0.19), t025+phasic1.0 (battery 0/6), and this one (2/6). Score 180 candidates on 3 dice rolls each, take the best, and you have selected partly for the parameters and partly for the dice. A 4-seed rerank over the top 10 does not undo that — reranking a shortlist the same dice produced is another selection step, not an evaluation. The enemy is not the fly, not the ceiling, and not the bar: robustness was only ever tested after the winner was chosen.

Problems / what bit us. (1) The rerank looked like the best evidence the project had produced, and it was worth nothing on its own. "Strongest rerank ever" is a statement about a selection stage. (2) Speed genuinely improved — 1.10 against the champion's 1.03 — and there is an obvious reading in which this round half-won. The bar was written as an AND before the run precisely so that reading is unavailable afterwards.

What changed in the model. Nothing in the fly; the change is in how the search is graded. Round 20 is registered and committed before any run: 4 seeds per candidate inside the search, phasic ceiling raised a third time to 5.0 (two consecutive ceiling pins), anchors p150 / p150@ph3.5 / p150@ph4.5, N = 240, same bar against the same champion.

Attribution. Human: the standing rules this verdict is enforced by — fresh-seed evaluation and pre-registration, both named in the reporting-standards directive of the same day; and the governing aim that makes a published failure worth the words, "every measurement is a constraint that might just make our goal vector space narrower" (2026-08-10). Agent (Claude Fable 5, per the commit trailer): the round-19 chamber, rerank and battery; the diagnosis that five scattered collapses share one cause; the round-20 registration that acts on it.

The second fly agrees with the first

We compared our walking circuit's wiring against a second individual fly, connection by connection. The strong wiring we simulate is 87% shared; the weak wiring we discard is a coin flip.

commit see "THE SECOND FLY part 1" committheta none — pure data analysisseeds none — deterministicn 2,918,999 testable connections; 24,206 matched neuronswall ~4 min

Question. Everything we simulate comes from ONE fly's wiring diagram. Are our conclusions about "the fly connectome" — or about this one fly?

Predicted (pre-registered, quoted). "MA1: conservation rises with BANC synapse count, and >=10-synapse edges are substantially more conserved than 1-9. MA2: conservation ~flat -> the cut stands on its behavioural result only." Written before the comparison ran — the day had already produced one retraction about this very threshold's history, so the bar was set blind.

Method. A second complete fly nerve cord exists: MANC, a male, published by Janelia in 2024 (public download, URL recorded this time). The BANC team had already matched 24,206 of our walking-core neurons to their MANC counterparts, cell by cell. For every connection in our core where both endpoints have a match, we asked: do the same two cells connect in the other fly, and how strongly?

Result (numbers). Conservation climbs smoothly with connection strength: 1-synapse connections are shared between the flies 38% of the time; 2 synapses, 54%; 5-9, 78%; 10-19, 85%; 100+, 94%. Our simulated core (10+ synapses): 87.1% shared. The tail we discard: 49.9%. Where a strong connection exists in both animals, its strength agrees too (correlation 0.47 on 200,448 shared connections).

Interpretation. The wiring we simulate is, to first order, the wiring every fly has; the wiring we drop is closer to individual handwriting. The same weak-varies/strong-conserved law was known from a worm study (Witvliet 2021); this is, to our knowledge, its first direct confirmation across two fly nerve cords — and it is a male and a female agreeing, which makes the shared core more striking, not less.

Problems / what bit us. Earlier today the agent claimed the 10-synapse cut was "a noise threshold, not an individuality filter" — the human remembered otherwise, the ledger proved the human right, and the claim was retracted in writing. This experiment then tested what the ledger asserted. Caveats that stand: the matches are morphology-based, not perfect; sex differences are folded in; the other dataset's own detection threshold makes weak-edge conservation a lower bound. The separation survives all three.

What changed in the model. Nothing — and that is the point: the substrate every result stands on just went from assumption to measurement. Part 2 (registered): port the rig to the male cord and see whether the SAME parameters walk.

Attribution. Human: "btw another fly connectome exists... WE should prolly run tests on both LOL" — the entire experiment, in one message; also the memory-correction that motivated testing the threshold's story. Agent: the download, the join, the analysis, and the earlier wrong claim this experiment repaid.

Question. Why does a cord that demonstrably walks keep its legs unphased — and what would let it hear its own legs?

Predicted (pre-registered, quoted). From the TR1 registration: "T1 = closed-loop leg PLV rises above per-arm rolled floors with dose -> transduction depth was the bottleneck." Method (jargon defined inline). A four-probe chain recorded named neuron populations while the fly behaved. It found the leg cycle reaches the cord only as a whisper: our sensors are tonic-dominated — they fire at their absolute level (~76 Hz) with the movement barely modulating them, where real fly proprioceptors are phasic (they fire on CHANGE). We added one default-off parameter: subtract each sensor's own running baseline and amplify the residual. Then a 180-candidate search (chamber) with that dial searchable, judged on stand-and-step displacement, coordination scored only by the validated instrument.

Result (numbers, with variance). Standing 3/6, speed 1.03 mm/s (2x the incumbent), min lifts 9, all six joint ranges in-band. Title transferred.

Interpretation. The stand/walk trade that defined the whole project broke on physiology, not on search cleverness: a cord that hears changes can afford to move. Honest speed is now 1.03 against a real-fly floor of 2.0 — inside 2x for the first time.

(1) An intermediate battery (t025 + phasic, before the search) went 0/6 — the fourth time a small-n result collapsed on fresh seeds; only the paired comparison survived, which is exactly what paired designs promise and no more. (2) The video renderer predates the new parameter and silently ran the champion WITHOUT its phasic sensing — a different animal that fell. 2026-08-17 The night of instruments ★ validated instruments Our tripod ruler failed its own test. Rebuilding it revealed the reference "tripod" was a wave — and the fly's legs keep no phase at all.
2026-08-17finding our feet

The night of instruments

Our tripod ruler failed its own test. Rebuilding it revealed the reference "tripod" was a wave — and the fly's legs keep no phase at all.

★ A first principle is born here: validated instruments — no metric without a manipulation test

Robin asked us to optimize for the tripod gait. The statistic we built to measure tripod-ness failed its manipulation test: fed a known reference gait, it returned the wrong answer. The replacement failed too. The third — step-event phases, validated on constructed gaits where the truth is known by design — passed, and promptly delivered two uncomfortable results.

First: the reference program we had called "the tripod walk" for days is not a tripod. It is a perfectly coherent metachronal wave (phase-locking 0.976) — the gait real SLOW flies use. Every design in our target lineage inherited wave phasing; our chambers had been grading flies against a tripod ideal the teacher never had.

Second: measured properly, the closed-loop fly's legs are genuinely unphased — inter-leg locking sits exactly at the noise floor.

Four instrument flaws were caught and recorded this night, each before its verdict was used. The rule since: no coordination claim except through the validated instrument.

Human: the tripod directive that started the chase. Agent: three broken rulers, one honest one, two discoveries.

t025, and the day the command channel showed its hand

A blend fly took the best card in project history; the same fly walks or stands depending on which command neuron you drive.

Two different searches crossed the same valley independently — one by gradients on a differentiable twin, one by honest-objective search — and their strengths merged in a quarter-blend fly, t025: 11 PASS, all six measured joint ranges inside real-fly bands for the first time, honest speed 0.52 mm/s.

Then the command experiments. Same fly, same parameters: drive descending neuron DNg100 and it walks; drive MDN instead and it stands 6/6 — the first perfect stability score ever. Drive rate trades speed against stability monotonically. The command channel is a program selector and a dial, like in the real animal.

The day also cost us: five challenger flies died at the battery, each one looking excellent on the seeds that found it and collapsing on fresh ones. The discipline of never grading a fly on dice rolls it practiced on (fresh-seed evaluation) went from principle to reflex. The glue, the tick, and two human catches

The fly looked like it walked. Its feet were glued to the floor and its clock was inflating the tempo. Robin caught both.

★ A first principle is born here: honest measures + the parity rule — both from human catches

Two artifacts had been flattering every result for days. The simulation tick was coarse enough to inflate step tempo; and foot adhesion was permanently on, so "walking" flies were dragging themselves with glued feet, and the load signal chattered fake steps.

Both fell to human eyes on videos. Robin: "the latest video barely walks... what is it that is difficult?" — which forced the honest lift measure (a step counts only if the foot's tip actually leaves the ground). And an earlier "it tipped over" catch, when a video contradicted the numbers we'd reported, created the parity rule: every video's displacement and uprightness must match its simulation record to the digit before it ships. That rule caught a renderer bug as recently as today.

With honest measures and releasable feet, the first genuinely stepping, in-band fly appeared — slower and humbler than the glued ones, and real.

Human: both catches. This entry exists because the human watched the videos the agent summarized. Agent: the fixes, and the measures that made flattery harder.

2026-08-14 The battery is born, and the fly-invariant core ★ the battery Every satisfied constraint became a permanent test. Dropping the connections that vary between flies doubled walking.
2026-08-14finding our feet

The battery is born, and the fly-invariant core

Every satisfied constraint became a permanent test. Dropping the connections that vary between flies doubled walking.

★ A first principle is born here: the battery — constraints that re-run forever

The walking battery was born: fixed real-fly bands (step frequency, swing duration, duty factor, contralateral phase, speed, six joint ranges, reflex rules), measured on fresh seeds, never widened to make a conflict disappear. From here on, every fly gets a card and the cards are comparable forever.

Same night, the invariant-core experiment: keep only connections of at least 10 synapses — the ones measured as >90% reproducible between individual flies — and drop the rest. Standing tied (16/30 vs 17/30), but standing WALKS DOUBLED (median 3.92 vs 1.95 mm, p = 0.0003), 2.4x faster to simulate. The individual-variability tail wasn't just noise; it was drag. The core became our standard substrate.

Also certified this day: load prolongs stance (rule R5), our first behavioural rule matched against fly literature.

Human: the standing question — "old truths must be re-measured, not assumed" — that made the battery re-run forever. Agent: battery design, the core experiment.

2026-08-10early chaos

The rhythm that didn't need the body — and the birth of pre-registration

A 14 Hz rhythm appeared; half of what we first believed about it was wrong; the discipline that fixed us was born here.

★ A first principle is born here: pre-registration — a failed test, recorded as failed

We closed the sensorimotor loop and found a 14 Hz rhythm that a shuffled connectome never produces (real 9/24 vs shuffled 0/24). Then we spent a day discovering how much of our first story was wrong: the rhythm needs no body at all (tonic drive alone produces it, on a tuning curve in activity); the "1.2% frequency spread" was the detector's resolution floor; n=6 counts flipped between seed batches.

The load-bearing event: we wrote a prediction down, hashed and committed it BEFORE running — the claim that afferent rate level explains the rhythm, with its own success bar. It got 4 successes where it demanded 5, p = 0.053 against its own criterion of 0.05. A post-hoc reading would have called 4-vs-0 a win. We recorded it as a failure, because that is what it was. Pre-registration has been law since — this entry is where the diary's own honesty machinery is born.

Human: "our aim is zero conflicts with measured data... every measurement narrows the space" — the reframe that made conflicts gifts. Agent: the rhythm hunt, the withdrawn claims, the failed test.

2026-08-09early chaos

The network that was either dead or screaming

One global synapse gain made the network bistable. A per-neuron balance rule opened the regime a brain lives in.

Every setting of the global synaptic gain gave one of two networks: one that dies the instant input stops, or one that latches at ceiling forever like a metronome (spike-time variability 0.06 — a clock, not a brain). At one gain value, 4 of 12 seeds latched and 8 died: both states coexist and noise picks. No fine-tuning could find the middle, because there was no middle.

The fix that worked was homeostatic: each neuron scales its own incoming inhibition to hit a target balance. The middle regime went from 0% of runs to 36%, firing at 7.5 Hz with brain-like irregularity.

A correction is preserved here on purpose: we first wrote that per-class gains were the fix. Measuring before building showed the imbalance lives WITHIN cell classes, not between them — the fix we'd already written down would not have worked. This kind of preserved correction later became diary policy.

Human: patience while the network screamed. Agent: the sweep, the wrong first fix, the measurement that caught it, the homeostatic rule.

2026-08-06 Counting our guesses 48% of the model's numbers are guesses. We measured which guesses the output actually depends on.
2026-08-06early chaos

Counting our guesses

48% of the model's numbers are guesses. We measured which guesses the output actually depends on.

We tiered every scalar in the model by how much we believe it: measured (448), principled (42), arbitrary (460). Then we perturbed the live ones and re-ran the whole 188k-neuron simulation to see which matter.

The winner was embarrassing: the single biggest lever in the model (196x the noise floor) is nt_sign_glutamate — whether glutamate is treated as inhibitory — a convention inherited from a published model, not measured, applied to 25,099 neurons. Meanwhile two pure guesses covering 33,452 neurons turned out to matter less than the difference between two random seeds.

The lesson that stuck: tier alone tells you nothing — a wild guess the answer ignores is harmless; a "principled" value the answer hinges on is a research program.

Human: the demand that everything be justified or labelled a guess. Agent: the ledger and the sensitivity runs.

2026-08-05early chaos

Day one — the bet

Goal set, connectome downloaded, behavioural scorer built. Almost nothing else exists yet.

Robin set the frame in one message: a fully closed-loop fly, grounded in real measurement, judged on behaviour — "behavioural data is king compared to functional data in the brain. this is a lofi upload not a full WBE."

We downloaded BANC (188,508 neurons, 13.6 million synapses, one female fly) and built the scorer: 7 gait metrics validated on ~3,000 real flies. The rule that the scorer is a frozen instrument — any bad score is the model's fault, never the metric's — existed from this first day. Almost nothing else did. There was no battery, no pre-registration, no parity rule. Those all had to be earned the hard way, and this diary shows when and how.

Human: the entire framing. Agent: the downloads and the scorer.
